Description: Bardney Limewoods NNR is a complex of ancient woodlands between Lincoln and Horncastle in Lincolnshire. It preserves the largest remaining small-leaved lime woods in Britain, rich in biodiversity. The reserve offers habitats for various flora and fauna, including rare invertebrates.

Name: Bareland Street
Description: Bareland Street nature reserve in Torfaen features two flower-rich meadows, hosting species like yellow rattle, ragged robin, and northern marsh orchid. Traditional methods manage these habitats for wildlife.

Name: Barford Wood and Meadows
Description: Barford Wood and Meadows is a diverse nature reserve in Northamptonshire, featuring ancient woodland, wildflower meadows, and a lake. It supports various wildlife, including butterflies, birds, and badgers. Managed for biodiversity and visitor enjoyment.

Name: Barkbooth Lot
Description: Barkbooth Lot is an upland pasture within the Lake District National Park, part of a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). It features species-rich grassland and a stream, providing habitats for rare butterflies and birds. Grazing by cattle maintains its ecological value.

Name: Barkway Chalk Pit
Description: Barkway Chalk Pit is a small former chalk quarry and nature reserve in North Hertfordshire, managed by North Hertfordshire District Council. It is a Regionally Important Geological Site (RIGS) due to its chalk exposure, displaced by the Anglian ice sheet. The site features chalk grassland and scrub, supporting wildflowers like bee orchid and common spotted orchid, and butterflies such as the grizzled skipper and brown argus.

Name: Barlow Common
Description: Barlow Common Nature Reserve, near Selby, transformed from a railway goods yard and ash tip. It now features diverse habitats including wetlands, ponds, and woodland. The site supports a variety of birds, amphibians, and insects. Ponds host newts and dragonflies, whilst the woodland edge provides shelter.

Name: Barn Elms Wetland Centre SSSI
Description: Barn Elms Wetland Centre SSSI, located in London, is a nationally important site for wildlife. It encompasses a variety of wetland habitats and supports diverse bird species and other wildlife in an urban environment. It is managed to conserve its ecological value.

Name: Barnes Meadow
Description: Barnes Meadow is a riverside wildflower meadow by the Great Ouse, managed to protect water voles and diverse plant species. The site features a rich array of flora and supports various invertebrates, with a public footpath offering access.

Name: Barnsley Canal
Description: Barnsley Canal Nature Reserve at Wilthorpe, managed by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust, protects a section of the historic canal. It serves as a gateway into the Upper Dearne Valley, featuring extensive wetland habitats including reedbed, marsh, scrub, and woodland. The reserve supports diverse wildlife such as water voles, kingfishers, dragonflies, damselflies, and great crested newts.

Name: Barnsley Main Nature Reserve
Description: Barnsley Main Nature Reserve, managed by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust, is a green landscape with an industrial past, located on the edge of urban Barnsley. It features a diverse mosaic of habitats, including wildflower meadows, ponds, and woodland, providing homes for various insects and birds.

Name: Barnwell Meadows
Description: Barnwell Meadows is a traditional hay meadow in the heart of Cambridge, managed by Cambridge Past, Present & Future. It supports diverse wildflowers, grasses, and insects, offering a glimpse into the area's agricultural past. Visitors enjoy peaceful walks and observe wildlife.

Name: Baron's Haugh
Description: Baron's Haugh is an RSPB reserve in Motherwell, North Lanarkshire, Scotland. It features a diverse wetland habitat alongside the River Clyde, attracting numerous waterfowl, waders, and other bird species throughout the year. Visitors can enjoy several trails and hides.

Name: Barossa
Description: Barossa is a 498-hectare lowland heathland nature reserve north of Camberley in Surrey, owned by the Ministry of Defence and managed by Surrey Wildlife Trust. The site, an MOD Dry Training Area, features open dry heath scattered with mixed woodland, acid grassland, and mire. It is a key habitat for diverse heathland wildlife, including rare species like sand lizards, adders, grass snakes, slow worms, common lizards, nightjars, woodlarks, and Dartford warblers. Public access is permitted only in the Dry Training Area via permissive footpaths, respecting military byelaws.

Name: Barrington Hill Meadow
Description: Barrington Court estate in Somerset features diverse landscapes, including extensive meadows that support a range of local wildlife. These grasslands are managed to enhance biodiversity, providing habitats for insects and ground-nesting birds within the historic grounds.

Name: Barrow Haven Reedbed
Description: Barrow Haven Reedbed is a vital brackish reedbed habitat in the UK, important for birds such as reed warblers, sedge warblers, and bearded tits. It is also home to various insects and otters. Observation screens and bird hides provide excellent birdwatching opportunities near the river. Managed by the Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust, it is one of the most important disused flooded clay pits on the Humber Bank.

Name: Barrow Wake
Description: Barrow Wake is a nature reserve on the Cotswold scarp, offering panoramic views across the Severn Vale. The site features flower-rich limestone grassland, scrub, and woodland habitats. It is managed to conserve its rich butterfly, moth, and plant populations, supporting significant biodiversity.

Name: Bartinney
Description: Bartinney Nature Reserve in West Cornwall forms part of the Penwith Moors SSSI and West Penwith ESA. Managed by Cornwall Wildlife Trust, the site protects rare plants and birds, restoring heathland and traditional farming practices.

Name: Barton Broad
Description: Barton Broad, the second largest Norfolk Broad, is a crucial wildlife site managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust. Visitors can explore the 163-hectare reserve, including fen and woodlands, via accessible boardwalks. The site features rich biodiversity, supporting various species. Conservation efforts are ongoing.

Name: Barton Broad and Marshes
Description: Barton Broad, the second-largest Norfolk Broad, is part of the Broads National Park. It features extensive reedbed and carr woodland habitats, supporting rare plants, insects, and otter. A wheelchair-accessible boardwalk allows visitors to explore the unique wetland environment.

Name: Barton Gravel Pit
Description: Barton Gravel Pit, a restored former gravel pit in Bedfordshire, features open water, reedbeds, grassland, and woodland. The site supports diverse wildlife, including wading birds, dragonflies, and rare plants. It is actively managed for conservation.

Name: Barton Meadows
Description: Barton Meadows is a 38-hectare nature reserve north of Winchester. Opened in 2018, it features newly planted woodland, restored chalk grassland, and a wetland scrape. This former arable site supports species like brown hairstreak butterflies and barn owls, offering accessible wildlife habitats.

Name: Barton Pool
Description: Barton Pool is a small wetland reserve adjacent to Attenborough Nature Reserve in Nottinghamshire. The site comprises reedbeds, open water, and scrub, supporting diverse birdlife including warblers and ducks. It offers a tranquil habitat managed for biodiversity.

Name: Barton's Bank
Description: Barton's Bank is a small ancient oak woodland nature reserve on the edge of the Wyre Forest, near Cleobury Mortimer. Historically part of the Kinlet Estate, it hosts a wide variety of woodland flowers and provides habitat for birds, bats, and invertebrates. Shropshire Wildlife Trust manages the site for biodiversity.

Name: Bartonsham Meadows
Description: Bartonsham Meadows is a 23.9-hectare nature reserve outside Hereford city centre. Located on the River Wye's southern bank, it comprises flood meadows managed for nature recovery and flood management. The site offers walking routes and river access.

Name: Bassenthwaite Lake NNR
Description: Bassenthwaite Lake NNR is a shallow lake in the Lake District National Park, Cumbria. It hosts diverse habitats like reedbeds, woodlands, and open water, supporting a variety of wildlife including rare fish and otters.

Name: Basted Mill
Description: Basted Mill Public Open Space is located near Borough Green, Kent. It features diverse habitats including an old mill pond, meadows, and woodland, providing a haven for wildlife. Public access paths are available.

Name: Baston Fen
Description: Baston Fen is a 33-hectare nature reserve in Lincolnshire, featuring fen, wet woodland, and unimproved grassland habitats. It supports diverse insect populations and breeding birds. A boardwalk and trails provide visitor access.

Name: Bath Skyline
Description: The Bath Skyline, a six-mile National Trust route, overlooks Bath. It features ancient woodlands, Iron Age hill forts, hidden valleys, and wildflower meadows, supporting diverse wildlife habitats.

Name: Bathampton Meadow
Description: Bathampton Meadow is a tranquil floodplain meadow and ox-bow lake by the River Avon, near Bath, managed by Avon Wildlife Trust. Created in 1996 for flood relief, it hosts diverse wildflowers, various invertebrates, and a rich array of migrant and water birds, including waders, sand martins, and kingfishers. Traditional hay cutting and grazing are used for biodiversity.

Name: Bathampton Meadows
Description: Bathampton Meadows is a riverside flood plain near Bath, offering tranquil green space and city skyline views. Popular for walking and cycling, the meadows support diverse wildlife, including birds and wildflowers, and are managed for conservation.

Name: Bawdeswell Heath
Description: Bawdeswell Heath, near Dereham, Norfolk, is a medieval heathland fragment. It features wet and dry heath, acid grassland, and woodland. Diverse flora and fauna thrive, including common lizards and adders. Site management maintains its character.

Name: Bawsinch and Duddingston
Description: Bawsinch and Duddingston Loch is a Scottish Wildlife Trust reserve in Edinburgh. The site features a freshwater loch and surrounding wetlands, attracting various waterfowl and bird species. Habitats include reedbeds, scrub, and woodland. The reserve offers walking trails and bird hides.

Name: Bay Meadows
Description: Bay Meadows is a Wiltshire Wildlife Trust nature reserve near Marlborough. This site features wet grassland and ancient hedgerows, supporting diverse wetland flora and fauna, including water voles. A circular walking route is accessible for visitors.

Name: Bay Pond
Description: Bay Pond is a significant wetland habitat in Surrey, featuring a large pond, fen, and wet grassland. It supports diverse wildlife, including waterfowl, dragonflies, and water voles. A public footpath encircles the reserve.

Name: Beacon Hill
Description: Beacon Hill is a small nature reserve in north Kent, situated on the edge of the urban area of Vigo. It features chalk grassland with orchids and a variety of invertebrates.

Name: Beacon Hill
Description: Beacon Hill is a peaceful woodland and recovering heathland site in Monmouthshire, Wales, located within the Wye Valley National Landscape. Managed by Natural Resources Wales, it offers stunning views and public footpaths, protecting diverse habitats and supporting varied wildlife, including Nightjars. Gwent Wildlife Trust is actively involved in conservation efforts and events at the site.

Name: Beacon Hill Conservation Park
Description: Beacon Hill Conservation Park is an extensive network of habitats, including scrub, woodland, hedgerows, and grassland. The large central area, formerly a landfill site, has been restored as a wildflower meadow, with a wood gully at the southern edge. It provides habitat for diverse wildlife, including various bird species and notable moths. The park offers public access for quiet recreation and nature observation.

Name: Beacon Hill Country Park
Description: Beacon Hill Country Park in Leicestershire features ancient 600-million-year-old rocks and panoramic views across Charnwood Forest. The park contains mature woodlands, heathland, wildflower meadows, walking trails, and reconstructed Bronze Age log houses.

Name: Beaconwood and the Winsel
Description: Beaconwood and The Winsel spans 11 hectares, featuring a mix of mature and regenerating broadleaf trees. The site provides various walking trails and supports diverse wildlife habitats. It includes remnants of ancient woodland and offers a natural environment, renowned for stunning bluebell displays each spring.

Name: Beales Meadows
Description: Beales Meadows is a Cornwall Wildlife Trust nature reserve, featuring traditional hay meadows, ancient woodland, and borders the River Lynher. The site supports diverse wildflowers, dormice, and otters. Grazing helps maintain its rich biodiversity for conservation.

Name: Beam Parklands
Description: Beam Parklands is a multi-award-winning 53-hectare wetland park in the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham, managed by The Land Trust. Created as part of the Thames Gateway regeneration, it serves as a crucial flood defense and provides diverse habitats including open water, reedbeds, wet woodland, and grasslands for wildlife. The River Beam flows through the site, offering a valuable green space for local communities.

Name: Beane Marsh
Description: Beane Marsh is a tranquil five-acre nature reserve in Hertford, located on the River Beane floodplain. This peaceful floodplain grassland, a designated Local Wildlife Site, comprises wet pasture, willow scrub, and ditches. It provides habitat for wetland birds and diverse invertebrates like dragonflies and damselflies, and is known to support rare species such as Water Vole. The reserve is managed by the Hertfordshire and Middlesex Wildlife Trust, with careful management including seasonal cattle grazing. While there is no public access to the reserve itself, Beane Road offers excellent views over the site.

Name: Beck Bottom
Description: Beck Bottom is an ancient semi-natural woodland near Guisborough, featuring mature oak, ash, and birch trees. A dense undergrowth of hazel and hawthorn supports wildflowers like bluebell and wild garlic. Beck Bottom Beck, a small stream, flows through the reserve, hosting aquatic invertebrates.

Name: Beckenham Place Park
Description: Beckenham Place Park in South London hosts the River Ravensbourne, a site of significant river restoration work. Thames21, in partnership with local groups, improves habitats and naturalises the river course, with ongoing volunteer tasks contributing to its ecological recovery.

Name: Beddington Farmlands
Description: Beddington Farmlands, a nature reserve in south London, is built on a former landfill site. Managed for biodiversity since the 1980s, it provides a crucial habitat for various wildlife, particularly birds. It serves as a significant area for ecological restoration.

Name: Bedford Purlieus National Nature Reserve
Description: Bedford Purlieus is a 211-hectare ancient woodland in Cambridgeshire, UK, and one of the largest ancient woodlands in lowland England. It is a National Nature Reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest, renowned for its exceptional diversity of trees, plants (including over 460 vascular plant species), and invertebrates. It is also home to over 40 species of breeding birds, including the Lesser Spotted Woodpecker. The site is managed by Forestry England for conservation and research.

Name: Bedfords Park
Description: Bedfords Park, a 215-acre deer park and Local Nature Reserve near Romford, is owned by the London Borough of Havering and managed jointly with Essex Wildlife Trust, who run the visitor centre. It features woodlands, grasslands, and ponds, supporting diverse wildlife. The park offers walking trails, a visitor centre, and panoramic views across London.

Name: Bedfords Park
Description: Bedfords Park is a nature reserve located in Havering, offering panoramic views across London. It features woodlands, ponds, and meadows, supporting a variety of wildlife including red deer. The site has a visitor centre and promotes environmental education.

Name: Bedgebury National Pinetum and Forest
Description: Home to a world-leading collection of conifers, the National Pinetum is a centre for research and conservation. The wider forest offers walking, cycling, and family activities, supporting biodiversity and public engagement.

Name: Bedgebury National Pinetum and Forest
Description: Bedgebury National Pinetum and Forest, located in the High Weald AONB, is a world-leading collection of conifers and a significant center for conifer conservation and research. Managed primarily by Forestry England, it offers diverse wildlife habitats, extensive trails for recreation, and serves as a living laboratory for conservation efforts.

Name: Bedgebury Pinetum
Description: Bedgebury National Pinetum and Forest, located in Kent, is a renowned arboretum housing a world-leading collection of conifers and other trees. It offers extensive walking and cycling trails, alongside a popular adventure play area.

Name: Beechenhurst - Forest of Dean
Description: Beechenhurst Lodge is a popular visitor centre within the Forest of Dean, Gloucestershire. It offers a café, adventure play, sculpture trail, and easy access walks. Visitors can find information and explore Go Ape Tree Top Adventure.

Name: Beechwoods
Description: Beechwoods is a small ancient woodland south of Cambridge, noted for its fine mature beech trees. The reserve is home to varied fungi species and supports birds such as tawny owl and nuthatch. Spring sees wildflowers like bluebells and wood anemones.

Name: Begwary Brook
Description: Begwary Brook Nature Reserve is an attractive marsh and open pools located next to the meandering River Great Ouse. The area, once a large marsh, was transformed in the 1960s by gravel extraction, creating a small lake and a series of smaller pools and marshland. It is managed by the Wildlife Trust for Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Northamptonshire and provides habitat for various wildlife, including willow trees, great burnet, common fleabane, marsh woundwort, warblers, foxes, dragonflies, and damselflies.

Name: Beinn Eighe and Loch Maree Islands National Nature Reserve
Description: Beinn Eighe and Loch Maree Islands National Nature Reserve, established in 1951, is the UK's first National Nature Reserve. Located in Wester Ross, Scotland, it encompasses a vast area from loch-side to mountain top, including the Beinn Eighe ridge and over 60 islands in Loch Maree. It is famed for its ancient Caledonian pine forests, diverse upland habitats, and a wealth of Scottish wildlife such as golden eagles, pine martens, and black-throated divers.

Name: Beinn Eighe NNR
Description: Beinn Eighe and Loch Maree Islands National Nature Reserve, established 1951 in Wester Ross, Scottish Highlands, is the UK's first National Nature Reserve. This approximately 4,800-hectare site features ancient Caledonian pinewood, mountain habitats and diverse wildlife.

Name: Belhus Chase
Description: Belhus Chase is a 55.44-hectare (136.99 acres) site near Aveley in Essex, within the Thames Chase Community Forest. This new woodland, acquired by the Woodland Trust in 1998, features a mix of mature native broadleaves and younger plantings, creating a parkland atmosphere. It offers walking routes through diverse habitats, providing a green space for wildlife and visitors, and is connected to the historic Belhus Estate.

Name: Bellever Moor and Meadows
Description: Bellever Moor and Meadows is a Dartmoor nature reserve, managed for its diverse habitats including mire, wet heath, and riverine woodland. It supports significant wildlife such as otters, dormice, and marsh fritillary butterflies.

Name: Bellfield's Pasture
Description: Bellfield's Pasture is a small nature reserve managed by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust, located near Ingleborough in North Yorkshire. It forms an important wild link between neighbouring Ashes Pasture and the wider Ingleborough National Nature Reserve. This pasture is being restored after years of sheep grazing, attracting diverse wildflowers, insects, and butterflies. It is part of the Wild Ingleborough project.

Name: Belmaduthy Dam
Description: Belmaduthy Dam is an artificial loch on the Black Isle, north of Inverness. The reserve protects woodlands along its south bank, featuring birch and pine, attracting diverse waterfowl and wading birds. It is managed by the Scottish Wildlife Trust.

Name: Belsize Wood
Description: Belsize Wood is a 0.7 hectare Local Nature Reserve in Belsize Park, London Borough of Camden. It is managed by Camden Council, with active involvement from Camden Green Gym volunteers who undertake woodland management, coppicing, path clearance, and litter picking. The site offers a peaceful retreat and habitat for wildlife in London.

Name: Beltingham River Gravels
Description: Beltingham River Gravels is a nature reserve along the River South Tyne, near Bardon Mill and Beltingham. It is notable for its calaminarian grassland, a rare habitat influenced by historical heavy metal pollution, supporting unique metallophyte species such as alpine penny-cress, spring sandwort, and mountain pansy. The reserve also features open shingle and gravel banks, providing habitat for species like little ringed plover, and includes riverside woodland supporting various butterflies and dragonflies.

Name: Belton Estate
Description: Belton Estate, a National Trust property in Lincolnshire, features a Grade I listed country house surrounded by a 1,300-acre deer park. The estate includes formal gardens, ancient woodland, and parkland. Visitors can explore varied landscapes and observe wildlife.

Name: Belvide Reservoir
Description: Belvide Reservoir is a Site of Special Scientific Interest in South Staffordshire. Managed as a private bird reserve, it focuses on wildlife conservation and bird observation. The site hosts a bird ringing station, recording over 200 species annually. Access requires a permit.

Name: Bemersyde Moss
Description: Bemersyde Moss is a rare lowland raised bog and Site of Special Scientific Interest in the Scottish Borders. It features peatland, acid grassland, and woodland, supporting sphagnum mosses, heather, diverse invertebrates and birds. Managed for biodiversity.

Name: Ben Lawers NNR
Description: Ben Lawers National Nature Reserve in Perthshire, a site of international importance for arctic-alpine flora. Seven Munros offer challenging walks with dramatic views. The reserve is managed for nature conservation and protects a unique plant community.

Name: Ben Lomond
Description: Ben Lomond is Scotland's most southerly Munro, offering stunning views across Loch Lomond & The Trossachs National Park. The National Trust for Scotland manages conservation efforts, focusing on path maintenance, erosion control, and supporting native wildlife.

Name: Beningbrough
Description: Beningbrough Hall is a Georgian mansion near York, managed by the National Trust. It features extensive gardens, including a walled garden and a dedicated Wilderness Project area for nature exploration and play. The hall houses artworks from the National Portrait Gallery.

Name: Benmore Botanic Garden
Description: Benmore, within Argyll Forest Park, features an impressive avenue of towering Californian giant redwoods. This botanical garden near Dunoon showcases a wide variety of trees and shrubs, including a unique Chilean rainforest glade, offering diverse plant collections.

Name: Bennett's Patch and White's Paddock
Description: Bennett's Patch and White's Paddock is a nature reserve in the Avon Gorge, Bristol. Created from a former sports facility, it features wildflower meadows, native woodland, and wildlife ponds, providing habitats for various butterflies, bees, birds, bats, and badgers. Managed by Avon Wildlife Trust, it offers walking trails and is known for its wicker whale sculptures.

Name: Benscliffe Wood
Description: Benscliffe Wood is a 9.8-hectare ancient woodland and biological Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Leicestershire. It features mature oak, ash, and birch trees with a rich understorey of wildflowers, ferns, and diverse plant communities. The wood is particularly notable for having one of the richest varieties of lichens in the East Midlands, with over thirty species, eleven of which are rare in the county, growing on Precambrian rocks. This important habitat supports a variety of birds and mammals, preserving a key part of the region's natural heritage. Please note that Benscliffe Wood is private land with no public access.

Name: Bentinck Banks
Description: Bentinck Banks is a 13-hectare former colliery spoil tip near Kirkby-in-Ashfield, Nottinghamshire. It features diverse habitats including grassland, scrub, and woodland, supporting butterflies and common lizards. Public access is available.

Name: Bentley Community Woodland
Description: Bentley Community Woodland is a former colliery site in Doncaster, transformed into a green space with native trees, shrubs, ponds, and wildflower meadows. It enhances local biodiversity and is managed with community volunteer involvement.

Name: Bernwood Forest
Description: Bernwood Forest, a former royal hunting ground, consists of various woodlands across Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire. It provides diverse habitats for rare butterflies and wildlife. Visitors can enjoy walking, cycling, and horse riding on established trails, with public access maintained for recreation.

Name: Bernwood Meadows
Description: Bernwood Meadows is a traditionally managed hay meadow, rich in wildflowers, with diverse grasses and herbs. The site, situated in the Bernwood Forest, supports various insect life, including butterflies like the brown argus. A small stream flows through the meadow.

Name: Berry Head
Description: Berry Head is an iconic headland and National Nature Reserve, home to the UK's most southerly guillemot colony. Features include a Napoleonic fort and spectacular views across Torbay. It offers opportunities for wildlife spotting.

Name: Berry Head National Nature Reserve
Description: Berry Head is a limestone headland and National Nature Reserve on the South West Coast Path, offering extensive views across Torbay. This Site of Special Scientific Interest features Napoleonic War fortifications and supports significant seabird colonies, including guillemots and kittiwakes.

Name: Besthorpe
Description: Besthorpe Nature Reserve, near Newark, features diverse habitats including sand and gravel workings, ponds, woodland, and grasslands. It is home to various bird species, invertebrates, and flora. Mons Pool is a prominent feature.

Name: Betchworth Quarry
Description: Betchworth Quarry is a stunning chalk downland nature reserve in Surrey, set within the Surrey Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty and part of the North Downs. This former chalk quarry features exposed chalk cliffs, lime kilns, and diverse habitats including chalk grassland, yew, and broad-leaved woodland. The site is rich in wildflowers such as rare orchids and horseshoe vetch, supporting varied fauna including chalkhill blue butterflies and several bat species.

Name: Bevercotes Wood
Description: Bevercotes Wood is a Sherwood Community Woodland near Newark, transforming former arable land into a diverse habitat. It offers surfaced paths for walking, cycling, and horse riding, alongside quiet areas for reflection, providing space for people and wildlife.

Name: Bevere Fish Pass
Description: Bevere Fish Pass is a significant fish pass near Worcester on the River Severn. It allows migratory fish, such as shad and salmon, to bypass Bevere Weir and access upstream spawning grounds. The pass is a key part of the Unlocking the Severn project.

Name: Bicester Wetland Reserve
Description: Bicester Wetland Reserve, a former Thames Water sewage sludge disposal site, offers a mosaic of habitats including ponds, scrapes, and reedbed. It supports diverse wildlife, notably wading birds like lapwing and curlew, and various invertebrates. The reserve aims to increase biodiversity within its varied landscapes.

Name: Bickham Wood
Description: Bickham Wood is a very wet, semi-natural ancient woodland on the edge of the Blackdown Hills AONB, managed for conservation by Somerset Wildlife Trust. It supports diverse tree species and a rich ground flora, including a wonderful display of woodland flowers in spring. The reserve is also notable for its ferns, sedges, horsetails, and diverse insect and fungi life.

Name: Biddulph Grange Garden
Description: Biddulph Grange Garden in Staffordshire features a Victorian stumpery, a unique garden design utilising upturned tree roots and stumps for dramatic effect. The site also includes various themed gardens, reflecting global horticultural styles from the 19th century.

Name: Big Pool Wood
Description: Big Pool Wood is a small wetland reserve in North Wales, featuring a reedbed and fen. It supports rare plants, invertebrates, and water birds. A boardwalk offers views across the reedbed, while a circular path goes through ancient woodland. Summer brings butterflies and dragonflies.

Name: Big Waters
Description: Big Waters is a Northumberland Wildlife Trust nature reserve north of Newcastle upon Tyne. It features a large lake, woodlands, and reedbeds, supporting diverse birdlife including overwintering wildfowl and migrating waders. This urban wetland stronghold offers peaceful wildlife watching opportunities.

Name: Bigbury-on-Sea & Burgh Island Coast
Description: Bigbury-on-Sea, a coastal village in South Devon, offers sandy beaches, rock pools, and views of Burgh Island. The island is accessible via a tidal causeway or sea tractor, featuring an Art Deco hotel. The area is popular for watersports, walks, and wildlife observation.

Name: Birch Moss Covert
Description: Birch Moss Covert Nature Reserve is a woodland reserve located on Carrington Moss, Broadheath, Greater Manchester. Managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust, it lies on a remnant of peaty soil from the once extensive Carrington Moss. The woodland is dominated by birch, with rowan and young oak, and features glades and rides to support species like the speckled wood butterfly. It is also known for woodland birds such as long-tailed tits and various fungi. Restoration efforts are ongoing to enhance its mossland habitats, including creating suitable conditions for water voles and willow tits.

Name: Birch Wood
Description: Birch Wood is a beautiful and secluded semi-ancient woodland nature reserve in the western North York Moors, managed by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust. It features a mix of oak, birch, and sycamore, with an understorey of rowan, hazel, hawthorn, and elder. The reserve provides habitat for various birds, including redstarts, pied flycatchers, blackcaps, and chiffchaffs, as well as roe and fallow deer. In spring, the woodland floor is adorned with a stunning display of bluebells. Visitors can explore paths through the woods, enjoying spectacular views towards the Hambleton Hills.

Name: Birches Farm
Description: Birches Farm is a 24-hectare Herefordshire reserve featuring unimproved grasslands and traditional orchards. It supports diverse wildflowers and insects, including the brown hairstreak butterfly, alongside ancient hedgerows and veteran trees.

Name: Birdbrook Road Nature Reserve
Description: Birdbrook Road Nature Reserve is a small urban woodland, grassland, and pond system in Kidbrooke, within the London Borough of Greenwich. It features a mosaic of habitats, including mature trees, scrub, open grassy areas, and several ponds, making it an important stronghold for amphibians, particularly newts, and supporting various local wildlife species.

Name: Birkrigg Common
Description: Birkrigg Common, a limestone grassland, provides panoramic views of Morecambe Bay and the Furness Peninsula. A Site of Special Scientific Interest, it hosts diverse flora, fauna, and ancient cairns. Managed for conservation and public access.

Name: Birling Gap and the Seven Sisters
Description: Birling Gap and the Seven Sisters form a dramatic coastal landscape of chalk cliffs and shingle beach. Rapid erosion reveals new fossils. The area provides habitat for diverse wildlife and offers popular cliff-top walks.

Name: Bishop Middleham Quarry
Description: Bishop Middleham Quarry, a Durham Wildlife Trust reserve, features limestone grassland and ancient woodland. It supports wildflowers and butterflies such as dark-red helleborine and dingy skipper, and is a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI).

Name: Bishop Monkton Railway Cutting
Description: Bishop Monkton Railway Cutting Nature Reserve is a disused railway cutting near Ripon, North Yorkshire. The site features species-rich grassland, ancient woodland, and marshy areas, supporting diverse wildlife including orchids, butterflies, and amphibians.

Name: Bishop Wood
Description: Bishop Wood, a diverse woodland in North Yorkshire, features mature oak, birch, and hazel trees, alongside conifers. It supports roe deer, woodpeckers, and various butterfly species. This ancient site provides important habitats for fungi and invertebrates.

Name: Bishop Wood
Description: Bishop Wood is a large ancient woodland in North Yorkshire, featuring diverse broadleaf and conifer tree species and significant wildlife habitats. It offers walking trails and is known for its rich ground flora. Historically managed for timber, the site provides a tranquil environment for visitors.

Name: Bishop's Wood
Description: Bishop's Wood is a 33.7-hectare ancient woodland near Selby, North Yorkshire. The site features a diverse mix of tree species and supports rich wildlife, including ground flora. It offers walking trails and is part of a wider landscape.

Name: Bishopswood Meadows
Description: Bishopswood Meadows, located near Taunton in Somerset and within the Blackdown Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, is a species-rich nature reserve managed by Somerset Wildlife Trust. The reserve features five fields of limestone and marshy meadows on a gentle north-facing slope, with the River Yarty flowing at its base. Its diverse habitats, including calcareous and neutral soils, rush pasture, and thick hedgerows, are partly a legacy of 19th-century lime quarrying. The site supports a wide array of wildflowers like cowslips, dwarf thistle, quaking grass, and various orchids, alongside insects such as common blue, ringlet, and marbled white butterflies. Wildlife includes otters, kingfishers, dippers, golden-ringed dragonflies, and hazel dormice. Public access is available, with parking advised in Bishopswood village.

Name: Bisley & West End Commons and Reidon Hill
Description: Bisley & West End Commons and Reidon Hill forms part of the Thames Basin Heaths Special Protection Area. This important heathland site hosts all three native reptile species and diverse insects. Habitats include dry and wet heathland, acid grassland, and woodland.

Name: Bissoe Valley
Description: Bissoe Valley Nature Reserve is situated within the Cornish Mining World Heritage Site. It encompasses diverse habitats including wetlands, heathland, and acid grassland along the Bissoe River valley, supporting various flora and fauna.

Name: Black Bourn Valley
Description: Black Bourn Valley is a mosaic of habitats, including wildflower meadows, wet woodlands and riverine fen. The reserve is located along the Black Bourn river. It supports a variety of wildlife, from otters to dragonflies.

Name: Black Devon Wetlands
Description: Black Devon Wetlands is a key wildlife reserve near the Firth of Forth in Scotland. It features a mosaic of wetland habitats, including reedbeds, lagoons, and wet grassland. It provides a vital stopping point for migrating birds and supports many resident species. Visitors can observe diverse birdlife from hides.

Name: Black Lake
Description: Black Lake, near Delamere Forest, Cheshire, is a nature reserve with a rare floating bog habitat. This glacial relict supports diverse invertebrates, like dragonflies, and carnivorous plants. It holds Site of Special Scientific Interest status.

Name: Black Moss Covert
Description: Black Moss Covert is a 2.1-hectare nature reserve managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust, located on Carrington Moss, near Altrincham. This small, flat birch-dominated woodland features a circular path and is known for its diverse ground flora, including bramble species, remote sedge, bluebell, wood avens, and dog rose. It is also a good site for fungi, butterflies like speckled wood and peacock, and common woodland birds such as long-tailed tit, jay, wren, and treecreeper. A public footpath runs past the entrance.

Name: Black Mountain Quarry Biodiversity Transition
Description: The Black Mountain Quarry Biodiversity Transition project enhances biodiversity through habitat management, grassland restoration, scrub control, tree planting, and pond creation. This former quarry within the Belfast Hills offers a mosaic of habitats for various wildlife species.

Name: Black Rocks
Description: Black Rocks is a prominent gritstone outcrop near Cromford, Derbyshire. It offers panoramic views over the Derwent Valley. Adjacent woodlands provide walking, cycling, and horse riding trails. The site is popular for rock climbing.

Name: Blackadon
Description: Blackadon is a nature reserve in the South Hams, Devon. Its ancient woodland, damp meadows, and river valley support diverse wildlife. Features include oak woodland, the River Avon, and habitats for rare butterflies and numerous bird species.

Name: Blackburn Flow
Description: Blackburn Flow is a significant peatland restoration project, likely referring to work at Butterburn Flow, a key site within the Border Mires on the Cumbria/Northumberland border. As part of the Great North Bog initiative, it aims to rewet 450 hectares of peatland to reduce carbon emissions and enhance wildlife habitats.

Name: Blackcap
Description: Blackcap offers spectacular views over the South Downs National Park and chalk grasslands near Lewes. This site features ancient trees and diverse flora and fauna, characteristic of a chalk downland environment.

Name: Blackhall Rocks
Description: Blackhall Rocks is a coastal nature reserve in County Durham, known for its limestone cliffs, intertidal rock pools, and unique magnesian limestone grassland. It supports diverse wildlife, including seabirds, wildflowers, and rare invertebrates, and offers panoramic views of the North Sea coastline.

Name: Blackleach Country Park
Description: Blackleach Country Park is a Green Flag park in Salford, Greater Manchester. It features a large reservoir, woodland, and grassland, providing habitat for diverse wildlife including waterfowl and woodland birds. Visitors enjoy walking, fishing, and birdwatching.

Name: Blackmoor Copse
Description: Blackmoor Copse is an ancient woodland in Wiltshire, managed by Wiltshire Wildlife Trust since 1963 as their first nature reserve. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and covers approximately 90 acres (36 hectares). The woodland features oak, ash, hazel, and field maple, supporting diverse wildlife including dormice, badgers, and a variety of butterflies. Spring brings vibrant bluebells and other wildflowers.

Name: Blackness Banks
Description: Blackness Banks is a Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust nature reserve, purchased in 2021, comprising three fields of unimproved limestone grassland. It is known for its species-rich flora, with over 65 species of flowering plants, and provides habitat for at least 30 different butterfly species, including threatened small and large blue butterflies, and autumn lady's-tresses. The reserve also supports noctule bats and acts as a vital wildlife corridor linking habitats in the Golden Valley to Rodborough and Minchinhampton Commons. Its steep banks have protected it from intensive agriculture, preserving its biodiversity and offering views across the Golden Valley.

Name: Blackpool Sands & Strete Gate Coast
Description: This stretch of the South Devon coast features Strete Gate and Blackpool Sands, a shingle beach. The area, part of Start Bay, is known for its diverse geology, coastal habitats, and scenic views. The National Trust cares for segments of the coastline, providing access for visitors.

Name: Blagrove Common
Description: Blagrove Common is a small nature reserve managed by Hertfordshire Wildlife Trust. It features grassland, scrub, and wet woodland habitats. The site supports diverse flora and fauna, providing valuable ecological corridors for wildlife.

Name: Blair-nam-Faoileag NNR
Description: Blair-nam-Faoileag National Nature Reserve protects a vast area of blanket bog, forming part of the internationally important Flow Country of Caithness and Sutherland. This peatland landscape supports diverse wildlife.

Name: Blakehill Farm
Description: Blakehill Farm, a former WWII airfield in Wiltshire, is a 250-hectare nature reserve transformed into species-rich grassland, wetlands, and arable margins. It supports diverse wildlife, including skylarks, lapwings, invertebrates, and wildflowers, maintained through conservation grazing.

Name: Blakeney National Nature Reserve
Description: Blakeney National Nature Reserve in Norfolk features Blakeney Point, home to England's largest grey seal colony. It serves as a vital nesting ground for various bird species and holds international importance for wildlife. Visitors can explore the shingle beach.

Name: Blakey Topping
Description: Blakey Topping is a distinctive conical hill in the North York Moors National Park. This landmark offers panoramic views across the Pickering valley and features unique geological formations, including sandstone outcrops. It forms part of a wider landscape managed for its natural beauty and heritage.

Name: Blashford Lakes
Description: Blashford Lakes Nature Reserve, near Ringwood, spans 150 hectares of lakes, woodland, and grassland, formed from former gravel pits. Managed by Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust, it is a key site for resident and migratory birds, offering hides and walking trails.

Name: Blashford Lakes Nature Reserve
Description: Blashford Lakes Nature Reserve is a key wintering site for thousands of wildfowl and other water birds. Managed by Hampshire & Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust, it encompasses former gravel pits, River Avon floodplain, woodlands and grasslands, supporting a diverse range of wildlife throughout the year.

Name: Blaxhall Common
Description: Blaxhall Common is a Suffolk SSSI featuring dry and wet heath, fen, and woodland habitats. It supports specialist heathland birds like nightjar and woodlark, alongside adders and silver-studded blue butterflies. Public access is available.

Name: Blickling Estate
Description: Blickling Estate in Norfolk features a Jacobean house, historic gardens, and extensive parkland with ancient trees. Managed by the National Trust, it offers woodland walks, lakeside paths, and diverse natural habitats near Aylsham.

Name: Blindley Heath
Description: Blindley Heath is a lowland wet grassland and heathland site located in Surrey, south-east England. It supports diverse flora and fauna, including rare invertebrates and ground-nesting birds. The site is managed for conservation, with habitat restoration ongoing.

Name: Bloody Oaks Quarry
Description: Bloody Oaks Quarry, a former limestone quarry in Rutland, is now a Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust nature reserve. It features unimproved limestone grassland, a priority habitat rich in wildflowers such as the bee orchid. Diverse butterflies and insects thrive, with scrub and trees providing valuable bird habitats.

Name: Blow's Downs
Description: Blow's Downs is a 62.3-hectare nature reserve, which includes a 33.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Dunstable, Bedfordshire. Managed by the Wildlife Trust BCN, this chalk grassland, scrub, and woodland site hosts rare plants like the Pasque flower and diverse butterflies, including Chalkhill Blue. It offers panoramic views.

Name: Bloxholm Wood
Description: Bloxholm Wood is an ancient, ash-dominated semi-natural woodland, also featuring sycamore and horse chestnut. Its rich ground flora includes early purple orchids and bugle. The reserve hosts diverse birdlife, such as buzzards, woodcock, tawny owl, and nuthatch, along with various woodland insects. It is managed by the Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust for biodiversity.

Name: Blue House Farm
Description: Blue House Farm is a coastal farm reserve on the River Blackwater, featuring grazing marsh, mudflats, and saltmarsh. It is vital for wintering wildfowl and waders, including Brent Geese and Pintail. Water levels are controlled via ditches and sluices for wildlife habitats. Footpath access is available.

Name: Bluebank Pools
Description: Bluebank Pools, on the Chesterfield Canal near Staveley, is a former subsidence flash. It now thrives as a vibrant wetland, teeming with diverse wildlife and offering a significant habitat for various species.

Name: Blythe Alive - River Blythe SSSI
Description: Blythe Alive focuses on restoring the River Blythe SSSI and its surrounding habitats. The project enhances biodiversity and climate change resilience by removing weirs, reconnecting the river with its floodplain, and creating new wetlands and ponds. It also involves community engagement.

Name: Bo'mains Meadow
Description: Bo'mains Meadow is a small, species-rich grassland located near Linlithgow, West Lothian. It features a diverse range of wildflowers, including common spotted orchid and cowslip, supporting various insect species.

Name: Boathouse Field
Description: Boathouse Field is a riverside meadow beside Derwentwater near Keswick. This site forms part of a larger network of wetland habitats. Grazing maintains species-rich grassland, supporting diverse flora including rare tubular water-dropwort and water voles.

Name: Boddington Meadow
Description: Boddington Meadow is a traditionally-managed, unploughed floodplain meadow in Northamptonshire. It supports diverse wildflowers and grasses, providing habitat for a wide range of insects and birds. The site is managed to enhance its biodiversity for wildlife.

Name: Bodenham Lake
Description: Bodenham Lake is one of the largest stretches of open water in Herefordshire, covering approximately 50 acres. Managed by Herefordshire Wildlife Trust, it is a significant reserve for wintering wildfowl and various water birds, with over 170 bird species recorded. It is also a key breeding site for otters and toads. The reserve is designated as a Site of Local Importance, and where it borders the River Lugg, it is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and Special Area of Conservation. The site features multiple bird hides, reedbeds, wet woodland, orchards, and meadows, focusing on habitat conservation and visitor engagement.

Name: Bodnant Garden
Description: Bodnant Garden is a National Trust property near Tal-y-bont, Conwy, Wales. It features formal gardens, grand terraces, wooded glades, and an arboretum with champion trees. The garden offers stunning views of the Conwy Valley and Snowdonia.

Name: Bog Meadows
Description: Bog Meadows, situated off the Falls Road in West Belfast, is a vital urban nature reserve. It offers a mosaic of reedbeds, meadows, ponds, and woodland, providing sanctuary for diverse wildlife including water rail, snipe, and various dragonflies.

Name: Boilton Nab Redscar and Tunbrook Woods
Description: Boilton Nab, Redscar, and Tunbrook Woods form a mosaic of woodland, grassland, and river habitats along the River Ribble. The site features ancient woodland, open grassland, and riverside paths, supporting diverse wildlife and industrial heritage.

Name: Bolam Lake
Description: Bolam Lake Country Park, located between Belsay and Whalton, offers extensive footpaths, lakeside walks, and open grasslands. The site supports diverse wildlife, including red squirrels and birds, across its managed woodlands and meadows, providing recreational and nature study.

Name: Bolberry Down
Description: Bolberry Down offers dramatic coastal views near Salcombe. This area features rare wildflowers, birds, and insects, making it a valuable habitat. Visitors can walk the South West Coast Path and enjoy the rugged coastline.

Name: Bold Forest Park
Description: Bold Forest Park in St Helens is a significant regeneration project transforming 450 hectares of former industrial land into new woodlands, wetlands, and grasslands. It offers walking, cycling, and horse riding opportunities and is part of the larger Mersey Forest initiative.

Name: Bolderwood
Description: Bolderwood, located in the New Forest, features ancient woodlands and walking trails. Visitors can observe fallow deer from a purpose-built viewing platform at the deer sanctuary. The area offers various routes through mature trees and picnic facilities.

Name: Bolgoed Quarry
Description: Bolgoed Quarry is a former quarry near Pontarddulais, transformed into a rich wildlife habitat. It features mixed deciduous woodland, dense gorse scrub, and quarry faces irrigated by groundwater. The reserve supports diverse woodland birds like Chiffchaff, Great Tit, and Tawny Owl, and its damp quarry floor is a winter roost for Woodcock. This site demonstrates a successful transition from industrial land to a biodiverse landscape.

Name: Bolt Head to Bolt Tail
Description: This dramatic stretch of South Devon coastline between Bolt Head and Bolt Tail offers spectacular views and diverse wildlife. Walk the South West Coast Path, exploring jagged cliffs and secluded coves rich in maritime history.

Name: Boltby Forest
Description: Boltby Forest, a 632.1-hectare mixed woodland managed by Forestry England, is situated in the Cleveland Hills within the south-west corner of the North York Moors National Park. Dominated by Sitka spruce, it also features broadleaves and ancient woodlands, supporting diverse flora and fauna, including Lake Gormire SSSI. The forest offers extensive walking and cycling trails, with the Cleveland Way skirting its eastern edge, and provides views across the Vale of Mowbray.

Name: Bolton Percy Station
Description: Bolton Percy Station Nature Reserve, near Appleton Roebuck, preserves grassland and scrub habitats on a former railway line. This site supports a variety of wildflowers, butterflies, and moths, acting as a crucial wildlife corridor.

Name: Bolton-on-Swale Lake
Description: Bolton-on-Swale Lake, a former sand and gravel quarry near the River Swale, is now a wetland nature reserve. It supports overwintering wildfowl and breeding waders. Reedbeds and open water habitats provide diverse wildlife. The site is managed for conservation.

Name: Bonny Grove
Description: Bonny Grove is a small woodland in Middlesbrough, managed by Tees Valley Wildlife Trust. It provides a vital green space for both wildlife and people, featuring mature trees and a diverse understory of plant life, offering a quiet natural retreat.

Name: Bonny Wood
Description: Bonny Wood is an ancient coppice woodland and part of the Barking Tye woods, which are a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). It features diverse habitats, including newly planted areas and rides, and is home to various tree species like oak, ash, hazel, and field maple. The reserve supports a range of wildlife, including birds (such as blackcap and willow warbler), butterflies, badgers, and deer. Notable flora includes wood anemone, woodruff, herb-paris, and various orchids like early-purple, lesser twayblade, common spotted, and greater butterfly orchids. The site also features ponds and streams.

Name: Bonsai Bank
Description: Bonsai Bank is a flower-rich chalk grassland area within Denge Wood, known for its diverse orchid populations, including the rare Lady Orchid. It features stunted conifers, which gave it its name, and supports a rich ground flora on its sloping terrain.

Name: Boon's Copse
Description: Boon's Copse is a species-rich ancient woodland on the Blackdown Hills, a relic of the original Neroche Royal Forest. It is predominantly hazel coppice with oak standards, providing a habitat for diverse woodland birds, dormice, and a rich invertebrate fauna. The woodland floor supports ancient woodland indicator species such as bluebells, primroses, wild garlic, greater butterfly orchid, and wood anemone.

Name: Booton Common
Description: Booton Common is a small nature reserve managed by Norfolk Wildlife Trust, located in a tributary valley of the River Wensum near Reepham. This species-rich fen and wet heathland is a treasure trove of wildflowers and rare plants, including adder's tongue, marsh helleborine, grass-of-Parnassus, and fragrant orchid.

Name: Booton Common
Description: Booton Common is an 8.2-hectare (20-acre) biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Norfolk, managed by Norfolk Wildlife Trust. It features diverse habitats including rich fen, wet heathland, damp calcareous grassland, and alder carr woodland, supporting a variety of wildflowers, insects, and bird species. Visitors can explore marked trails.

Name: Border Mires
Description: The Border Mires are a vast complex of peatlands located within Northumberland National Park. Active restoration enhances biodiversity, improves water quality, and sequesters carbon. This site forms a key part of the wider peatland recovery programme.

Name: Borough Hill
Description: Borough Hill, a Local Nature Reserve near Daventry, comprises heathland, grassland, and scrub. It supports rare plants and diverse butterflies. The site includes an Iron Age hillfort and Roman villa remains, with views across Northamptonshire.

Name: Borrowdale Rainforest Project
Description: The Borrowdale Rainforest Project, a National Trust initiative, aims to restore and expand temperate rainforests across the Borrowdale valley in the Lake District. It focuses on regenerating ancient woodlands and enhancing biodiversity.

Name: Bossington Beach
Description: Bossington Beach, part of the Holnicote Estate in Somerset, is a shingle beach forming a natural barrier with saltmarshes. It offers views across the Bristol Channel and is a starting point for coastal walks.

Name: Bosvenning Common
Description: Bosvenning Common is a small nature reserve near Newbridge, Penzance, managed by Cornwall Wildlife Trust. It protects an undisturbed heathland with three different species of wild heathers, featuring cross-leaved heath and bog asphodel. The site supports diverse invertebrates and amphibians within a rare habitat, offering spectacular views of the surrounding Penwith landscape.

Name: Bough Beech
Description: Bough Beech reservoir and surrounding woodland in west Kent is a Site of Special Scientific Interest. Formerly managed by Kent Wildlife Trust until July 2020, it is now managed by Sutton and East Surrey Water. It offers important habitats for wildfowl, waders, and gulls, with bird hides available for observation.

Name: Bouldnor Forest
Description: Bouldnor Forest is an ancient woodland on the western Solent coast near Yarmouth, Isle of Wight. It features diverse habitats including saltmarsh, reedbeds, meadows, and mature broadleaf woodland, supporting a range of wildlife.

Name: Bouldnor Forest Nature Reserve
Description: Bouldnor Forest is a coastal woodland and heathland mosaic on the Isle of Wight. It supports raptors, reptiles such as slow worms and adders, and rare invertebrates. The reserve offers views across the Solent and forms part of the Hamstead Heritage Coast.

Name: Boulmer Steel
Description: Boulmer Steel is an intertidal rock habitat situated on the Northumberland coast. The site is actively monitored by Northumberland Wildlife Trust for the presence of marine non-native species, contributing to regional biodiversity conservation efforts.

Name: Boundary Wood
Description: Boundary Wood is a newly established woodland site near Mansfield, Nottinghamshire, managed by Forestry England. It features a mix of broadleaf and conifer trees with accessible paths, contributing to local biodiversity and community green space.

Name: Bourne Mill
Description: Bourne Mill is a Grade I listed 16th-century watermill in Colchester, Essex, owned by the National Trust. Originally built as a fishing lodge in 1591, it was later converted into a fulling mill and then a corn mill. The site features a historic building with a working waterwheel, a large spring-fed millpond, and surrounding wetlands and woods. It is a haven for diverse wildlife, including kingfishers, various waterfowl, bats, dragonflies, and damselflies.

Name: Bourne Wood
Description: Bourne Wood, near Farnham in Surrey, is an ancient woodland on the Greensand Ridge. Managed by Forestry England, it offers walking paths through mature trees and open heathland, popular with locals and dog walkers. It serves as a haven for diverse wildlife.

Name: Bovey Heathfield
Description: Bovey Heathfield, near Newton Abbot, is a surviving fragment of the extensive Bovey Basin heathlands. This important nature reserve is one of Devon Wildlife Trust's most significant sites for invertebrates, hosting many rare and protected species, including the nationally rare heath tiger beetle and the silver-studded blue butterfly.

Name: Bovey Valley Woods
Description: Bovey Valley Woods, within Dartmoor National Park, is an ancient woodland patchwork along the River Bovey. Managed by The Woodland Trust, it provides critical habitat for dormice, otters, and rare bats, featuring significant geological formations.

Name: Bovingdon Flood Meadow
Description: Bovingdon Flood Meadow is a wetland site by the River Brain near Bocking. It supports diverse wildlife, including kingfishers and watervoles, within its mature trees, scrub, sedges, and wildflowers. The meadow functions as a natural flood plain.

Name: Bow Creek Ecology Park
Description: Bow Creek Ecology Park is a wildlife haven in East London, at the confluence of Bow Creek and the River Thames. It features diverse wetland and brownfield habitats, supporting birds, insects, and plants, with peaceful walking routes and viewing platforms.

Name: Bowber Head Farm
Description: Bowber Head Farm is a 30-hectare nature reserve near Kirkby Stephen, Westmorland Dales. It features species-rich upland hay meadows, traditional barns, and diverse habitats supporting rare flora like globeflower and wood crane's-bill.

Name: Bowdown Woods
Description: Bowdown Woods, near Thatcham, Berkshire, is a diverse nature reserve. It comprises ancient woodland, heathland, and acid grassland habitats. Managed by BBOWT, the site supports various wildlife, including rare fungi. Public footpaths are present for access.

Name: Bowesfield
Description: Bowesfield, near Stockton-on-Tees, is an internationally important wetland nature reserve. Part of the Teesmouth and Cleveland Coast SSSI, this former quarry on the River Tees' west bank supports diverse bird species, otters, water voles, and rare plants.

Name: Bowesfield Wetland
Description: Bowesfield Wetland is a former gravel quarry restored to a wildlife haven near Stockton-on-Tees. It features shallow wetland habitats and open water, providing important breeding and feeding grounds for various bird species, amphibians, and invertebrates.

Name: Bowness on Solway
Description: Bowness-on-Solway is a coastal nature reserve at the western end of Hadrian's Wall in Cumbria, managed by Cumbria Wildlife Trust. Originally a gravel quarry, it now features diverse habitats including ponds, grassland, and scrub, supporting species like Great Crested Newts, Pond Mud Snails, and various dragonflies. Its coastal location also makes it an important feeding and roosting site for migratory birds such as oystercatcher, curlew, and redshank.

Name: Box Hill
Description: Box Hill is a prominent North Downs summit in Surrey, England, offering panoramic views across the Surrey Hills. Managed by the National Trust, it features woodlands, chalk grasslands, and walking trails.

Name: Box Meadows
Description: Box Meadows is a Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust reserve near Minchinhampton Common. It features species-rich unimproved grassland, ancient hedgerows, and is grazed by cattle. The site provides a vital wildlife corridor in the Stroud Valleys.

Name: Box Wood
Description: Box Wood is an ancient woodland near Painswick, Gloucestershire, dominated by mature beech trees. Located on the limestone scarp, it offers views across the Severn Vale. Hazel and ash are present in the understory alongside varied flora.

Name: Boxford Water Meadows
Description: Boxford Water Meadows is a diverse wetland reserve in Berkshire, featuring flower-rich meadows, reedbeds, and wet woodland. The River Lambourn flows through the site, supporting water voles, otters, kingfishers, and dragonflies.

Name: Bracketts Coppice
Description: Bracketts Coppice is a small ancient semi-natural woodland in West Dorset, managed by Dorset Wildlife Trust. The site includes a valley with a fast-flowing stream and hazel coppice, providing a vital habitat for various plants and insects, including dormice, otters, and woodpeckers. It is managed for nature conservation.

Name: Brackfield Wood
Description: Brackfield Wood is The Woodland Trust's First World War Centenary Wood for Ireland, nestled within the stunning Faughan Valley Woodlands, a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). It is home to native tree species and diverse wildlife, including red squirrel, otter, and Atlantic salmon in the River Faughan. The site offers a network of footpaths for walking and nature observation, providing views of the River Faughan, and connects with other woods in the Faughan Valley.

Name: Bradfield Woods
Description: Bradfield Woods is a significant ancient coppice woodland in Suffolk, traditionally managed for over 700 years. This National Nature Reserve features hornbeam and hazel coppice, glades, and rides, supporting a rich diversity of flora and fauna. It provides a vital habitat for numerous species.

Name: Bradlaugh Fields
Description: Bradlaugh Fields is a 60-hectare open space in Northampton, with 17.5 hectares managed as a nature reserve by the Wildlife Trust BCN. It features ancient ridge and furrow grassland, wildflower meadows, and mature hedgerows. The reserve is known for its unimproved, semi-natural limestone grassland, supporting diverse bird species like blue tits and sparrowhawks, various insects, and mammals such as foxes and badgers. Public footpaths allow access for recreation.

Name: Bradley Canal Restoration & Habitat Link
Description: This project restores a disused canal stretch in Bilston, West Midlands, creating a vital 'green corridor' linking existing green spaces. It aims to improve access to green and blue spaces and provide new walking and cycling routes.

Name: Bradwell Shell Bank
Description: Bradwell Shell Bank is a coastal nature reserve on the Dengie Peninsula near Bradwell-on-Sea, Essex. Managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust, it features extensive shell banks of cockle and oyster shells and saltmarsh. The site is internationally important for breeding birds such as little terns, ringed plovers, and oystercatchers, and hosts large flocks of overwintering waders including grey plovers, knots, and bar-tailed godwits. It is part of the Dengie Site of Special Scientific Interest, Special Protection Area, and Ramsar site, and supports diverse flora like yellow-horned poppies and sea lavender.

Name: Brae Pasture
Description: Brae Pasture nature reserve, near Selside and Horton-in-Ribblesdale, is part of the Ingleborough National Nature Reserve. It features species-rich grassland, limestone pavement, and scrub, supporting diverse flora including rare Alpine bistort and various orchids, as well as numerous insects like the Northern brown argus butterfly. Management focuses on maintaining habitat diversity and protecting its 150 plant species.

Name: Braeburn Park
Description: Braeburn Park is a 22.3-hectare nature reserve in Crayford, southeast London, managed by the London Wildlife Trust. It features a diverse mix of habitats including woodlands, grasslands (chalk, acid, and neutral), scrub, relict orchard, sandy banks, steep cliffs, and a pond. The site is a haven for invertebrates and supports diverse wildlife such as kestrels, grass snakes, common lizards, and various butterflies. It also includes Wansunt Pit, a geological Site of Special Scientific Interest. Footpaths offer views across the River Cray valley.

Name: Bramley Bank
Description: Bramley Bank is a local nature reserve with ancient woodland, meadow, and a pond in South Croydon. It supports diverse wildlife, including nuthatches, kestrels, and various invertebrates. Footpaths provide access through the site for visitors.

Name: Brampton Wood
Description: Brampton Wood is a 130-hectare ancient woodland in Cambridgeshire, once part of the Royal Forest of Huntingdonshire. Managed for biodiversity, it features diverse tree species, wildflowers, and wildlife habitats for public enjoyment.

Name: Bramshill Forest
Description: Bramshill Forest in Hampshire features ancient woodland, conifer plantations, and heathland. It provides habitat for rare species like the Dartford warbler, nightjar, and sand lizard. The forest offers various walking trails for visitors to explore its diverse landscapes.

Name: Brancaster Beach
Description: Brancaster Beach, on the Norfolk coast, is a vast National Trust sandy expanse popular for walking and birdwatching. The SS Vina shipwreck is visible at low tide. This site protects diverse coastal wildlife and offers expansive views.

Name: Brancaster Staithe
Description: Brancaster Staithe is a harbour village on the North Norfolk coast, managed by the National Trust. It features extensive saltmarsh and mudflats, home to diverse wading birds like oystercatchers and curlews. The area is popular for sailing and provides vital habitat.

Name: Brandlehow Woods
Description: Brandlehow Woods is an ancient woodland on the western shore of Derwent Water in the Lake District. The National Trust acquired it in 1902, making it their first property. It provides public access and walking routes near the lake.

Name: Brandon Country Park
Description: Brandon Country Park, within Thetford Forest, Suffolk, covers 30 acres of parkland and 300 acres of woodland. It features an arboretum, lake, mausoleum, visitor centre, and a tea room. Miles of trails are available for walking, cycling, and riding.

Name: Brandon Hill Nature Reserve
Description: Brandon Hill is Bristol's oldest park, rising steeply behind Park Street. The site offers panoramic city and harbour views, with wildflower meadows, mature trees, and a pond. It is managed by Avon Wildlife Trust to enhance biodiversity for urban wildlife.

Name: Brandon Reach
Description: Brandon Reach is a Warwickshire Wildlife Trust nature reserve near Coventry. It protects ancient woodland and species-rich grassland, home to mature oak and ash trees. The site supports diverse wildlife, including birds and invertebrates, and provides walking trails for visitors.

Name: Brandon Wood
Description: Brandon Wood, a former golf course near Coventry, undergoes rewilding by Warwickshire Wildlife Trust. It creates a diverse mosaic of woodland, grassland, and wetland habitats, supporting various wildlife and aiding ecological recovery efforts locally.

Name: Brankley Pastures
Description: Brankley Pastures is an ancient wood pasture, featuring venerable oak and ash trees. It supports a diverse range of invertebrates, fungi, and lichens, including nationally rare species. The site is managed for conservation, with grazing maintaining the open woodland structure.

Name: Branscombe to Beer Cliffs
Description: Branscombe to Beer Cliffs is a dramatic coastal area in East Devon, managed by the National Trust. It features striking cliffs, secluded beaches, and ancient woodlands. Part of the Jurassic Coast World Heritage Site, it offers diverse wildlife and geological formations.

Name: Brassey
Description: Brassey is a two-hectare nature reserve in the Cotswolds, managed by Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust. It is a significant site for biodiversity, comprising both unimproved limestone grassland and one of Gloucestershire's few freshwater marshes. It protects diverse wildflowers and insects, including rare species like the Pasqueflower and Duke of Burgundy butterfly, as well as unique marshland plants.

Name: Brean Down
Description: Brean Down is a prominent limestone headland in Somerset, offering panoramic views over the Bristol Channel. It features an Iron Age hill fort and a 19th-century fort. The site is known for its diverse wildlife and coastal habitats, providing historical walks and natural beauty.

Name: Bredhurst Wood
Description: Bredhurst Woods is a 600-acre (approximately 240-hectare) ancient woodland surrounded by chalk grassland, located on the North Downs in Kent. It is a Local Wildlife Site and part of the Kent Downs Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. Primarily managed by the Bredhurst Woodland Action Group (BWAG) in collaboration with Kent Wildlife Trust, the site features diverse oak, hornbeam, and sweet chestnut trees, and supports a rich biodiversity including fungi, invertebrates, butterflies (such as Adonis blue), and dormice.

Name: Bredhurst Woods
Description: Bredhurst Woods is a tranquil nature reserve comprising 600 acres of ancient woodland and chalk grassland near Bredhurst. Dominated by oak, ash, and hazel, the site supports diverse flora and fauna, including many bird species, orchids, and invertebrates within its undergrowth, along its paths, and near a small stream. It is managed by the Bredhurst Woodland Action Group (BWAG) in partnership with Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Breney Common
Description: Breney Common is a designated SSSI and SAC in Cornwall, forming part of the Mid Cornwall Moors. This lowland wet heath and valley mire supports diverse wetland flora and fauna, including rare butterflies and birds, managed for conservation.

Name: Brentmoor Heath & Folly Bog
Description: Brentmoor Heath & Folly Bog is an SSSI near West End, Woking. This nature reserve features a mosaic of open heathland, bog, wet and dry grassland, and woodland. It supports diverse wildlife including Dartford warbler, nightjar, woodlark, and great crested newts.

Name: Brett's Wood
Description: Brett's Wood is a 33.5-hectare nature reserve near Fakenham, Norfolk. It comprises a former conifer plantation undergoing restoration to woodland and heathland. The site features planted oak, sweet chestnut, and hornbeam, creating new habitats for local wildlife.

Name: Brettenham Heath
Description: Brettenham Heath is a National Nature Reserve in Norfolk, located north-east of Thetford. It is an important area of heathland, woodland, and acid grassland, forming part of the Breckland Special Area of Conservation and Special Protection Area. The reserve supports breeding woodlark, nightjar, and stone-curlew, along with reptiles such as slow-worm, common lizard, and adder. It is home to a diverse flora with over 240 plant species recorded.

Name: Brickfield Meadow
Description: Brickfield Meadow is a delightful unimproved meadow on the edge of the Ashdown Forest, near Fairwarp and Maresfield in East Sussex. It is a wildflower-rich site supporting many characteristic Wealden meadow plants. The site features mature hedgerows and a small stream, providing a valuable habitat for various insects, amphibians, and bird species.

Name: Briddlesford Woods
Description: Briddlesford Woods is an ancient woodland and Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) on the Isle of Wight, managed by the People's Trust for Endangered Species (PTES). It is a significant habitat for red squirrels, dormice, and various bird species, featuring a mix of oak, ash, and hazel.

Name: Bridestones, Crosscliff and Blakey Topping
Description: Bridestones, Crosscliff and Blakey Topping presents dramatic moorland in the North York Moors National Park. Wind and ice shaped the spectacular rock formations, including the Bride and Groom. The site features ancient woodland, heather moorland, and rich biodiversity, offering walking trails and scenic views. Managed by the National Trust.

Name: Bridgham Heath
Description: Bridgham Heath, a fragment of Breckland heathland in Norfolk, features dry acid grassland, heather, and small copses. It supports diverse insects, common lizards, and various bird species, actively managed for conservation.

Name: Brierdene LNR
Description: Brierdene LNR, also known as Brierdene Wildlife Site, is a coastal denemouth and designated Site of Nature Conservation Importance (SNCI) in Whitley Bay, North Tyneside. It encompasses woodland, grassland, and freshwater habitats, supporting diverse wildlife. The dene connects directly to the beach, offering varied coastal and woodland environments. It is actively managed by the Friends of Brierdene, with support from Northumberland Wildlife Trust.

Name: Brilley Green Dingle
Description: Brilley Green Dingle is a small but important ancient woodland nature reserve in Herefordshire, managed by the Herefordshire Wildlife Trust. It is entirely wooded, with different management histories on its western and eastern sides, reflected in the rich ground flora, including bluebells and wood anemones. The dingle structure creates a sheltered habitat, with Millhalf Brook running through the reserve, providing a home for interesting invertebrates like the white-clawed crayfish. Notable species include Dipper, Wood warbler, Pied flycatcher, Hazel dormouse, and Early purple orchid.

Name: Brimham Rocks
Description: Brimham Rocks, a biological SSSI in North Yorkshire, features unique rock formations sculpted over 320 million years by natural erosion. This moorland landscape offers free access and supports diverse wildlife.

Name: Brimley Hill Mire
Description: Brimley Hill Mire is a small acidic mire and wetland system on Greensand in East Devon. It supports rare mosses, diverse dragonflies including the golden-ringed dragonfly, and plants like bog asphodel. Managed via grazing and scrub control.

Name: Brinsley Headstocks
Description: Brinsley Headstocks is a 5.17-hectare Local Nature Reserve near Eastwood, Nottinghamshire. The site preserves former colliery structures and offers diverse habitats, including grassland and wetlands, supporting varied wildlife. It is managed for both heritage and biodiversity.

Name: Broad Oak Orchard
Description: Broad Oak Orchard is a small, traditional orchard near Stourpaine, Dorset. It features various apple, pear, and plum trees, providing habitat and food for local wildlife. The site is actively managed to enhance biodiversity and preserve traditional fruit varieties.

Name: Broadham Down
Description: Broadham Down is a 16-hectare nature reserve east of Chilham, Kent, managed by Kent Wildlife Trust. This site features chalk grassland, woodland, and scrub, offering views over the Stour Valley. It supports diverse wildlife, including three species of bat and various flowering plants like fragrant and common spotted orchids.

Name: Broadhead Clough
Description: Broadhead Clough is a small, wooded valley with a stream flowing to the River Calder. This ancient woodland reserve features mature oak, ash, and birch, supporting diverse flora. Notable species include bluebells and wood anemones. The site is actively managed for conservation.

Name: Broadhurst Edge Wood
Description: Broadhurst Edge Wood is a steep-sided woodland in Derbyshire, dominated by mature sessile oak, birch, and hazel. Ground flora includes bluebell, wood sorrel, and dog's mercury. The site is important for woodland birds and invertebrates. A public footpath runs through the site.

Name: Broadmead
Description: Broadmead is a small wetland nature reserve located east of Colchester, near Elmstead. It features a mosaic of habitats including wet woodland, reedbeds, scrub, and grassland, supporting diverse wildlife. The reserve provides an important habitat for water voles and other species.

Name: Broadstreet Backside & Rydes Commons
Description: Broadstreet Backside & Rydes Commons is a Surrey nature reserve featuring heathland, woodland, and ponds. It supports rare marsh gentian and diverse birdlife including Dartford warblers and nightjars. This site is a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Broadwater Lake
Description: Broadwater Lake is a large lake with extensive reedbeds, wet woodland, and grassland habitats, supporting a diverse array of wildlife. It is home to significant bird populations and various invertebrates, serving as a key site for nature conservation and observation.

Name: Broadwater Lake SSSI
Description: Broadwater Lake SSSI is a former gravel extraction site. It supports significant populations of wildfowl, including wintering gadwall, pochard, and shoveler. Important aquatic vegetation thrives here, contributing to diverse wetland habitats.

Name: Broaks Wood
Description: Broaks Wood is a mature ancient woodland in Essex, featuring hornbeam, ash, and oak trees, and notably a unique Giant Redwood Grove. It contains an ancient stream, medieval fishpond remains, and seasonal ponds. Wildflowers like wood anemone, bluebell, and ramsons thrive here, and it is managed by Forestry England with conservation as a priority.

Name: Brockadale
Description: Brockadale is a nationally important magnesian limestone woodland and grassland reserve in West Yorkshire's Went Valley. It features ancient woodland, wildflower-rich grassland, and the River Went, supporting rare orchids, butterflies, and diverse bird species.

Name: Brockhampton Estate
Description: Brockhampton Estate is a medieval manor house and estate set in a secluded valley near Bringsty, Herefordshire. The property features ancient orchards, woodlands, and a working farm. Visitors can explore the timber-framed house, a moat, and 1,000 acres of parkland.

Name: Brockholes Wood
Description: Brockholes Wood is an ancient upland oak woodland with moorland in the far north of Derbyshire, near Crowden, managed by Derbyshire Wildlife Trust. It features sessile oak, hairy birch, and rowan, supporting diverse bird species like tree pipit, wren, willow warbler, redstart, blue tit, mistle thrushes, blackbirds, and fieldfare. Public footpaths provide access to this valuable wildlife habitat, which is one of the few remaining areas of its kind.

Name: Brodsworth Community Woodland
Description: Brodsworth Community Woodland is a former colliery site in South Yorkshire. TCV supports its management, with ongoing activities including path maintenance, tree planting, and coppicing. The woodland offers views across the Dearne Valley.

Name: Bromeswell Green
Description: Bromeswell Green, managed by Suffolk Wildlife Trust, is a nature reserve in Suffolk. It features wet grassland, reedbed, and wet woodland habitats, supporting diverse birds and invertebrates. The site is a key area for local wildlife conservation.

Name: Brompton Cemetery
Description: Brompton Cemetery is a Grade I listed garden cemetery established in 1840 in West London. It features over 20,000 monuments, including notable figures like Emmeline Pankhurst, and a diverse range of trees and wildlife. Managed by The Royal Parks, it is a site of special historic interest.

Name: Brook Vessons
Description: Brook Vessons is a Shropshire Wildlife Trust reserve featuring upland heathland, acid grassland, woodland, and wetlands.
