Description: Greno Woods near Sheffield is an ancient woodland and heathland. It features oak, birch, and rowan trees, with diverse flora like bilberry and ling heather. Wildlife includes roe deer, badger, and many bird species. A Local Wildlife Site, it offers walking and cycling.

Name: Grey Hope Bay
Description: Greyhope Bay is an award-winning community-led marine experience at the mouth of Aberdeen Harbour. It offers views of bottlenose dolphins, harbour porpoise, grey seals, and various seabirds. The site features a repurposed shipping container visitor centre and cafe.

Name: Grey Mare's Tail
Description: Grey Mare's Tail is a dramatic 60m waterfall in the Moffat Water Valley, offering a challenging upland walk to a tranquil loch above. The nature reserve is home to peregrine falcons, ospreys during summer, and a population of wild mountain goats.

Name: Greyfield Wood
Description: Greyfield Wood is a 36.23-hectare (89.5-acre) ancient woodland situated on the outskirts of High Littleton in north-east Somerset, approximately 16 km from Bath and 19 km from Bristol. Managed by the Woodland Trust, it features a diverse mix of ancient broadleaf trees, naturally regenerated areas, and conifer plantations, supporting a rich array of flora and fauna. It offers extensive permissive paths for public access, including circular walks.

Name: Greylake
Description: Greylake is an RSPB nature reserve situated on the Somerset Levels. The site features an accessible hide and boardwalk, offering views of wetland birds such as lapwings, snipe, and various duck species. It provides habitat for diverse wildlife, with seasonal highlights including breeding waders and wintering wildfowl.

Name: Greystones Farm
Description: Greystones Farm is a 66-hectare nature reserve in Bourton-on-the-Water, Gloucestershire. It features wildflower meadows, the River Eye, and Iron Age archaeology. The site protects wildlife, including rare native plants and aquatic species, offering visitor walks and learning experiences.

Name: Greywell Moors
Description: Greywell Moors is a tranquil wetland nature reserve in northeast Hampshire, managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust. It is a nationally important fenland, part of the Greywell Fen Site of Special Scientific Interest, featuring a mosaic of habitats including chalk stream (the River Whitewater), fen, and wet woodland. It supports diverse wildlife, including rare species, and is renowned for its sedges, rushes, mosses, and liverworts. The collapsed Greywell Tunnel of the Basingstoke Canal, located within the reserve, is a hugely important site for bats.

Name: Greywell Moors
Description: Greywell Moors, a Hampshire SSSI, is a significant chalk spring fed mire system supporting rare invertebrates, blunt-flowered rush, and early marsh orchids. Otters, water voles, and kingfishers inhabit this important wetland, managed through grazing.

Name: Griffin Wood
Description: Griffin Wood is a 12-hectare community woodland in Bold, south St. Helens, Merseyside, managed by The Mersey Forest in partnership with the Friends of Griffin Wood. It comprises both mature and newly planted broadleaved trees and pines, along with wildflower meadows. The site features meandering paths, a community orchard, and a sculpture trail, offering green space for recreation and nature observation. It is part of the larger Bold Forest Park.

Name: Grime’s Graves
Description: Grime’s Graves is a unique Neolithic flint mine site and Scheduled Monument, managed by English Heritage. It features diverse chalk grassland and woodland, supporting rare plants like the military orchid and various invertebrate species, important for its archaeology and biodiversity, with ecological input from Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Grimwith Reservoir
Description: Grimwith Reservoir, a large upland reservoir in the Yorkshire Dales National Park near Pateley Bridge, supplies drinking water. It features extensive peat bogs, heather moorland, and grasslands, supporting diverse wildlife and critical habitats for wading birds.

Name: Gringley Carr
Description: Gringley Carr is the northern section of Idle Valley Nature Reserve, a large wetland site north of Retford. It covers arable farmland on peaty soil, drained by ditches, alongside a 2km section of the River Idle.

Name: Grizedale Forest
Description: Grizedale Forest, located in the Lake District, features an extensive network of walking and cycling trails through woodlands. It is home to a unique collection of outdoor sculptures and provides habitats for diverse wildlife, including red deer. A visitor centre offers amenities.

Name: Grogley Wood
Description: Grogley Wood, part of the larger Bishop's, Hustyn, and Grogley Woods complex, is a semi-ancient woodland site near Bodmin, Cornwall. Managed by Forestry England, it features broadleaf and conifer areas, rich ground flora, and diverse birdlife. The woods are popular for public footpaths and offer extensive mountain biking trails, with connections to the Camel Trail.

Name: Groton Wood
Description: Groton Wood is a 20.2-hectare ancient woodland in Suffolk, managed by Suffolk Wildlife Trust. It features diverse habitats like oak, hornbeam, and hazel coppice, supporting dormice, nightingales, and many insects. Public footpaths allow access near Hadleigh.

Name: Grove Park
Description: Grove Hill Nature Reserve is one of Warwickshire's largest areas of semi-natural limestone grassland, featuring a mosaic of grass, scrub, woodland, and ponds. It supports diverse flora, including orchids and rare wildflowers, and a rich array of insects like butterflies and moths. The reserve is also home to various birds, deer, and dragonflies.

Name: Grovelands Park
Description: Grovelands Park is a Grade II* listed Green Flag park in Enfield, London. It features extensive woodlands, a formal garden, and a large lake. The lake has undergone enhancements to boost its biodiversity, supporting local wildlife.

Name: Grubbins Wood
Description: Grubbins Wood is an ancient semi-natural woodland near Arnside, Cumbria, dominated by mature oaks. A path leads to the estuary shore. It forms part of the Arnside and Silverdale Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Name: Guisborough Forest
Description: Guisborough Forest is a popular woodland site managed by Forestry England, located on the edge of the North York Moors National Park. It provides trails for walking, cycling, and horse riding, along with a visitor centre and children's play areas for recreational activities.

Name: Gullivers Farm
Description: Gullivers Farm is a 90-acre organic and biodynamic working farm and social enterprise in West Moors, Dorset, managed by Sturts Community Trust. It provides support and opportunities to adults with varying support needs, alongside sustainable farming practices and a farm shop and cafe.

Name: Gun Moor & Gun Moor Meadow
Description: Gun Moor & Gun Moor Meadow protects blanket bog, wet heath, and acidic grassland in the Peak District uplands. It supports red grouse, curlew, hen harrier, and adder. Active management includes habitat restoration and invasive species control.

Name: Gunby Hall Estate
Description: Gunby Hall Estate near Spilsby, Lincolnshire, is a Victorian country house with gardens and parkland managed by the National Trust. It focuses on 'Wolds Edge Farming for Nature' to encourage wildlife and biodiversity across the landscape. Visitors can explore the house, formal gardens, and wider estate.

Name: Gunners Park and Shoebury Ranges
Description: Gunners Park and Shoebury Ranges is a coastal mosaic of grasslands, wetlands, scrub, and woodland in Essex. It is a vital green space for wildlife, bordering the Thames Estuary, and is important for breeding birds and overwintering wildfowl. The site includes a Local Nature Reserve and part of the Shoeburyness SSSI.

Name: Gunpowder Park
Description: Gunpowder Park, a Green Flag site in Lee Valley Regional Park, was transformed from a former testing ground. It offers 100 acres of meadows and woods, providing habitats for diverse wildlife. The park features trails for walking and cycling.

Name: Gunton Warren
Description: Gunton Warren is a coastal reserve in north Suffolk, featuring dune, shingle, and grassland habitats. It supports nesting birds like little terns and ringed plovers, rare plants, and various insects. The site is a key stopover for migrating birds.

Name: Gunwalloe & Church Cove
Description: Gunwalloe and Church Cove in Cornwall is a coastal site managed by the National Trust. It features sandy beaches, a historic church, and access to the South West Coast Path. The area is known for shipwrecks and natural beauty.

Name: Gutteridge Wood and Meadows
Description: Gutteridge Wood and Meadows, located in Hillingdon, West London, features diverse woodland, grassland, and wetland habitats. It supports varied wildlife including amphibians, insects, and birds. The site is managed for biodiversity and public access.

Name: Gwenffrwd-Dinas
Description: Ancient oak woodlands in the Tywi valley, Carmarthenshire, Wales. A Special Area of Conservation, home to pied flycatchers, redstarts, and wood warblers. Bluebells carpet the valley floor. Features rocky river stretches and waterfalls, managed by RSPB.

Name: Hackhurst and White Downs
Description: Hackhurst Downs is a 40-hectare nature reserve in Surrey, managed by Surrey Wildlife Trust. It is a high area of open chalk grassland on the North Downs, featuring diverse flora and fauna, including notable butterflies like adonis blue and chalk hill blue, and rare chalk grassland flowers. The site is designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest and a Local Nature Reserve, offering public access via footpaths and a section of the North Downs Way.

Name: Hackhurst Downs
Description: Hackhurst Downs is a chalk grassland nature reserve near Abinger Hammer, Surrey, managed by Surrey Wildlife Trust. It supports diverse flora including orchids and wildflowers, attracting various insects and butterflies. The site offers walking trails and panoramic views across the Surrey Hills.

Name: Hackpen Hill
Description: Hackpen Hill is a large, flower-rich chalk grassland site in the North Wessex Downs Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. It features a prominent Iron Age hill fort. The reserve supports diverse flora and fauna, including orchids and rare butterflies.

Name: Hadfields Quarry Nature Reserve
Description: Hadfields Quarry Nature Reserve, located in the beautiful Hope Valley, is a diverse site featuring species-rich grassland, small-scale wetland, woodland, and bare rock within and around a disused limestone quarry. It provides a habitat for a variety of wildlife, including palmate newts, glow worms, dingy skipper butterflies, and green tiger beetles. Notable plant species include mossy saxifrage, ploughman's spikenard, and cowslip. The reserve is managed by Derbyshire Wildlife Trust and requires a special permit for access due to the fragility of its habitats and potential rock fall hazards.

Name: Hadrian's Wall & Housesteads Fort
Description: Housesteads Roman Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site on Hadrian's Wall, offers visitors a unique blend of history and nature. Explore Britain's most complete Roman fort, including barracks, a hospital, granaries, and latrines, while discovering Roman soldier life. The fort is set within a dramatic natural landscape cared for by the National Trust, offering stunning views across the wall and opportunities to experience the surrounding natural wilderness and spot diverse wildlife, contributing to wider nature conservation efforts along Hadrian's Wall.

Name: Hadrian's Wall Wetlands Landscape Recovery Project
Description: Hadrian's Wall Wetlands is an 11,000-acre Landscape Recovery Project. It restores and enhances peatlands and wetlands across the Hadrian's Wall area in Northumberland, aiming to improve biodiversity, water quality, and carbon storage within the national park.

Name: Hagbourne Copse
Description: Hagbourne Copse, also known as Swindon Pocket Wood, is a small woodland in West Swindon, located within the Blagrove Industrial Estate. Managed by Wiltshire Wildlife Trust, it features diverse trees like oak, ash, and hazel, and is known for its stunning display of native bluebells in spring. It supports various bird species and invertebrates, providing a valuable green space and a peaceful place for walks. It is designated as a County Wildlife Site.

Name: Hagg Lane Idle Washlands
Description: Hagg Lane Idle Washlands is a 45-hectare nature reserve acquired in 2021, situated alongside the River Idle north of Retford. It forms part of the Idle Valley's nationally important network of floodplain wetlands, including an SSSI and SPA. The site is a nationally important breeding ground for waders and wintering wildfowl. No public access is currently permitted.

Name: Hainault Forest
Description: Hainault Forest spans 335 acres in northeast London, featuring ancient woodland, grasslands, a lake, and a zoo. Visitors can explore various walking trails, engage with wildlife, and enjoy open spaces for recreation. The site is a significant green lung.

Name: Halbullock Moor
Description: Halbullock Moor is a nature reserve near Scorrier in Cornwall. It features a mosaic of wet and dry heathland, bog, and grassland habitats. It supports diverse flora and fauna, including rare plant species and various invertebrates. The site offers important conservation value for lowland heath.

Name: Haldon Forest Park
Description: Haldon Forest Park, near Exeter, provides varied outdoor activities including walking, running, and cycling trails for all abilities. It features scenic views and diverse woodlands managed for recreation and conservation. The site offers a Discovery Trail and challenging mountain bike routes.

Name: Halesworth Millennium Green
Description: Halesworth Millennium Green is a 55-acre nature reserve on the River Blyth flood plain in Suffolk, offering diverse habitats from meadows to woodlands. The site provides walking trails and focuses on conservation, with ongoing river restoration work, and is managed by the Halesworth Millennium Green CIO.

Name: Halwill Junction
Description: Halwill Junction is a former railway junction now featuring woodland, wetlands and grassland, providing diverse habitats. The reserve is known for its dragonflies, damselflies and rare marsh fritillary butterflies. Walking trails offer visitor access.

Name: Ham Hill
Description: Ham Hill is a chalk downland site on a steep scarp slope overlooking the Vale of Pewsey. Its chalk grassland, rich in wildflowers like orchids and bellflowers, supports diverse insects including chalkhill and adonis blue butterflies. Yellowhammer and corn bunting are present.

Name: Ham House and Garden
Description: Ham House is a 17th-century house by the River Thames in Richmond, London. Its formal gardens feature an orangery, kitchen garden, and ancient trees. Re-created 17th-century wilderness areas and wildflower meadows also exist within the estate.

Name: Ham Street Woods
Description: Ham Street Woods is a 97-hectare ancient woodland National Nature Reserve (NNR) and Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) near Hamstreet, Ashford, Kent. It is a remnant of the extensive oak forests that once covered the Weald, featuring diverse habitats including oak and hornbeam stands, supporting varied flora and fauna. The reserve is actively managed by Natural England for conservation, scientific research, education, and public access, offering waymarked trails.

Name: Ham Wall
Description: Ham Wall is a Somerset wetland nature reserve managed by the RSPB. It features extensive reedbeds, open water, and wet woodland, providing habitat for diverse wildlife including bitterns, marsh harriers, and otters. Visitors can explore a network of trails and viewing hides.

Name: Hambleton Wood
Description: Hambleton Wood is an ancient woodland located on the Hambleton Peninsula within Rutland Water. Managed by the Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust, it features diverse tree species and supports various wildlife, including deer, birds, and insects. Visitors can explore marked trails within this significant natural habitat.

Name: Hamford Water National Nature Reserve
Description: Hamford Water is an internationally important wetland, encompassing creeks, saltmarsh, and mudflats. It supports significant populations of overwintering and breeding birds, including avocets and dark-bellied brent geese. This estuarine site is also home to seals and diverse marine life.

Name: Hammond's Field
Description: Hammond's Field is a gently sloping unimproved grassland, forming part of the South Pennine Moors Special Protected Area (SPA) around the moorland fringes of Sheffield. It supports a diverse range of wildflowers, including common spotted orchid and yellow rattle, within its semi-improved wet pasture and traditional drystone walls. The site offers a vital green space for wildlife.

Name: Hampstead Heath
Description: Hampstead Heath is a large, ancient parkland in north London, offering diverse habitats, natural swimming ponds, and panoramic city views. It features extensive woodlands, meadows, and sports facilities, managed for public access and conservation.

Name: Hampton Meadow
Description: Hampton Meadow is a traditional hay meadow on the River Lugg flood plain in Herefordshire. It hosts plants such as great burnet and ragged robin. Insect life includes orange-tip butterflies, while reed bunting and kingfisher are present. Herefordshire Wildlife Trust manages the site.

Name: Hampton Wood & Meadow
Description: Hampton Wood & Meadow combines ancient woodland and wildflower-rich grassland in Warwickshire. The reserve is famed for its primroses, bluebells, wood anemone, and lesser celandine in spring. It supports a diverse range of wildlife including dormice, 28 butterfly species (like white-letter and purple hairstreaks, white admiral, and holly blue), over 200 species of fungi, and over 500 species of beetles. Birds such as woodcock and various warblers are present, and kingfishers are seen along the River Avon. The flood meadow hosts wetland plants and breeding toads. The reserve is managed through coppicing and grazing to enhance biodiversity, and public footpaths offer access.

Name: Hamsterley Forest
Description: Hamsterley Forest covers 2,000 hectares, making it County Durham's largest woodland. It features diverse walking, cycling, and horse riding trails, alongside play areas and a cafe. The forest offers year-round opportunities for wildlife observation and outdoor activities.

Name: Hanbury Hall
Description: Hanbury Hall is a William and Mary style country house in Worcestershire, cared for by the National Trust. It features a formal Baroque garden, extensive parkland, and an orchard, reflecting 18th-century design and rural life.

Name: Handa Island
Description: Handa Island, off Sutherland, is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and Special Protection Area. It hosts globally important seabird colonies including razorbills, guillemots, and kittiwakes. The Scottish Wildlife Trust manages the island.

Name: Hannah's Meadow
Description: Hannah’s Meadow is a rare upland hay meadow, home to a variety of wildflowers and grasses. Located in the North Pennines, the site is managed by Durham Wildlife Trust to preserve its biodiversity and traditional farming methods. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI).

Name: Hanningfield Reservoir
Description: Hanningfield Reservoir is a large Essex Wildlife Trust site in Essex. It features a vast expanse of water, ancient woodland, and farmland. The site offers footpaths, bird hides, a visitor centre, and education facilities, supporting diverse wildlife.

Name: Hardcastle Crags
Description: Hardcastle Crags features ancient woodlands and a rare temperate rainforest. The 19th-century Gibson Mill is water-powered. Miles of footpaths wind through steep valleys, home to diverse wildlife and over 100 species of mosses and liverworts.

Name: Harden Quarry
Description: Harden Quarry is an active hard rock quarry within Northumberland National Park, known for significant Bronze Age archaeological discoveries including a settlement and burial sites. Located in the Cheviot Hills, it is also a site where nature recovery efforts are underway, involving local partners and volunteers for conservation tasks.

Name: Hardington Moor
Description: Hardington Moor is a nature reserve near Hardington Mandeville, Somerset. It is managed by Somerset Wildlife Trust. The site comprises wildflower meadows and ancient hedgerows, supporting diverse insect life, including marbled white butterflies. It features accessible footpaths.

Name: Hardwick Dene & Elm Tree Wood
Description: Hardwick Dene and Elm Tree Wood is a local nature reserve in Stockton-on-Tees, featuring ancient woodland, grassland, and the flowing Elm Tree Beck. The site supports diverse wildlife, including various bird species and invertebrates, offering a natural habitat within an urban setting.

Name: Hardwick Hall
Description: Hardwick Hall, a National Trust property, is undergoing significant restoration within the Doe Lea River Valley. Work focuses on improving river health, water quality, and biodiversity. Efforts aim to restore natural river flow and create new habitats for a diverse range of wildlife.

Name: Hardwick Wood
Description: Hardwick Wood is a 15.5-hectare ancient medieval woodland and a biological Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Cambridgeshire. Managed by the Wildlife Trust for Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Northamptonshire (Wildlife Trust BCN), it features mature oak, ash, and field maple, with traditional coppicing practices. The reserve supports diverse flora, including bluebells, early-purple orchid, yellow archangel, cowslips, and the rare crested cow-wheat. It is also home to various woodland birds like willow warblers, marsh tits, blackcaps, and tawny owls, with bats patrolling its edges. Visitors can explore the site via established public footpaths.

Name: Hare Hill
Description: Hare Hill is a tranquil wooded garden and parkland managed by the National Trust, located near Macclesfield in Cheshire. It features a delightful walled garden, renowned rhododendrons, azaleas, and diverse plant collections. Visitors can explore various paths, serene ponds, and a natural play area for families.

Name: Haresfield Beacon & Standish Wood
Description: Haresfield Beacon and Standish Wood offers expansive views across the Severn Vale towards the Brecon Beacons. This Cotswold escarpment features ancient woodland, limestone grassland, and Iron Age hillfort remnants. It provides habitats for diverse wildlife, including wildflowers and butterflies.

Name: Harland Mount
Description: Harland Mount is a nature reserve in Scarborough, managed by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust. Set on a steep hill, it features rough acid pasture and scrub woodland, offering beautiful views across the town and over the sea. The reserve supports local wildlife with a mix of native trees, wildflowers like bluebell and primrose, and has potential for dew-pond restoration.

Name: Harridge Woods
Description: Harridge Woods is a diverse ancient woodland site near Frome in Somerset, managed by Somerset Wildlife Trust. It features oak, ash, and hazel trees with rich ground flora including bluebells and wild garlic. The site supports various bird species and dormice.

Name: Hartington Meadows
Description: Hartington Meadows is a flower-rich hay meadow in the Upper Dove Valley, Derbyshire. It supports a diverse range of wildflowers, including globeflower and great burnet, providing vital habitat for insects and birds. The site is managed to enhance its biodiversity.

Name: Hartlepool Submerged Forest
Description: The Hartlepool Submerged Forest is a rare geological site on the Co Durham coastline. Dating back 7000 years, this ancient forest becomes visible only during very low tides. It offers a unique glimpse into prehistoric landscapes.

Name: Hartslock
Description: Hartslock is a steep chalk grassland slope overlooking the River Thames near Goring. It is home to a significant population of monkey orchids and a rare hybrid orchid swarm. The reserve also supports rare juniper and features ancient woodland, managed for biodiversity.

Name: Harwood Forest
Description: Harwood Forest, north of Rothbury, is a vast expanse of commercial conifers and ancient woodland. It offers numerous walking and cycling trails, providing scenic views across the Northumberland countryside.

Name: Haskayne Cutting
Description: Haskayne Cutting is a linear wildlife site near the Leeds and Liverpool Canal in Lancashire. It features reed-fringed ponds, wet meadows, and scrub, known for rare dragonflies like the black darter. It is part of a former railway line and managed by the Lancashire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Hat Gate
Description: Hat Gate is a 1-hectare nature reserve near Marlborough, Wiltshire, forming part of a dismantled railway corridor. It features diverse habitats including damp grassland, scrub, and woodland. The site supports various insects, wildflowers, and bird species, contributing to local biodiversity.

Name: Hatchmere
Description: Hatchmere is a significant nature reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) within Delamere Forest, forming part of the Northwest Midlands Meres and Mosses Ramsar site. It hosts the Cheshire Beaver Project, a five-year reintroduction trial launched in 2020, where beavers enhance the site's rich wetland habitats, boosting biodiversity and improving water quality.

Name: Hatfield Forest
Description: Hatfield Forest is a unique example of a nearly complete medieval hunting forest. Managed in partnership by Essex Wildlife Trust and the National Trust, it features ancient trees, open glades, and a large lake, providing diverse habitats for wildlife. Visitors can explore woodlands and grasslands.

Name: Hatfield Forest
Description: Hatfield Forest, a National Nature Reserve in Essex, is England's only remaining intact Royal hunting forest. It features ancient trees, woodlands, grasslands, and a lake, demonstrating a landscape shaped by centuries of traditional forest management.

Name: Hatfield Moors
Description: Hatfield Moors is a large nature reserve in South Yorkshire, part of the Humberhead Peatlands National Nature Reserve, featuring extensive blanket bog and wet heath. It supports species like red grouse, golden plover, and curlew. The site is crucial for carbon storage and water quality.

Name: Hatton Meadows
Description: Hatton Meadows is a species-rich grassland in Lincolnshire, featuring traditional ridge and furrow patterns. It supports diverse wildflowers, including common spotted-orchid and meadow saffron. Butterflies like gatekeeper and small skipper are present. The Trust manages the site to maintain biodiversity and prevent scrub encroachment.

Name: Haughmond Hill
Description: Haughmond Hill offers views over Shrewsbury, the Shropshire Hills, and the Cheshire Plain. It features waymarked trails for walking and cycling through mixed woodland. Visitors can find picnic areas, a cafe, and a play area. The site is managed by Forestry England.

Name: Hauxley Wildlife Discovery Centre
Description: Hauxley Wildlife Discovery Centre, managed by Northumberland Wildlife Trust, is a flagship nature reserve located at the northern end of Druridge Bay. Originally an open-cast mine, it was transformed into a wildlife haven in 1983. Renowned as one of the best wildlife-watching spots in the North East, it features diverse habitats including ponds, meadows, and reedbeds, supporting a wide variety of bird species (over 140 annually), red squirrels, otters, insects, and mammals. The eco-friendly straw-bale visitor centre offers panoramic views, and the reserve provides hides and accessible trails for observation.

Name: Hawkchurch Common
Description: Hawkchurch Common is a nature reserve near Axminster, East Devon. It features wet heathland, damp grassland, and ancient broadleaved woodland. The site supports diverse flora, including purple moor-grass, and birds like Dartford warblers. Ponies graze to maintain its habitats.

Name: Hawkes Wood
Description: Hawkes Wood is a diverse woodland reserve nestled along the banks of the River Camel, near Wadebridge. Ancient oak, ash, and hazel trees provide habitat for Dormice, woodpeckers, and buzzards. The river attracts kingfishers and otters. Paths allow exploration.

Name: Hawthorn Dene
Description: Hawthorn Dene is an ancient woodland and coastal dene near Seaham, County Durham, featuring a magnesian limestone gorge, cliffs, and a beach. It supports diverse flora and fauna, including rare plants and woodland birds. Part of the Durham Heritage Coast, it provides walking trails.

Name: Haxey Turbary
Description: Haxey Turbary is a small, wet grassland and fen site in the Humberhead Levels. This SSSI is a rare remnant of the Isle of Axholme's original lowland peatlands. It supports species-rich grassland, ditches, and ponds.

Name: Haydon Hill
Description: Haydon Hill is a 27-hectare nature reserve in Dorset, featuring ancient woodland, grassland, and scrub. Managed for its diverse habitats, it supports a range of wildflowers, insects, and bird species. Visitors can explore marked trails.

Name: Hayley Wood
Description: Hayley Wood is an ancient woodland, traditionally managed on a 12-year coppice rotation. It boasts significant wildlife, particularly notable for its rich array of wildflowers like oxlip and a diverse population of butterflies and moths.

Name: Haysden Country Park
Description: Haysden Country Park, near Tonbridge, is a Local Nature Reserve. It features varied habitats, including lakes, a river, and woodlands. The park supports diverse wildlife and offers recreational activities such as walking and watersports. It is popular for its natural beauty and accessible paths.

Name: Headley Gravel Pit
Description: Headley Gravel Pit, a former quarry, is now a thriving seven-hectare nature reserve managed by the Hampshire & Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust. It features a mosaic of woodland, grassland, open water, reedbeds, and willow scrub. This diverse habitat supports a rich array of wildlife, including a population of black adders, thousands of green-winged orchids in late spring, and various invertebrates and birdlife. Footpaths allow visitors to observe the rich wildlife.

Name: Headley Heath
Description: Headley Heath is a rare heathland and woodland site in the Surrey Hills National Landscape, South East England. This Site of Special Scientific Interest supports diverse habitats, including rare birds and reptiles. It is popular with walkers, cyclists, and horse riders.

Name: Headstone Manor Park
Description: Headstone Manor Park in Harrow, London, features a river restoration project that daylighted 150m of the Yeading Brook. A new meandering channel replaces a culvert, improving water quality, habitats, and reducing flood risk, enhancing the park's environment.

Name: Heartwood Forest
Description: Heartwood Forest near St Albans, Hertfordshire, is England's largest new native forest, spanning 858 acres. Managed by the Woodland Trust, it features extensive woodlands, meadows, and orchards, offering walking trails and diverse wildlife habitats.

Name: Heather Underhill
Description: Heather Underhill is a 13-hectare woodland, part of the National Forest in Leicestershire. It features diverse native broadleaf and conifer trees, offering wildlife habitat. The site provides public access for walking and connects to a wider path network. It is actively managed.

Name: Heaton Park
Description: Heaton Park is a municipal park in north Manchester, England, covering over 600 acres. The largest park in Greater Manchester, it features woodlands, grasslands, and wetlands. Biodiversity recovery areas are actively managed to enhance ecological value for diverse wildlife.

Name: Heber's Ghyll
Description: Heber's Ghyll is a beautiful woodland area and stream with waterfalls located near Ilkley, West Yorkshire. It offers scenic walks through ancient woodland and is managed by Bradford District Parks, providing a tranquil spot for nature observation.

Name: Hedgecourt
Description: Hedgecourt Lake, a Surrey SSSI, is a key wetland. It features a shallow lake, fen, swamp, and wet woodland, supporting diverse wildlife. Notable species include greater tussock-sedge, royal fern, various dragonflies, and the scarce hazel dormouse.

Name: Hedley Stringer Wood
Description: Hedley Stringer Wood is a young woodland near the village of Wilsden, Bradford, planted in 2000. It offers open vistas, a small stream, and a network of paths suitable for dog walking and family visits. The site enhances local biodiversity and provides green space.

Name: Hedleyhope Fell
Description: Hedleyhope Fell is a 202-hectare nature reserve in County Durham, managed by Durham Wildlife Trust. It features wet and dry heath, mire, and acid grassland habitats. The site supports breeding birds such as snipe and curlew, along with diverse invertebrates. Conservation work focuses on habitat restoration.

Name: Heigham Holmes
Description: Heigham Holmes is a secluded island in the Norfolk Broads, only accessible by boat on the River Thurne. It serves as a vital wildlife haven, home to otters and the rare fen raft spider. Visits are by pre-booked boat trip only.

Name: Helford River Seagrass Regeneration
Description: The Helford Seagrass Project regenerates seagrass meadows in Cornwall's Helford River. Pioneering methods involve volunteers collecting 10,000 seeds from healthy beds, planting them in biodegradable bags, and deploying them in the river. This vital project supports marine biodiversity and carbon capture, with growth ongoing.

Name: Hell Hole Ancient Woodland
Description: Hampton Wood and Meadow is an ancient woodland and meadow in Warwickshire, managed by Warwickshire Wildlife Trust. It is known for its beautiful spring display of primroses, bluebells, wood anemone, and lesser celandine. Mature oak and ash trees dominate the canopy, supporting a diverse range of woodland birds and over 500 species of insects and 28 butterfly species. Managed for conservation, it offers quiet walking paths.

Name: Hellenge Hill
Description: Hellenge Hill is an unimproved ancient grassland, designated a Site of Nature Conservation Interest (SNCI). This reserve supports diverse wildflowers, including several orchid species and rare plants like honewort and Somerset hair-grass, and attracts various butterflies. It offers panoramic views across the Somerset Levels and the Bristol Channel.

Name: Helman Tor Nature Reserve (Creney Farm Expansion)
Description: Cornwall Wildlife Trust has acquired Creney Farm, expanding the Helman Tor reserve. This project aims to create a significant rewilded landscape in central Cornwall. It restores natural processes, enhances biodiversity, and provides habitat connectivity for wildlife.

Name: Hem Heath Woods
Description: Hem Heath Woods is a 54-hectare mixed woodland on Stoke-on-Trent's southern fringe. It features mature oak and birch with a diverse understorey, supporting nuthatches and woodpeckers. The site, an ancient woodland, is currently undergoing an urban oasis restoration project.

Name: Hemsted Forest
Description: Hemsted Forest is a working woodland near Benenden, Kent, offering walking, cycling, and horse riding trails. It features mature conifer and broadleaf trees, and is managed by Forestry England. The site provides a natural habitat for various wildlife.

Name: Hendover Coppice
Description: Hendover Coppice is an ancient woodland site with a rich history of coppicing, now undergoing restoration. It features diverse tree species, wildflowers, and a variety of wildlife. The reserve offers walking trails through managed woodland habitats.

Name: Henllys Urban Woodland
Description: Henllys Bog is a small but significant valley mire and wetland nature reserve near Cwmbran, Torfaen, managed by Gwent Wildlife Trust. Recognised as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), it features rare and interesting plants, including orchids and broad-leaved cottongrass, within a secluded setting encircled by alder and beech trees. It supports diverse wildlife, including butterflies, crickets, grasshoppers, and dragonflies.

Name: Herrington Hill
Description: Herrington Hill, a grassland SSSI in Tyne and Wear, features magnesian limestone supporting diverse flora including blue moor-grass and orchids. It provides habitat for invertebrates and small mammals, actively managed for biodiversity.

Name: Hertford Heath
Description: Hertford Heath, a nature reserve near Hertford, Hertfordshire, encompasses ancient woodland, acid grassland, and ponds. It supports a range of wildlife, including reptiles and diverse insect species. Hertfordshire and Middlesex Wildlife Trust manages the site.

Name: Hertford Heath
Description: Hertford Heath is a nature reserve in Hertfordshire, featuring rare acid heathland and mature broadleaved woodland. It supports silver birch, oak, Scots pine, heather, and gorse. The site provides habitat for nightjars, woodlarks, and reptiles like adders.

Name: Hesleden Dene
Description: Hesleden Dene is a Local Wildlife Site in County Durham, managed by Durham Wildlife Trust. This characteristic coastal dene features ancient oak, ash, and abundant hazel stands. The reserve boasts exceptional natural exposures of magnesian limestone, forming impressive outcrops with caves and fissures. These damp, humid conditions support diverse mosses, lichens, and fungi. Magnesian limestone grassland hosts plants like devil's-bit scabious, common spotted orchid, and twayblade. Woodland wildlife, including roe deer, fox, woodpeckers, and tawny owls, thrives here. Public access paths are available, and the reserve is best visited in spring for woodland flora and autumn for fungi and turning leaves.

Name: Hetchell Wood
Description: Hetchell Wood is a mosaic of ancient woodland, grassland, and exposed rock outcrops. This Yorkshire Wildlife Trust nature reserve provides diverse habitats for flora and fauna. Notable features include rare plants and geological formations, with public access via a network of footpaths.

Name: Hethel Old Thorn
Description: Hethel Old Thorn nature reserve protects a truly ancient hawthorn tree, estimated to date back to the 13th century, making it potentially 700 years old. This unique site is one of the smallest nature reserves in the UK, primarily focused on the venerable tree, which provides habitat for diverse insect and bird life within its grassland and scrub surroundings.

Name: Hewitts Chalk Bank
Description: Hewitts Chalk Bank is a small chalk grassland nature reserve located on the North Downs in Kent. Managed by Kent Wildlife Trust, it supports a diverse range of wildflowers and butterflies. The site was acquired in 1968, preserving a valuable habitat.

Name: Hexhamshire Common
Description: Hexhamshire Common, part of the Northumberland uplands, is a significant peatland area within the Great North Bog initiative. This landscape-scale restoration project aims for environmental recovery across Northern England.

Name: Hexton Chalk Pit
Description: Hexton Chalk Pit is a 1.9-hectare former chalk quarry, now a Site of Special Scientific Interest in north Hertfordshire, managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust. The reserve features chalk grassland with steep slopes and mature woodland, supporting diverse flora and fauna, including five species of orchid, chalk-loving plants like horseshoe vetch, yellow-wort, milkwort, and rockrose, as well as a large colony of chalkhill blue butterflies and various bird species. The site offers extensive views over the surrounding countryside.

Name: Heyford Meadow
Description: Heyford Meadow is a species-rich floodplain meadow by the River Thames, Oxfordshire. It features colourful wildflowers such as the nationally scarce snake's head fritillary, supporting diverse insects, birds, and other wildlife.

Name: Heysham Coast
Description: Heysham Coast offers varied coastal habitats including saltmarsh, sand dunes, and grassland, important for diverse birdlife. Visitors can explore historic St Patrick's Chapel ruins and enjoy scenic views across Morecambe Bay, a significant natural environment.

Name: Heysham Moss
Description: Heysham Moss is a lowland raised bog and SSSI. It supports diverse flora, including sphagnum mosses, cotton grass, and heather. The site provides a habitat for various invertebrates, dragonflies, and birds like snipe, and is actively managed.

Name: Heysham Nature Reserve
Description: Heysham Nature Reserve is a wildlife haven built on the site of a former power station. Habitats include reedbed, open water, and woodland, supporting birds and insects. Visitors use accessible paths and hides.

Name: Hickling Broad and Marshes
Description: Hickling Broad is the largest expanse of open water in the Broads National Park. It is a vital haven for rare wildlife, including common crane and swallowtail butterflies. The reserve features reedbeds, marshes, and open water habitats.

Name: Hickling Broad and Marshes National Nature Reserve
Description: Hickling Broad and Marshes is the largest of the Norfolk Broads and a National Nature Reserve, managed by Norfolk Wildlife Trust. It is a nationally important wetland ecosystem, renowned for its diverse wildlife, including swallowtail butterflies, bitterns, and cranes. The reserve offers extensive walking trails, a visitor centre, and guided wildlife boat trips.

Name: High Clear Down
Description: High Clear Down is a steep chalk downland in Wiltshire, home to ancient earthworks and a Neolithic long barrow. This Site of Special Scientific Interest is grazed by cattle to maintain diverse chalk grassland, supporting wildflowers and butterflies.

Name: High Close Estate and Arboretum
Description: High Close Estate and Arboretum, near Loughrigg Fell, Lake District, features historic gardens with mature trees, rhododendrons, and azaleas. It offers views across Langdale Valley and includes diverse plant collections and walking paths for visitors.

Name: High Elms Country Park
Description: High Elms Country Park, near Orpington, features ancient woodlands, wildflower meadows, and chalk grassland. It supports diverse wildlife. Managed by London Borough of Bromley, Kent Wildlife Trust also manages a part.

Name: High Halks
Description: High Halks is a Kent Wildlife Trust nature reserve in Kent, featuring a mosaic of woodland, grassland, and ponds. Acquired in 1993, the site supports diverse wildlife, including dragonflies and various bird species, across its planted broadleaf woodland and wet grassland habitats.

Name: High Leys Farm
Description: High Leys Farm is a nature reserve in Cumbria, featuring traditionally managed upland hay meadows rich in wildflowers and diverse grasses. These habitats support various invertebrates and ground-nesting birds, playing a role in local biodiversity conservation.

Name: High Wood
Description: High Wood is part of Staveley Woodlands Nature Reserve, an ancient woodland managed by Cumbria Wildlife Trust in the Lake District. It features mature trees, diverse ground flora like bluebells and wild garlic, and supports a variety of woodland birds. Public footpaths provide access for visitors to explore its natural beauty.

Name: High Wood and Meadow
Description: High Wood and Meadow is an enchanting ancient woodland and species-rich meadow located in Northamptonshire, managed by The Wildlife Trust for Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Northamptonshire. The ancient woodland, traditionally coppiced, supports a rich ground flora including bluebells and wild cherry trees. The species-rich acidic grassland meadow provides habitat for various wildflowers, butterflies like marbled white and speckled wood, and features numerous yellow meadow ant hills.

Name: High Woods Country Park
Description: High Woods Country Park, a Green Flag award winner in Colchester, features woodland, grassland, lake, and marsh habitats. Owned by Colchester City Council, it provides crucial space for local wildlife and community recreation. Essex Wildlife Trust manages adjacent areas.

Name: Higham Ferrers Riverside
Description: Higham Ferrers Riverside is a flood plain meadow and riverbank site along the River Nene. Managed by Wildlife BCN, it supports wildflowers and grasses, providing habitat for insects and birds. Public footpaths offer access for nature observation.

Name: Higher Kiln Quarry
Description: Higher Kiln Quarry, near Buckfastleigh, is a disused limestone quarry and nature reserve in South Devon. It is a nationally important bat roost, primarily for Greater Horseshoe bats. The site features flower-rich limestone grassland, supporting diverse butterflies.

Name: Higher Moors
Description: Higher Moors and Porth Hellick Pool form the largest wetland on St Mary's, Isles of Scilly, featuring reedbed, marsh, and open water habitats. This reserve supports resident and migratory birds, dragonflies, and rare plants, and is managed for biodiversity by the Isles of Scilly Wildlife Trust.

Name: Highgate Common
Description: Highgate Common is a nationally important lowland heathland in South Staffordshire, managed by Staffordshire Wildlife Trust. The site features diverse habitats including acid grassland, woodland, and ponds, supporting adders, slow worms, and many invertebrates.

Name: Highgate Wood
Description: Highgate Wood is a 28-hectare ancient woodland in north London, managed as a public open space. It features mature trees, diverse wildlife, and facilities including a playground, cafe, and sports pitches. The site is popular for recreation and nature observation.

Name: Hill Court Farm
Description: Hill Court Farm and The Blacklands, near Longdon and Upton upon Severn in Worcestershire, is a 120-hectare site undergoing significant wetland habitat restoration. Formerly an intensive dairy and arable farm, it now supports diverse wildlife, including curlews, lapwings, and otters, through a mosaic of ponds, wetlands, and woodlands.

Name: Hill Hook Local Nature Reserve
Description: Hill Hook Local Nature Reserve in Sutton Coldfield is a former Victorian pleasure ground, now managed by Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust in partnership with Birmingham City Council and the Friends of Hill Hook LNR. It features diverse habitats including grassland, woodland, and a historic mill pool, supporting a wide variety of local wildlife.

Name: Hill of White Hamars
Description: Hill of White Hamars is a varied nature reserve featuring lowland heath, scrub, grassland, and woodland. It provides habitats for juniper, various heathers, and a diverse range of birds and invertebrates. The site supports significant biodiversity within its landscape.

Name: Hilton Gravel Pits
Description: Hilton Gravel Pits is a 29-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) nature reserve in Derbyshire, managed by Derbyshire Wildlife Trust. Formerly an aggregate quarry, it features a diverse mosaic of habitats including open water, reedbeds, grassland, and woodland. It is a haven for wildlife, particularly known for its 15 species of dragonflies, great crested newts, black poplar, bats, and various waterfowl such as coot, great crested grebe, and tufted duck. The reserve offers numerous trails for exploration, with parking available on Willowpit Lane.

Name: Hindhead Commons and the Devil's Punch Bowl
Description: Hindhead Commons and the Devil's Punch Bowl is a large area of heathland and woodland in Surrey, managed by the National Trust. It offers dramatic views, walking trails, and significant natural heritage. This site is known for its diverse wildlife and ongoing conservation.

Name: Hinksey Heights
Description: Hinksey Heights is a diverse nature reserve in Oxford, featuring a nationally rare alkaline fen, reedbeds, wet woodlands, and grasslands. It provides vital habitats for rare plants, butterflies, and birds, including species like Marsh Helleborine and the Dark-winged Soldier fly. Ongoing restoration efforts are focused on enhancing its significant biodiversity. Visitors enjoy extensive views across the city.

Name: Hobbyhorse Wood
Description: Hobbyhorse Wood is an ancient woodland nature reserve near Ware, Hertfordshire, managed by Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust. It features diverse tree species and a rich ground flora, with notable bluebell displays in spring. The site supports various bird species.

Name: Hockenhull Platts
Description: Hockenhull Platts is a nature reserve in Cheshire, renowned for its medieval packhorse bridge and rich biodiversity. The site features various habitats, including woodlands, meadows, and the River Gowy, supporting diverse flora and fauna. It provides public access for nature observation and walks.

Name: Hockley Meadows
Description: Hockley Meadows is a diverse wildlife haven along the River Itchen in Hampshire. It features wet grassland, reedbed, scrub, and woodland. Otters and water voles frequent the river. Managed for wildlife, it offers a mosaic of habitats.

Name: Hoe Grange Quarry
Description: Hoe Grange Quarry is a Derbyshire Wildlife Trust nature reserve near Longcliffe. This disused limestone quarry, owned by Longcliffe Quarries, features species-rich grassland, supporting diverse wildflowers and insects. The site is particularly noted for its significant butterfly populations, with 24-29 species recorded. Please note: The site is currently closed to visitors due to unstable rockfaces/rockfall.

Name: Hoe Road Meadow
Description: Hoe Road Meadow is a species-rich SSSI in Bishop's Waltham. The meadow supports grassland fungi and wildflowers, maintained by traditional hay-cutting and grazing. Diverse habitats support various insects and birds.

Name: Hoe Rough and Beetley Meadows
Description: Hoe Rough and Beetley Meadows form a nature reserve in Norfolk, featuring a mosaic of woodland, grassland, heathland, and fen. Part of a SSSI along the River Wensum, it supports diverse invertebrates, rare plants like marsh orchids, and offers public footpaths.

Name: Hog's Back
Description: The Hog's Back nature reserve stretches across the North Downs, between Guildford and Seale. It features ancient woodland, grassland, and scrub, supporting diverse wildlife. The site is managed for biodiversity, offering walking trails and scenic views.

Name: Holborough Marshes
Description: Holborough Marshes is a Kent Wildlife Trust nature reserve located on the River Medway. It features diverse habitats including reedbeds, ditches, and wet grassland, supporting wildlife such as water voles, otters, kingfishers, and various dragonfly species.

Name: Holburn Moss
Description: Holburn Moss is a raised mire and internationally designated wetland (Ramsar site and SSSI) located west of Lowick in Northumberland. Managed by the Northumberland Wildlife Trust, it supports diverse bog plants such as sphagnum mosses, cotton-grass, heather, cranberry, and round-leaved sundew. The reserve provides crucial habitat for various bird species, particularly as a wintering wildfowl roost, and is linked to the nearby Lindisfarne National Nature Reserve. It showcases a unique peatland ecosystem.

Name: Holcroft Moss
Description: Holcroft Moss is a Cheshire Wildlife Trust nature reserve, a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), Special Area of Conservation (SAC), and a Ramsar site of international importance. This 18-hectare lowland raised bog is the only known area in Cheshire that has never been cut for peat, making it a rare and crucial habitat. It supports diverse Sphagnum mosses, common cotton-grass, cross-leaved heath, and cranberries, along with species like round-leaved sundew. The reserve is also home to various invertebrates, including dragonflies and damselflies, and provides habitat for bog bush crickets, common lizards, snipe, and woodcock. The functioning peat bog plays a vital role in capturing and storing carbon dioxide.

Name: Holiday's Hill
Description: Holiday's Hill is a small nature reserve near Lyme Regis, featuring ancient woodland, neutral grassland, and unimproved acid grassland. It supports a variety of flora and fauna, including rare plant species and diverse invertebrates.

Name: Holland Haven
Description: Holland Haven is a coastal nature reserve in Essex, featuring saltmarsh, reedbeds, and grasslands. It provides essential habitats for a variety of birds, including bearded tits and marsh harriers, alongside diverse insect populations. The site offers accessible walking routes and birdwatching opportunities.

Name: Hollinhurst Wood
Description: Hollinhurst Wood is a semi-ancient woodland with an oak, ash, and hazel canopy. Bluebells carpet the ground in spring. Located near Barnsley, it supports diverse bird species and wildflowers. The site features a meandering stream and is accessible via public footpaths.

Name: Holly Hill
Description: Holly Hill is a public open space managed by Tonbridge and Malling Borough Council, located on the North Downs between Vigo and Snodland, near Meopham. It features ancient woodland with coppiced hazel, mature oak, and sweet chestnut trees. The site supports diverse wildlife, including various bird species and invertebrates, providing a habitat for woodland flora.

Name: Holme Dunes
Description: Holme Dunes National Nature Reserve is a dynamic coastal landscape in Norfolk, featuring sand dunes, saltmarsh, and pine woodlands. It serves as a crucial stop-over for migratory birds and supports a colony of natterjack toads. Public access includes bird hides and walking trails.

Name: Holme Dunes NWT Reserve
Description: Holme Dunes NWT Reserve spans 124 hectares of dunes, saltmarsh, woodland, and beach in Norfolk. It is an internationally important bird migration watch-point, supporting natterjack toads and diverse flora. A visitor centre is present.

Name: Holme Fen
Description: Holme Fen is Great Britain's lowest point and Cambridgeshire's largest original fenland. It features a Silver Birch woodland and diverse fen habitats, including reedbeds and open water. The reserve supports rare invertebrates and birds.

Name: Holme Fen National Nature Reserve
Description: Holme Fen is a National Nature Reserve in Cambridgeshire and a key part of the Great Fen project. It holds the lowest point in Britain and features diverse habitats including silver birch woodland and fenland. Distinctive 'bog oaks' are present.

Name: Holmsley Gravel Pit
Description: Holmsley Gravel Pit is a former quarry in the New Forest. It features ponds, wet and dry heathland, acid grassland, and woodland, supporting diverse wildlife including dragonflies, damselflies, birds, and reptiles.

Name: Holt Fish Pass
Description: Holt Lock & Weir is the highest point fish can reach on the River Severn. The fish pass, part of the Unlocking the Severn project, helps species like the Twaite Shad bypass the weir. The site includes an observation window for visitors to view migrating fish. Parking is available nearby.

Name: Holt Lowes
Description: Holt Lowes is a diverse heathland, grassland, and woodland site in Norfolk. It supports a range of wildlife, including nightjars, woodlarks, and adders. The site features various habitats, providing important biodiversity.

Name: Holway Woods
Description: Holway Woods is an ancient woodland managed by Dorset Wildlife Trust, featuring a mix of mature and recently planted trees including oak, ash, hazel, field maple, and sweet chestnuts. In spring, the woodland floor is carpeted with wildflowers such as bluebells, primroses, and pink purslane. The reserve supports diverse wildlife, including various bird species like tawny owls, song thrushes, and great spotted woodpeckers, as well as mammals like roe deer, badgers, and bats. Public footpaths offer visitors access and superb views over the surrounding countryside towards south Somerset and Glastonbury Tor.

Name: Holwell Nature Reserve
Description: Holwell Nature Reserve, near Melton Mowbray, Leicestershire, is a 16.4-hectare site managed by the Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust. It encompasses Brown's Hill Quarry, Holwell Mineral Line, and North Quarry, featuring former limestone quarries and ancient woodland. The reserve is notable for its diverse habitats, rare plants, abundant butterflies, and significant geological features, including Jurassic-era rocks. It is designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Holwell Nature Reserve
Description: Holwell Nature Reserve is a former ironstone quarry near Melton Mowbray, managed by Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust. It features diverse habitats including woodland, grassland, and wetland, supporting a wide range of flora and fauna, such as marsh orchids, butterflies, and amphibians. It is a Local Wildlife Site.

Name: Holyfield Marsh
Description: Holyfield Marsh, part of Lee Valley Regional Park in Essex, is an internationally important wetland. It provides a vital habitat for diverse bird populations, including waterfowl and waders, offering year-round birdwatching.

Name: Holywell Bay & Kelsey Head
Description: Holywell Bay offers golden sands, grassy dunes, and the iconic Gull Rocks on the North Cornwall coast. Part of a larger landscape including Kelsey Head, it provides coastal walks, wildlife spotting, and rock pool exploration for visitors.

Name: Holywell Pond
Description: Holywell Pond is a key Northumberland nature reserve, noted for its diverse birdlife. A large freshwater pond, surrounded by reedbeds and grassland, provides essential habitat for many species. Visitors can observe various waterfowl from hides.

Name: Homefield Wood
Description: Homefield Wood is a mixed woodland nature reserve near Marlow. It features ancient woodland characteristics and supports diverse flora and fauna, including dormice and various orchids. Traditional coppicing is used to maintain biodiversity and create habitats for rare butterflies.

Name: Honeygar
Description: Honeygar is an 81-hectare (200-acre) nature reserve on the Somerset Levels, undergoing restoration from arable land to wetland habitats. It supports bird species like lapwing and curlew, plus many invertebrates, forming part of a larger Living Landscape area within the Avalon Marshes.

Name: Hook Common and Bartley Heath
Description: Hook Common and Bartley Heath is a large nature reserve in northeast Hampshire. It features diverse habitats including dry and wet heathland, acid grassland, woodland, and ponds. The reserve supports wildlife such as dragonflies, common lizards, woodlarks, and Dartford warblers. It is managed for conservation.

Name: Hook Common and Bartley Heath
Description: Hook Common and Bartley Heath, a Site of Special Scientific Interest, features extensive heathland, acid grassland, and woodland. Part of the Basingstoke heathlands, it supports rare ground-nesting birds, reptiles such as common lizards, slow worms, grass snakes, and adders, and diverse invertebrates. Popular for walking and cycling.

Name: Hook Norton Cutting
Description: Hook Norton Cutting is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a regionally important geological site. It features Lower Jurassic Marlstone rock, rich in ironstone fossils and minerals. The reserve includes limestone grassland, home to diverse flora and insects. Managed by BBOWT for geological and ecological interest.

Name: Hookheath Meadows
Description: Hookheath Meadows is a small wildlife haven bordering the River Blackwater. It comprises two traditionally managed hay meadows. The site hosts diverse wildflowers like ragged robin and great burnet, along with various grasses. It supports a range of insects, including butterflies and dragonflies.

Name: Hookheath Meadows Nature Reserve
Description: Hookheath Meadows is a tranquil 14-hectare nature reserve in Southwick, Hampshire, leased to the Hampshire & Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust by Southwick Estates. It features a diverse mosaic of unimproved wildflower meadows, ancient woodland, scrub, and hedgerows, traversed by a river. Part of the reserve is a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). It provides a vital habitat for various plants, insects (including plentiful silver-washed fritillary butterflies and a wide range of hoverflies), and birds, and is managed for conservation and biodiversity.

Name: Hope Valley
Description: Hope Valley, near Minsterley, Shropshire, is a steep-sided wooded valley with ancient semi-natural woodland, managed by Shropshire Wildlife Trust. It is home to a colony of dormice and features wildflowers like bluebells, yellow archangel, and early purple orchids. The site is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) primarily for its geological importance, showcasing Ordovician and Silurian strata, and its rich fossil faunas. Its lush, damp conditions contribute to its 'rainforest' classification.

Name: Hopland's Wood
Description: Hopland's Wood is a damp ancient woodland on moisture-retentive boulder clays, characteristic of the oak/ash woods of Lincolnshire. It features mature oak and ash, with a diverse understory including field maple, hazel, and wild cherry. In spring, bluebells, early purple orchid, spotted-orchid, and herb-Paris are present. The reserve supports a varied bird population, including woodcock, tawny owl, and treecreeper, and a pond attracts spawning frogs.

Name: Hopton Fen
Description: Hopton Fen is a mosaic of wet woodland, reedbed, and species-rich unimproved grassland in the Waveney Valley. It provides habitat for diverse wildlife, including otters, water voles, and various invertebrates. Springs create flush habitats.

Name: Hornchurch Country Park
Description: Hornchurch Country Park is a Green Flag park in Havering, London, on a former WWII airfield. It offers diverse habitats like grasslands, woodlands, and ponds, traversed by the River Ingrebourne, providing wildlife haven and recreation.

Name: Horndon Meadow
Description: Horndon Meadow is a small, 0.8-hectare unimproved hay meadow in Essex, managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust. It is home to over 80 species of wildflowers, including green-winged orchids, yellow rattles, musk mallows, black knapweeds, and adder's-tongue ferns. The meadow is managed with a single hay cut each summer.

Name: Horsey Mere & Marshes
Description: Horsey Mere and its marshes are a key part of the Norfolk Broads. The site offers panoramic views and provides habitat for diverse wildlife, including many bird species. Visitors explore the historic Horsey Windpump and its scenic walking trails.

Name: Horsey Windpump
Description: Horsey Windpump stands on the Horsey Estate in the Broads National Park, Norfolk. This iconic National Trust windpump offers panoramic views across the mere and surrounding marshes, a haven for wildlife. Visitors can climb to the top for expansive views.

Name: Hosehill Lake
Description: Hosehill Lake is a former gravel pit, now a nature reserve west of Reading. It offers open water, reedbeds, and woodland, supporting overwintering wildfowl and migrating birds. Footpaths provide access for wildlife observation and quiet recreation.

Name: Hosehill Lake
Description: Hosehill Lake is a former gravel pit near Theale, West Berkshire, now a diverse nature reserve. It features a large lake, reedbeds, and woodlands, providing a vital habitat for numerous bird species throughout the year. Visitors can enjoy walking trails and bird hides.

Name: Hoselaw Loch and Din Moss
Description: Hoselaw Loch and Din Moss is a Scottish Borders reserve with an ancient loch and peatland habitat. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest. The site supports otters, whooper swans, overwintering wildfowl, and diverse plant species. Habitats include fen, marsh, and woodland.

Name: Hothfield Heathlands
Description: Hothfield Heathlands is Kent's last remaining lowland heath, a rare habitat supporting bog plants, heather, and gorse. Rare insects thrive here, alongside birds like willow warbler and nightjar. The reserve features ponds and boardwalks.

Name: Houghton Forest
Description: Houghton Forest lies on the edge of the South Downs National Park in West Sussex. It features varied woodlands, open chalk grassland, and panoramic views across the Arun Valley. This site provides diverse habitats and is popular for walking.

Name: Houghton Meadows
Description: Houghton Meadows is an 8-hectare nature reserve in the Ouse Valley, Cambridgeshire, managed by The Wildlife Trust for Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Northamptonshire. It is designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and comprises ancient hay meadows and pasture with distinctive medieval ridge and furrow features. The reserve supports diverse wildflowers like cowslips, yellow-rattle, and green-winged orchids, providing habitat for various insects and birds such as green woodpeckers and great crested newts. It borders the River Great Ouse and includes a small brook and ancient hedgerows.

Name: Hounslow Heath Green Gym
Description: Hounslow Heath Green Gym is a TCV project in West London. It meets weekly, offering conservation activities like scrub removal, path clearing, and pond maintenance. Tasks vary seasonally, contributing to the management of Hounslow Heath. No experience is required.

Name: Hoveringham Pastures
Description: Hoveringham Pastures is a mosaic of grasslands, wetlands, and open water habitats located in the Trent Valley, Nottinghamshire. The reserve supports diverse birdlife, including migratory species, and a range of invertebrates. It is managed to enhance biodiversity and maintain ecological balance.

Name: How Hill National Nature Reserve
Description: How Hill National Nature Reserve offers diverse habitats within the Norfolk Broads, including wetlands and woodlands. Visitors can explore nature trails, the gardens of How Hill House, and a boardwalk through sedge and rush beds. Electric Eel boat trips provide unique water-based tours.

Name: Howe Ridding
Description: Howe Ridding Wood is an ancient woodland nature reserve in Cumbria, part of Witherslack Woods. It features exceptionally rich and diverse flowering plants, including rare species like Lancastrian whitebeam and dark-red helleborine. Coppice management supports various butterflies, such as fritillaries, and the reserve is home to a traditional orchard. It provides habitat for diverse invertebrates, fungi, and bird species like buzzard and redstart.

Name: Howell Hill
Description: Howell Hill is a 5-hectare nature reserve east of Ewell in Surrey, owned by Surrey County Council and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust. This chalk downland site features old chalk spoil heaps rich in wildflowers, with approximately 260 species recorded, including various orchids like bee, common spotted, fragrant, pyramidal, and white helleborine. It also supports diverse insect life, including over 20 butterfly species such as green hairstreak and small blue, and provides feeding grounds for green woodpeckers due to numerous anthills. Management includes conservation efforts to maintain its biodiversity.

Name: Howsham Mill Island
Description: Howsham Mill Island is a wooded island in the River Derwent near Malton, North Yorkshire. It provides habitat for otters, kingfishers, and various invertebrates. The island is part of the River Derwent Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and is managed for biodiversity by the Renewable Heritage Trust. The island is publicly accessible, though the mill building has specific opening hours.

Name: Huckerby's Meadows
Description: Huckerby's Meadows is a valuable 13-hectare wet meadow, rich in wildlife and supporting over 140 plant species. Situated on the floodplain of the River Crane, adjacent to Heathrow Airport, it features sedges, grasses, and wildflowers like cuckooflower and ragged-robin. Managed by London Wildlife Trust for biodiversity, it includes old pastures, remnant orchard, scrub, river, and wet woodland.

Name: Hucking Estate
Description: Hucking Estate offers a mosaic of ancient woodland, grassland, orchards, and arable land in the Kent Downs Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. This wildlife haven supports varied flora and fauna, including dormice and many bird species. Walking trails are present.

Name: Hucking Estate
Description: Hucking Estate is a large woodland and open space mosaic in Kent, South East England. It features ancient woodland, recently planted areas, and meadows, providing diverse habitats for wildlife. The site offers numerous walking trails and is part of a landscape restoration project.

Name: Huish Moor
Description: Huish Moor, a diverse nature reserve in Somerset managed by Somerset Wildlife Trust, features a mix of neutral grassland, mire, and woodland on a north-facing slope around the headwaters of the River Tone. This site supports a rich array of rare and protected species, including specific plants like Opposite-leaved Golden Saxifrage, various orchids, and a wide range of dragonflies and butterflies. Its wet habitats are particularly important for its diverse flora and invertebrate life.

Name: Humberhead Peatlands National Nature Reserve
Description: Humberhead Peatlands National Nature Reserve is England's largest lowland raised bog, encompassing Thorne, Hatfield, and Crowle Moors across 2,800 hectares. It is a Special Area of Conservation, vital for its unique peatland habitats and rare wildlife. Restoration efforts are ongoing.

Name: Humphrey Head
Description: Humphrey Head is a coastal limestone outcrop on the Cartmel Peninsula, providing spectacular views over Morecambe Bay. This Cumbria Wildlife Trust nature reserve features limestone grassland, woodland, scrub, and cliffs, supporting unique plants and diverse wildlife.

Name: Hunsdon and Eastwick Meads
Description: Hunsdon and Eastwick Meads is a Site of Special Scientific Interest in Hertfordshire. This traditional riverside grazing meadow supports diverse flora, including various grasses, sedges, and wildflowers. The site is important for insects, amphibians, and birds.

Name: Hunter's Baulk
Description: Hunter's Baulk is a small, species-rich grassland nature reserve in Warwickshire. It features a medieval field boundary baulk, creating diverse habitats for wildflowers such as cowslips and ox-eye daisies, alongside various insect species. The reserve offers valuable insight into traditional agricultural landscapes.

Name: Hunter's Hill
Description: Hunter's Hill is a woodland reserve overlooking the Douglas Valley near Parbold. Mixed oak and birch woodlands support diverse wildlife along a network of paths. The site also features the remains of a Victorian folly, offering historical interest to visitors.

Name: Hunter's Wood
Description: Hunter's Wood is a 1-hectare woodland, planted in 1999 on former pasture, managed by Cheshire Wildlife Trust. It aims to create a wildlife corridor linking fragments of ancient woodland. The reserve features young native trees, open glades, and a newly created pond. Species like small-leaved lime, devil's-bit scabious, meadowsweet, southern hawker, common darter, willow tit, and bullfinch are present.

Name: Hustyn Wood
Description: Hustyn Wood is a mixed woodland in Cornwall, managed by Forestry England, adjoining Bishop's Woods. It features ancient trees, including tall Douglas firs, and offers a diverse habitat for wildlife. The site provides popular walking and cycling trails, accessible from the Camel Trail, and contributes to local biodiversity.

Name: Hutchison's Meadow
Description: Hutchison’s Meadow is a charming wet meadow and woodland, spanning 1.25 hectares and offering a mosaic of diverse habitats that support a wide range of wildlife. It is an interesting flower-rich grassland that is a mix of spring-fed wet grassland and drier grassland associated with sand and gravels.

Name: Huttoft Bank Pit
Description: Huttoft Bank Pit is the largest of the Sea Bank Clay Pits, created after the 1953 floods for sea bank repairs. It features a large open water area and extensive reedbeds, providing habitats for diverse aquatic and terrestrial wildlife. The reserve supports numerous bird species, including moorhen, water rail, reed bunting, reed and sedge warblers, various ducks, short-eared owls, marsh harriers, and bitterns. Otters have also been recorded here. The vegetation includes species such as fennel pondweed, sea club-rush, great reedmace, and yellow flag.

Name: Huttoft Marsh
Description: Huttoft Marsh is a coastal grazing marsh and a Site of Special Scientific Interest in Lincolnshire. It features freshwater scrapes, ditches, and reedbeds, supporting breeding and wintering birds like avocets and lapwings. It is part of the Lincolnshire Coastal Country Park.

Name: Hutton Roof Crags
Description: Hutton Roof Crags, near Kirkby Lonsdale, is a nationally important mosaic of limestone grassland and ancient woodland. Its extensive limestone pavement provides a unique habitat for specialised plants and diverse invertebrates. Mixed broadleaf woodland also flourishes.

Name: Hyde Park
Description: Hyde Park in central London features The Dell, a picturesque rock garden, and the Serpentine lake, which supports diverse wildlife. It is one of the capital's eight Royal Parks, offering both natural habitats and recreational spaces for visitors.

Name: Ickenham Marsh
Description: Ickenham Marsh is a remnant of ancient wet woodland and marshland habitat along the River Pinn. Managed to protect its rich biodiversity, it supports various plant and animal species, including mature alder and willow trees, and diverse invertebrates.

Name: Ickworth Estate
Description: Ickworth Estate is an 1,800-acre Suffolk property featuring a neoclassical mansion, Italianate garden, and ancient deer park. The estate actively manages nature recovery projects across its parkland and Lownde Wood, enhancing diverse habitats for wildlife. Visitors can explore extensive walks.

Name: Ide Hill
Description: Ide Hill offers panoramic views over the Weald of Kent, featuring ancient woodlands and open commons along the Greensand Ridge. Visitors can follow waymarked trails through diverse habitats. The site is managed for conservation, providing opportunities for walking and enjoying nature.

Name: Idle Valley Nature Reserve
Description: Idle Valley Nature Reserve, a wetland of over 450 hectares in the East Midlands, features lakes, reeds, and grasslands along the River Idle. It supports diverse bird species like overwintering wildfowl and migrating waders, otters, various invertebrates, and reintroduced beavers.

Name: Iffley Meadows
Description: Iffley Meadows is a floodplain meadow in Oxfordshire, renowned for its snakeshead fritillaries. Located next to the River Thames, it offers a habitat for various invertebrates and waterfowl. Managed for wildlife conservation, it provides an important green space.

Name: Iffley Meadows
Description: Iffley Meadows is a riverside site in Oxford, famous for its display of Snakes-head Fritillaries in April. It is a floodplain meadow on the River Thames with various wildlife habitats including hedgerows, ditches, and the river itself.

Name: Ilam Park & Dovedale
Description: Ilam Park, a 160-acre riverside park, features a 17th-century hall and designed landscape near Dovedale. It offers walking routes along the River Manifold and serves as a gateway to the White Peak, known for its distinctive limestone geology.

Name: Ilfracombe & Torrs Park
Description: A dramatic coastal landscape near Ilfracombe, North Devon, offering rugged cliffs, panoramic views across the Bristol Channel, and ancient woodlands. Popular for walking, the site features maintained paths, including parts of the South West Coast Path. Managed for nature and public access.

Name: Ilkley Integrated Constructed Wetland
Description: The Ilkley Integrated Constructed Wetland is a nature-based solution designed to provide a final stage of wastewater treatment for the upgraded Ilkley Wastewater Treatment Works. It features six interconnected lagoons with specially chosen wetland plants that naturally treat water before its safe return to the River Wharfe. This project also creates new habitats, enhances biodiversity, and provides public access, contributing to the ecological health and natural flood management of the Lower Wharfe Valley.

Name: Inchnadamph NNR Bone Caves
Description: Inchnadamph NNR in the Scottish Highlands is a landscape of limestone hills, caves, and gorges. Its famous Bone Caves contain unique remains of arctic animals from the last Ice Age, including lynx and polar bear. The reserve supports ancient woodlands and diverse plant life.

Name: Inchree Waterfall & Wood
Description: Inchree, near Fort William, features a spectacular multi-tiered waterfall and accessible woodland trails for walking and cycling. Visitors enjoy nature and wildlife watching opportunities within the Scottish Highlands.

Name: Ingrebourne Valley
Description: Ingrebourne Valley is a diverse nature reserve in East London, featuring grasslands, woodlands, marshes, and the River Ingrebourne. It supports various wildlife, including water voles, kingfishers, and rare invertebrates, with accessible nature trails.

Name: Ingrebourne Valley
Description: Ingrebourne Valley, a nature reserve in Havering, offers diverse habitats including woodlands, grasslands, and wetlands. Part of Ingrebourne Marshes SSSI, it runs south from Upminster to Hornchurch, supporting various wildlife species and providing public recreation.

Name: Inkpen Common
Description: Inkpen Common is a heathland site on a high plateau, featuring heather, gorse, and acid grassland. It supports Dartford warblers, woodlarks, and nightjars. The site includes ancient woodland and ponds, providing diverse habitats.

Name: Inkpen Crocus Field
Description: Inkpen Crocus Field is a small, unique grassland site in West Berkshire, famous for its annual display of wild crocuses. It is managed to conserve this rare flowering spectacle, attracting visitors in late winter, and supports diverse flora.

Name: Inner Forth
Description: The Inner Forth Wetlands are a significant landscape project in Central Scotland, focused on restoring and connecting vital habitats for migratory birds and local wildlife. It encompasses a network of nature reserves and coastal areas.

Name: Insh Marshes
Description: Insh Marshes is one of Europe's most important wetlands, a vast flood plain alongside the River Spey. Thousands of migratory birds stop here seasonally, and many species of waders, ducks, and geese breed in summer. The reserve supports diverse wildlife, including otters and ospreys. Accessible trails and hides offer viewing opportunities.

Name: Invereshie and Inshriach NNR
Description: Invereshie and Inshriach NNR spans a vast Highland landscape between Strathspey and Speyside. It features extensive Caledonian pinewoods, open moorland, montane habitats, and the River Feshie. This reserve supports rare species including capercaillie, Scottish crossbill, red squirrel, and wildcat.

Name: Inverewe Garden & Estate
Description: Inverewe Garden & Estate is a historic botanical garden in Wester Ross, Scotland, established in the 19th century. It showcases diverse plant collections from around the world, benefiting from the Gulf Stream. The estate includes woodlands, a walled garden, and offers various walking routes.

Name: Iona
Description: Iona, an island off Mull, offers sandy beaches, rocky coves, and significant natural heritage. Its traditional crofting lands support diverse wildlife, including corncrakes. It is a historic place of pilgrimage and peace.

Name: Iping and Stedham Commons
