Description: Nunnery Wood is a 21-hectare Local Nature Reserve located within Worcester Woods Country Park in Worcester. It is an ancient semi-natural woodland, predominantly featuring pedunculate oak with an understorey of coppiced hazel. The wood is home to a variety of wildlife, including great crested newts, pond snails, water beetles, and dragonfly larvae, and is known for its bluebells in spring. It forms part of the Woodland Trail at the Country Park.

Name: Nunnington Hall
Description: Nunnington Hall is a picturesque 17th-century manor house nestled beside the River Rye. It features organic gardens, including a walled garden, and a tea-room. The site hosts art exhibitions and offers various family-friendly activities.

Name: Nunnington Hall
Description: Nunnington Hall, a National Trust property, is situated on the banks of the River Rye in North Yorkshire. Its organic gardens and surrounding estate are a key hub for nature conservation, including efforts to improve the River Rye's health and biodiversity, focusing on water quality, fish passage, and riparian habitat creation, often in partnership with the Ryevitalise Landscape Partnership and engaging local communities.

Name: Nutfield Marshes
Description: Nutfield Marshes is a key wetland reserve in Surrey, featuring open water, extensive reedbeds, damp grassland, and willow scrub. This former aggregate quarry now supports diverse bird species and provides important habitats for wildlife.

Name: Oak Hill Wood
Description: Oak Hill Wood is an ancient woodland in East Barnet, North London, featuring mature oak, hornbeam, and ash trees. The woodland floor supports a rich understorey of bluebells and wild garlic. It provides a vital habitat for various bird species and small mammals within an urban setting.

Name: Oak Hill Wood
Description: Oak Hill Wood is an ancient woodland nature reserve located in East Barnet, north London. Managed by the London Wildlife Trust, it features mature oak, hornbeam, and ash trees. The steeply-sloping medieval woodland supports diverse birdlife, bats, and fungi, offering a valuable urban green space.

Name: Oak Tree Farm
Description: Oak Tree Farm is a 30-acre wetland nature reserve managed by Herefordshire Wildlife Trust, located below Dinmore Hill, south of Leominster. The site features restored wet grassland, newly created pools and reedbeds, and aims to support diverse wetland wildlife and wildflowers.

Name: Oak Tree Farm
Description: Oak Tree Farm is a 30-acre Herefordshire Wildlife Trust site near Bodenham. It forms a key part of the Lugg Valley restoration project, creating wetlands and improving water quality. The farm supports biodiversity with wet grassland, traditional orchards, and new woodlands.

Name: Oak Tree Heath
Description: Oak Tree Heath is a Local Nature Reserve near Mansfield, Nottinghamshire. This scarce lowland heath and acid grassland habitat supports heather, gorse, insects, reptiles, and birds. Managed through grazing by cattle and sheep to preserve its unique biodiversity.

Name: Oakfield Wood
Description: Chinnor Hill Nature Reserve is a 28-hectare site near Chinnor, offering panoramic views over the Vale of Aylesbury. It features a rich mosaic of chalk grassland, mixed scrub, and mature woodland habitats, with diverse trees like beech, ash, and oak. The reserve is home to a variety of wildflowers, including orchids and Chiltern gentian, and provides important habitats for birds and insects. Paths and bridleways wind through the reserve, providing visitor access.

Name: Oakhill Nature Reserve
Description: Oakhill Nature Reserve near Goole is a wetland site managed by the Countryside Access Team and Friends of Oakhill. It features an open water scrape, reedbeds, and wet grassland, supporting diverse birdlife like sedge warblers and kingfishers, plus amphibians. A surfaced path and hide offer visitor access.

Name: Oakley Wood
Description: Oakley Wood, near Warwick, is a 47-hectare ancient woodland site managed by Warwickshire Wildlife Trust. It features mature oak, ash, and hazel trees and is undergoing restoration. The site provides habitat for diverse wildlife and is open for public access.

Name: Oakwood & Blacklow Spinney
Description: Oakwood and Blacklow Spinney are ancient woodlands, dominated by mature oak, ash, hazel and elm. Spring brings a carpet of bluebells and wood anemones. The reserve supports breeding birds and badgers. Maintained for its biodiversity.

Name: Oare Marshes
Description: Oare Marshes, near Faversham, features wet grasslands, reedbeds, saltmarsh, and mudflats. It is a vital habitat for migratory and breeding wading birds and wildfowl, offering a crucial stopping-off point for many species.

Name: Oare Marshes Bird Sanctuary
Description: Oare Marshes near Faversham is an internationally important bird sanctuary, managed by Kent Wildlife Trust. This reserve features saltmarsh, lagoons, and reedbeds, providing crucial habitats for breeding and wintering birds within the Kent Swale National Nature Reserve.

Name: Oare Marshes Nature Reserve
Description: Oare Marshes Nature Reserve is a key wetland site near Faversham, Kent, noted for its diverse birdlife and coastal habitats. It comprises extensive reedbeds, grazing marshes, and saline lagoons, supporting migrating and breeding waterfowl and waders throughout the year. The reserve offers hides and viewing screens.

Name: Ockbrook Wood
Description: Ockbrook Wood is a 12-hectare nature reserve in Derbyshire, preserving ancient woodland features. The site supports a diverse ground flora, including dog's mercury and yellow archangel, under oak, ash, hazel, and field maple canopies. Steep slopes and a stream create varied habitats for tawny owls, jays, and bats.

Name: Ockham Common & Bolder Mere
Description: Ockham Common & Bolder Mere is part of the larger Wisley & Ockham Commons & Chatley Heath nature reserve, a significant heathland area in Surrey. It features open heath, woodland, and the picturesque Bolder Mere lake. The site is a nationally important area for wildlife, designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), Local Nature Reserve (LNR), and part of the Thames Basin Heaths Special Protection Area (SPA). It is particularly noted for its diverse bird species, reptiles (including the rare sand lizard), and a rich variety of invertebrates, especially dragonflies and damselflies.

Name: Old Burghclere Lime Quarry
Description: Old Burghclere Lime Quarry is a Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust nature reserve and a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). This former quarry protects valuable chalk grassland, supporting diverse wildflowers, butterflies (including Small Blue), and orchids (like Fly Orchid and White Helleborine). The site offers refuge for various insect species. Access is generally restricted and requires a permit from the Hampshire & Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust due to the sensitive nature of the site.

Name: Old Hall Marshes
Description: Old Hall Marshes is an RSPB nature reserve, forming part of the Blackwater Estuary National Nature Reserve. Its varied habitats include extensive grazing marshes, brackish water fleets, reedbeds, and saltmarsh, supporting significant bird populations year-round, including avocets, lapwings, redshanks, and wintering brent geese.

Name: Old Lodge
Description: Old Lodge is a former deer hunting lodge on Ashdown Forest, Sussex. This heathland, woodland, and pond site is managed for rare bird species like Dartford warblers and nightjars. Public access allows walking and birdwatching.

Name: Old Moor
Description: Old Moor Nature Reserve, near Barnsley, South Yorkshire, is a wetland habitat managed for diverse wildlife. It features lagoons, reedbeds, and grasslands, providing refuge for birds. Visitor facilities include hides and a visitor centre.

Name: Old Nun Wood
Description: Old Nun Wood is an ancient woodland in Warwickshire. It features mature oak, ash, and hazel trees, with a rich understory of wildflowers including bluebells. The reserve provides crucial habitat for various bird species and small mammals.

Name: Old Park Wood
Description: Old Park Wood is an ancient woodland nature reserve near Harefield, managed by Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust. It is known for its mature oaks, hornbeams, and a rich ground flora, including spectacular spring bluebells and rare coralroot bittercress. It provides a vital habitat for various bird species, such as Tawny Owls and Great Spotted Woodpeckers.

Name: Old Sludge Beds
Description: Old Sludge Beds, a Devon Wildlife Trust nature reserve near Exeter, features reedbeds, scrub, and open water. It attracts diverse bird species year-round, with dragonflies and damselflies common in summer. Accessible paths allow for wildlife observation.

Name: Old Sulehay
Description: Old Sulehay is a Northamptonshire nature reserve, part of Rockingham Forest Limestone Mosaic. It features ancient woodland, species-rich grassland, and disused limestone quarries. Habitats support diverse flora and fauna, including rare orchids. Walking trails are present.

Name: Old Warden Tunnel
Description: Old Warden Tunnel is a disused Victorian railway tunnel, now a vital bat roost designated as a SSSI. It provides a crucial habitat for Natterer's, brown long-eared, and Daubenton's bats. Surrounding woodlands and grasslands enhance its ecological value, managed by Wildlife BCN.

Name: Old Wood of Drum
Description: The Old Wood of Drum, near Drumoak, is a significant remnant of an ancient Royal Forest, featuring oak trees over 500 years old. It supports diverse wildlife and is managed for conservation by the National Trust for Scotland.

Name: Oldbury Hill
Description: Oldbury Hill, an Iron Age hillfort and ancient woodland near Ightham, is a Site of Special Scientific Interest. It boasts mature trees and diverse flora, including bluebells and wood anemones. The reserve provides habitats for various bird species and offers marked walking trails.

Name: Oldbury-on-Severn Wood
Description: Oldbury-on-Severn Wood is a small, developing woodland. Planted in 2000, it features mixed broadleaves and conifer species. The site offers views of the River Severn estuary and is accessible via public footpaths.

Name: Oldhall Ponds
Description: Oldhall Ponds is a Scottish Wildlife Trust reserve featuring a mosaic of willow carr, semi-mature planted woodland, and tussocky grassland. Its open water and emergent vegetation attract breeding and wintering waterfowl, dragonflies, damselflies, and other pond life.

Name: Oliver Land
Description: Oliver Land is a 33.5-acre nature reserve near Wadebridge, Cornwall. It features flower-rich pastures, Cornish hedges, and ancient woodland. A River Camel tributary supports barn owls, otters, and kingfishers. Waymarked trails are open for visitors.

Name: Ollerton Pit Wood
Description: Ollerton Pit Wood, a former colliery site, is now a diverse woodland and wetland in Nottinghamshire. Managed by Forestry England, it features accessible walking trails, including the Strawberry Walk, and supports a range of wildlife, providing a quiet green space.

Name: One Tree Hill
Description: One Tree Hill offers panoramic views across the Weald of Kent. Visitors can explore ancient woodlands, rare acid grassland, and heathland. The site is managed by the National Trust, providing opportunities for walking and enjoying nature. Notable features include mature trees and diverse wildlife habitats.

Name: Onziebust
Description: Onziebust is an RSPB nature reserve on Egilsay, Orkney. It features a mosaic of wildflower meadows, grassland fields, and extensive wetland areas, including wet grassland and reedbeds. These habitats support breeding waders such as curlews, lapwings, and snipe, and are home to the nationally scarce Great Yellow Bumblebee. The reserve's tranquil lochs, rocky coast, and sandy beaches provide important feeding grounds for wintering waders and wildfowl like Redshanks and Wigeons. Raptors such as hen harriers also hunt here.

Name: Orford Ness National Nature Reserve
Description: Orford Ness is a remote, shingle spit on the Suffolk coast, managed by the National Trust. It holds a unique history as a secret military testing site and is now a significant nature reserve for wildlife, including rare birds and plants.

Name: Orlestone Forest
Description: Orlestone Forest is a mosaic of habitats in southeast Kent near Hamstreet. It features ancient woodland, coppiced hazel, rides, and open glades. The site supports various bird species, invertebrates, and wildflowers. It is managed for biodiversity and public access.

Name: Orlestone Forest
Description: Orlestone Forest is a significant ancient woodland in Kent, managed by Forestry England. Designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a Nature Conservation Review site, it is nationally important for its invertebrate populations, including rare moth and butterfly species. The forest features a mix of broadleaf and conifer trees, with a focus on both timber production and biodiversity. It offers an extensive network of walking trails for visitors, supporting diverse wildlife including dormice and a variety of woodland birds.

Name: Orlock Point
Description: Orlock Point is a coastal area in Northern Ireland, near Donaghadee, known for its important wildlife habitats. The site features coastal grazing pastures, supporting diverse flora and fauna, and offers views across Belfast Lough. It is managed for conservation.

Name: Orlock Point
Description: Orlock Point, managed by the National Trust, is a significant coastal area near Groomsport, forming part of the North Down Coastal Path. This site features rocky outcrops and diverse semi-natural habitats, supporting a rich variety of plants and animals. A coastal grazing restoration project is underway, benefiting pollinators and coastal flora. The area is also steeped in history and archaeology, offering stunning views across the Irish Sea to the Copeland Islands.

Name: Ormesby Beck
Description: Ormesby Beck Nature Reserve in Middlesbrough is a linear wetland habitat along the beck. It supports species like water vole, kingfisher, and various dragonflies. The reserve features reedbeds, ponds, and wet grassland, providing a vital green corridor.

Name: Ormesby Hall
Description: Ormesby Hall is a Georgian manor house, gardens, and parkland near Middlesbrough, managed by the National Trust. The estate includes a walled garden, woodland walks, and a popular model railway layout. It hosts various community events and seasonal activities throughout the year.

Name: Orton Moss
Description: Orton Moss is a peat bog formed in a glacial basin after the last ice age. Peat has been cut here for centuries. Cumbria Wildlife Trust is restoring the peatland habitat, supporting diverse plant and animal species like sphagnum mosses, cotton grass, dragonflies, and various birds.

Name: Osmington White Horse & Cliffs
Description: The Osmington White Horse is a large hill figure, carved into the limestone above Osmington village in Dorset. It depicts King George III on horseback. Nearby cliffs offer views of Weymouth Bay. The site is accessible for walkers, part of the Jurassic Coast World Heritage Site.

Name: Osterley Park
Description: Osterley Park, a large Georgian estate in west London, focuses on biodiversity recovery. Its varied habitats, including ancient trees, meadows, and lakes, support diverse wildlife. Conservation efforts protect and enhance these environments for future generations.

Name: Oughtonhead Common
Description: Oughtonhead Common is a nature reserve near Hitchin, featuring wet woodland, fen, and grassland habitats fed by the River Oughton. The River Oughton originates from Oughtonhead Spring, a SSSI. Wildlife includes kingfishers, water voles, otters, and Daubenton's bats.

Name: Ouse Estuary Nature Reserve
Description: The Ouse Estuary Nature Reserve, near Newhaven, is managed by East Sussex County Council. This site offers public footpaths and a cycle track, forming a vital wildlife corridor along the River Ouse. It is managed primarily for wildlife benefit and flood management, forming part of a wider conservation effort in the area.

Name: Overbeck's Coastal Garden & Cliffs
Description: Overbeck's is an exotic subtropical garden near Salcombe, Devon, housing rare plants that thrive in its microclimate. The site offers stunning coastal views and a museum showcasing the original owner's eclectic collections.

Name: Overdale
Description: Overdale Nature Reserve, near Buxton, is a dramatic limestone dale with species-rich grasslands. It supports wildflowers, butterflies, and birds, with steep slopes hosting orchids. Managed by Derbyshire Wildlife Trust, it offers public footpaths through unique geology.

Name: Overhall Grove
Description: Overhall Grove is an ancient woodland in Cambridgeshire, managed for diverse trees, wildflowers, and fungi. It provides important habitat for bird species, invertebrates, and mammals. Public access allows for quiet enjoyment, with conservation work maintaining biodiversity.

Name: Overton Carr
Description: Overton Carr is a 1.25-hectare nature reserve near Ashover, Derbyshire, featuring wet woodland and species-rich grassland. Managed for wildlife, it supports diverse flora and fauna, including rare sedges. Public access is available via a footpath.

Name: Owl Wood and Pit Plantation
Description: Owl Wood and Pit Plantation is a Yorkshire Wildlife Trust nature reserve, featuring ancient oak, ash, and hazel woodland alongside a newer plantation. The site supports diverse bird species and ground flora, with a network of paths for public access.

Name: Oxburgh Estate
Description: Oxburgh Estate features a moated manor house, gardens, and parkland in Norfolk. Home to the Bedingfeld family for 500 years, it showcases historic interiors, rare needlework, and a priest hole. Visitors explore extensive grounds with river walks, supporting ongoing heritage and landscape conservation.

Name: Oxey Mead
Description: Oxey Mead is an unimproved hay meadow near Oxford, adjacent to the River Thames. It supports diverse grasses and wildflowers, including large numbers of snakeshead fritillaries. Wading birds are present in winter, and cattle graze the area. This site is managed by BBOWT.

Name: Oxford Island NNR
Description: Oxford Island NNR is a National Nature Reserve on Lough Neagh's southern shore. It features diverse habitats including woodlands, reedbeds, and meadows, supporting significant bird populations. Owned and managed by Armagh City, Banbridge & Craigavon Council, the site offers visitor facilities and walking trails.

Name: Oxhouse Farm
Description: Oxhouse Farm, a 95-acre site run by Warwickshire Wildlife Trust, demonstrates wildlife-friendly farming. It integrates conservation with sustainable agriculture, creating diverse habitats including meadows, hedgerows, and wetlands for various species.

Name: Oxshott Heath & Woods
Description: Oxshott Heath and Woods is a mosaic of woodland and heathland in Surrey, featuring ancient oak and Scots pine trees. The site supports diverse wildlife including birds, invertebrates, and reptiles, with ponds and streams adding ecological value.

Name: Oxwich National Nature Reserve
Description: Oxwich National Nature Reserve, located within the Gower AONB, is a mosaic of diverse habitats. It features extensive sand dunes, saltmarsh, woodland, and a freshwater lake. The reserve supports a rich array of wildlife, including rare insects and plants. Public footpaths offer access for visitors.

Name: Oyster Creek
Description: Oyster Creek forms part of the Orford Ness National Nature Reserve in Suffolk, a vast shingle spit managed by the National Trust. This remote coastal landscape features brackish lagoons, creeks, and saltmarsh habitats, supporting diverse wildlife and significant bird populations.

Name: Oysters Coppice
Description: Oysters Coppice is an ancient woodland managed by the Wiltshire Wildlife Trust, nestled on a slope offering spectacular views over the Vale of Wardour. It features diverse tree species like oak, ash, and alder, with a rich ground flora including wild daffodils, bluebells, primroses, and wild garlic (ramsons) in spring. The reserve supports varied wildlife, notably dormice, badgers, smooth newts, frogs, and a range of woodland birds and dragonflies. Rising springs create boggy areas and streams within the coppice.

Name: Packwood House
Description: Packwood House is a restored timber-framed Tudor manor house in Warwickshire, set within extensive gardens, parkland, and a historic yew garden. It features period rooms, a collection of textiles, and rural walks. The estate reflects centuries of development.

Name: Padworth Common
Description: Padworth Common is a rare lowland heath in West Berkshire. It features diverse habitats including heathland, woodland, and acid grassland, supporting specific birds, reptiles, and invertebrates. The site is managed for nature conservation, offering accessible walking trails.

Name: Pagham Harbour
Description: Pagham Harbour, a West Sussex Site of Special Scientific Interest, is a protected wildlife haven. It features extensive mudflats, saltmarshes, and shingle beaches, supporting diverse bird species. Hides and walking trails are available.

Name: Paices Wood Country Parkland
Description: Paices Wood Country Parkland, located on the edge of Aldermaston in Berkshire, is a 35-hectare former sand and gravel quarry now managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust (BBOWT). It features diverse habitats including woodlands, grasslands, and several lakes in a narrow valley. The site supports a variety of wildlife, including grass snakes, slowworms, common frogs, and numerous butterfly species like the silver-washed fritillary. It offers walking trails for visitors.

Name: Pam's Pools
Description: Pam's Pools is a restored wetland reserve in Shropshire, transformed from a disused gravel pit. It now features open water, extensive reedbeds, and grassland, supporting a diverse array of wetland birds, insects, and amphibians. A valuable habitat for wildlife.

Name: Pamber Forest and Silchester Common
Description: Pamber Forest is an ancient woodland and SSSI in Hampshire, co-managed by Hampshire & Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust. Adjoining Silchester Common, it features diverse woodlands and heathland. The site supports various fungi, plants, and insects, including dormice, woodcock, and rare beetles.

Name: Pamber Forest and Upper Inhams Copse
Description: Pamber Forest and Upper Inhams Copse is an ancient 108.8-hectare woodland in Hampshire, managed by HIWWT. It features oak, birch, hornbeam, and hazel coppice. Rare butterflies like white admiral and purple emperor thrive here, alongside various birds, streams, and ponds.

Name: Panshanger Park
Description: Panshanger Park, near Hertford, is a historic landscape and country park. It holds SSSI status for its geological features and diverse habitats including ancient woodlands and wetlands. The park supports varied wildlife and offers public access for recreation and nature observation.

Name: Pant-y-Sais
Description: Panty-Sais is a valuable wetland site in north Pembrokeshire, featuring fen and reedbed habitats. It supports diverse wildlife, including otters, water voles, and various bird species. The reserve contributes to local biodiversity conservation.

Name: Papercourt Marshes
Description: Papercourt Marshes, part of the larger Papercourt SSSI complex in the Wey Valley, features wet grassland, marsh, scrub, and woodland by the River Wey and Broadmead Cut. This Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) supports diverse birdlife, including wintering wildfowl, waders, and breeding lapwing and snipe, with over 100 bird species recorded. It also provides habitat for water voles, otters, and kingfishers.

Name: Parc Slip
Description: Parc Slip is a nature reserve and visitor centre managed by the Wildlife Trust of South and West Wales. It features diverse habitats including wetlands, woodlands, and grasslands, supporting various bird species and wildflowers. The visitor centre offers facilities and information about local wildlife.

Name: Park Hoskyn Hayman Reserve
Description: Park Hoskyn, near Nanpean in mid-Cornwall, is a Hayman Reserve site. It features an alder and willow carr, grassland, and a section of the Luxulyan River. This small nature reserve supports diverse wildlife, including otters and bats. It provides a peaceful setting for nature observation.

Name: Park Road Pond
Description: Park Road Pond is a large pond in Uxbridge, in the London Borough of Hillingdon, managed as a nature reserve by the London Wildlife Trust. It is a Site of Borough Importance for Nature Conservation, Grade I, and is particularly important for amphibians, including great crested newts. The pond is surrounded by willows, oaks, and alders, and supports diverse aquatic plants and invertebrates.

Name: Parliament Piece
Description: Parliament Piece is a 6-hectare Local Nature Reserve near Kenilworth, Warwickshire, managed in partnership by Warwickshire Wildlife Trust and Warwick District Council. This species-rich site features unimproved grassland managed as a hay meadow, ancient hedgerows (up to 400 years old), tall trees, and a pond. It supports diverse wildflowers such as ragged-robin and common spotted-orchid, and is home to various wildlife including skipper and meadow brown butterflies, great spotted woodpeckers, common frogs, and smooth newts.

Name: Parndon Wood
Description: Parndon Wood Nature Reserve is an ancient woodland spanning over 50 acres, designated a Local Nature Reserve in Harlow, Essex. It features mature hornbeam coppice and oak standards, supporting diverse flora and fauna including deer and various bird species. The reserve offers tranquil walking paths, three bird-watching hides, a large pond, and a conservation centre with a café. It is managed by Harlow District Council in partnership with local charity ECCO and volunteers.

Name: Parsonage Moor
Description: Parsonage Moor is a small, species-rich fen meadow, a stronghold for rare wetland plants including orchids like common spotted and marsh fragrant orchid. The reserve supports diverse insect life and is managed by BBOWT for conservation.

Name: Parsonage Wood
Description: Parsonage Wood is a 9.7-hectare ancient Wealden ghyll woodland and a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Kent, managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust. This remote and tranquil reserve lies on a steep sandstone bank, featuring mature sweet chestnut, oak, birch, hazel, and hornbeam. It supports diverse flora, including bluebell, primrose, golden saxifrage, mosses, liverworts, and ferns, alongside ancient woodland indicator species like butcher's broom, violet helleborine, and pendulous sedge. The site is also home to a rich array of fungi, invertebrates, and common woodland birds.

Name: Pasture Wharf
Description: Pasture Wharf is a nature reserve on the north bank of the River Humber. It features diverse habitats including grassland, scrub, reedbed, and a pond. The site supports various bird species such as reed warblers and Cetti’s warblers. Winter brings waders and wildfowl to the area.

Name: Pathways for Pearls
Description: Pathways for Pearls enhances biodiversity at Welshpool's Old Station, creating wildflower meadows and butterfly habitats. It supports the Pearl-bordered Fritillary by planting nectar-rich flowers and sheltered areas. The project offers educational and volunteering opportunities.

Name: Patmore Heath
Description: Patmore Heath is an 8-hectare nature reserve in Hertfordshire, managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust. It is an outstanding example of grass heathland, a scarce habitat in the south-east of England, featuring a mosaic of valuable habitats including damp grassland and ancient ponds. It supports notable plant species like Heath Rush and Southern Marsh Orchid, and all three native newt species. The site is managed for biodiversity and provides public access via footpaths.

Name: Paull Holme Strays
Description: Paull Holme Strays is a large wetland nature reserve on the Humber Estuary, managed by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust. It provides vital habitat for thousands of migrating waders and wildfowl, especially in winter. The reserve features saline lagoons, mudflats, and reedbeds, with bird hides for visitors.

Name: Pavenham Osier Beds
Description: Pavenham Osier Beds is a 1.3-hectare site beside the River Great Ouse, managed by the Wildlife Trust BCN. It features wet woodland, reedbed, and floodplain grassland, supporting diverse birds, insects, and plant species.

Name: Paxton Pits Nature Reserve
Description: Paxton Pits Nature Reserve is a 77-hectare site in the Great Ouse valley, near Little Paxton, Cambridgeshire. It is a former sand and gravel quarry, now a rich mosaic of habitats including lakes, meadows, reedbed, scrub, and woodland, offering diverse wildlife year-round. It is designated as a Local Nature Reserve and a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Paycocke’s House
Description: Paycocke’s House is a surviving medieval merchant’s house in Coggeshall, Essex. Dating from around 1500, it features intricate timber framing and carvings. The property includes a cottage garden and meadow, showcasing traditional planting.

Name: Peascombe
Description: Peascombe is a 0.8-hectare nature reserve in Dorset, featuring broadleaf woodland and acidic grassland. Historically a WWII minefield, the site is bordered by arable fields. It supports various plants, including dwarf thistle and a range of lichens.

Name: Pease Dean
Description: Pease Dean is a beautiful, ancient semi-natural woodland reserve in the Scottish Borders, featuring steep gorges and two burns (Pease Burn and Tower Burn). Ferns, mosses, and liverworts thrive in its wet, sheltered deans. In spring and summer, the woodland floor is cloaked with a blanket of bluebells, primroses, and wood anemones, attracting diverse butterflies like the speckled wood. Mature ash, oak, and elm trees dominate, supporting rich invertebrate communities. The reserve is home to otters, badgers, roe deer, dippers, and treecreepers.

Name: Peckover House
Description: A Georgian merchant's house in Wisbech, Cambridgeshire, with a two-acre Victorian walled garden. The house contains original furnishings, and the garden features a parterre, fruit trees, and various garden rooms.

Name: Pegsdon Hills and Hoo Bit
Description: Pegsdon Hills and Hoo Bit is a 79-hectare chalk grassland nature reserve located in Pegsdon, Bedfordshire, on the border with Hertfordshire. Managed by The Wildlife Trust for Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Northamptonshire, it is a jewel of the Chilterns Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. The site features a mosaic of habitats including wildflower meadows, woodland, and scrub, with part of it designated as the Deacon Hill SSSI. It supports a variety of rare butterflies such as dingy and grizzled skippers, brown argus, green hairstreak, and small heath, alongside birds like wheatears and skylarks. Hoo Bit itself is a flower-rich grazed meadow surrounded by woodland. Visitors can enjoy panoramic views across the Chilterns.

Name: Pen Ponds, Richmond Park
Description: Pen Ponds are two large, man-made ponds in the centre of Richmond Park, created in 1746. Fed by a spring, they host diverse birdlife like Grey Herons and Great Crested Grebes. Fishing is permitted with a permit acquired from the Roehampton Gate office.

Name: Pen y Fan & Central Beacons
Description: Pen y Fan and the Central Beacons are a prominent landscape in the Brecon Beacons National Park. This area encompasses the highest peak in southern Britain, offering extensive views and diverse habitats. Popular for walking and outdoor activities, it features rugged terrain and rich natural beauty.

Name: Penbryn
Description: Penbryn estate on the Ceredigion coast features a mile of golden sand beach and ancient woodlands. A river, the Hoffnant, flows through the estate. It offers habitat for wildlife and trails for walkers, with a focus on nature conservation.

Name: Pencnwc Mawr
Description: Pencnwc Mawr Wood is a temperate rainforest site in Pembrokeshire, managed by the Wildlife Trust of South and West Wales. The project restores ancient and semi-natural woodland, replacing conifer plantations with native broadleaf trees. It is part of a wider rainforest project.

Name: Pendarves Wood
Description: Pendarves Wood is an ancient woodland near Camborne, Cornwall, featuring mature broadleaf and conifer trees with a diverse understory. Bluebells and ramsons carpet the woodland floor in spring. The site is home to badger setts and diverse wildlife.

Name: Peninnis Head
Description: Peninnis Head is a maritime heathland site on St Mary's, Isles of Scilly. It hosts rare plants like fescue and early meadow grass. The site is part of a restoration project aiming to return native heathland to the islands. Managed by the Isles of Scilly Wildlife Trust.

Name: Penlee Battery Woods
Description: Penlee Battery Woods overlooks Plymouth Sound. The woods contain diverse habitats including ancient semi-natural woodland, maritime grassland and scrub, alongside historic military features.

Name: Penmon Point
Description: Penmon Point, on the eastern tip of Anglesey, offers expansive views across to Puffin Island and the Great Orme. An iconic offshore lighthouse marks the site. It features a pebble beach, strong tidal currents, and is recognised for its diverse wildlife, especially seabirds. The area forms part of a significant marine gateway.

Name: Penn Wood
Description: Penn Wood is a nature reserve near Calne, Wiltshire, managed by Wiltshire Wildlife Trust. Originally farmland, it was a sand quarry and landfill before being restored. In 2010, 10,000 trees were planted, and rewilding efforts include relocating slow worms and creating ponds. It features diverse wildflowers and supports various wildlife species.

Name: Pennington Flash
Description: Pennington Flash, near Leigh, is a significant nature reserve managed by Wigan Council. It offers diverse habitats for wildlife, including many rare bird species, and provides opportunities for walking, cycling, and fishing. The site operates as a key nature recovery hub.

Name: Pennytown Ponds Local Nature Reserve
Description: Pennytown Ponds is a Local Nature Reserve near Somercotes, Ripley, Derbyshire, managed by Amber Valley Borough Council. It features a mosaic of four ponds, woodland, marshland, and grassland meadows, providing diverse habitats. The reserve is home to amphibians, numerous insects including damselflies and dragonflies, and a variety of birds such as moorhens, coots, mallards, green woodpeckers, spotted woodpeckers, and kingfishers. It also supports a diverse selection of wildflowers, including orchids, and has received Green Flag status.

Name: Penorchard Meadows
Description: Penorchard Meadows is a traditional hay meadow system. It features diverse wildflowers, including knapweed, bird's-foot trefoil, eyebright, dyer's greenweed, yellow rattle, yellow-wort, common spotted orchid, and ragged-robin. The reserve supports varied insect life, and many species of bird are seen throughout the year. A public footpath provides access, with parking available at St Kenelm's Church on Chapel Lane.

Name: Penrose & Loe Pool
Description: Penrose, encompassing Cornwall's largest natural freshwater lake, Loe Pool, is separated from the sea by a shingle bar. The estate offers diverse habitats across woodlands, historic parkland, and farmland, providing various walking routes.

Name: Pensthorpe Natural Park
Description: Pensthorpe Natural Park is an award-winning 700-acre nature reserve and conservation charity in Norfolk, UK. It features diverse habitats, including wetlands, woodlands, and gardens, supporting a variety of wildlife and offering conservation experiences.

Name: Penthellyg
Description: Penthellyg is a small field of unimproved, species-rich grassland in mid-Wales, adjacent to the River Dyfi. It supports wildflowers including greater butterfly-orchid and yellow rattle. Wetter areas host sedges, rushes, and various invertebrates.

Name: Pentire
Description: Pentire is a spectacular National Trust headland on the north Cornwall coast, managed for wildlife and offering far-reaching views. It encompasses diverse coastal landscapes, including the popular beaches of Polzeath, Daymer Bay, and Rock, and provides access to the Camel Estuary. The area is rich in history, with Iron Age ramparts, and supports an abundance of wildflowers and a variety of wildlife. Visitors can enjoy walking routes and coastal exploration.

Name: Pentrosfa Mire
Description: Pentrosfa Mire is a small lowland mire in Powys, Wales, managed by Radnorshire Wildlife Trust. This wetland, heath, and woodland reserve supports a diverse range of plant and insect life, including sundew, bog mosses, northern marsh-orchids, and a rare lichen species new to science. It is an important habitat for wintering birds like snipe and jack snipe, and in summer, dragonflies, damselflies, and butterflies thrive. The site is also a significant peat bog and carbon sink, contributing to biodiversity and climate change mitigation.

Name: Pentwyn
Description: Pentwyn, a 164-acre former farm in mid Wales, serves as Radnorshire Wildlife Trust's rewilding flagship. The site is transforming into diverse habitats like woodlands, meadows, and wetlands, driven by natural processes and species reintroduction. It aims to restore biodiversity and ecological resilience in the Marches.

Name: Pentwyn Farm
Description: Pentwyn Farm, in the Usk Valley, conserves a traditional hay meadow. Rich in wildflowers like orchids and various insect species, it provides habitat for butterflies. Sheep grazing maintains the sward structure. The reserve offers peaceful walking trails.

Name: Pentwyn Farm
Description: Pentwyn Farm is a 7.6-hectare nature reserve in Monmouthshire, southeast Wales, managed by Gwent Wildlife Trust. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) known for its traditionally-managed, flower-rich grasslands, ancient hedgerows, and an orchard. The reserve supports diverse wildlife including hazel dormice, green-winged orchids, and various butterflies and birds.

Name: Pepper Wood
Description: Pepper Wood is a small, broadleaved woodland in the City of Edinburgh, managed by the Scottish Wildlife Trust. It features predominantly ash, wych elm, and sycamore trees, supporting a diverse array of native and non-native flowering plants, including bluebells in May. Public footpaths offer access for visitors.

Name: Pepperbox Hill
Description: Pepperbox Hill is a chalk ridge south-east of Salisbury, Wiltshire, known for its distinctive 17th-century pepperbox-shaped folly. The site features a diverse scrub-grassland mosaic habitat, supporting various species including orchids, juniper, and yew woodland.

Name: Peppercombe Wood
Description: Peppercombe Wood is an ancient woodland located on the Urchfont Scarp. It features diverse broadleaf trees, including oak and ash, with ground flora like bluebells. The wood supports various bird species and invertebrates. Public footpaths offer visitor access.

Name: Perry Woods
Description: Perry Woods spans 149 acres near Selling, Kent, comprising woodland, orchards, and grassland. It sits on a north-facing chalk escarpment. The site is noted for its spring bluebells and hosts over 50 bird species and 20 butterfly species, including the grizzled skipper.

Name: Peter's Stone
Description: Peter's Stone is a prominent limestone knoll within Cressbrook Dale, part of the Derbyshire Dales National Nature Reserve, near Wardlow Mires in the Peak District. It features species-rich limestone grassland and ancient ash woodland, known for diverse flora including rare orchids. Managed by Natural England, it offers views across the Wye Valley.

Name: Petershill
Description: Petershill, a Scottish Wildlife Trust reserve near Bathgate in West Lothian, was formerly a limestone quarry and reservoir. It features varied habitats including species-rich grassland, scrub, and wetland, and is also an important geological site. It supports diverse birds, insects, and wildflowers, providing crucial local wildlife habitat.

Name: Pett Level Coastal Marsh
Description: Pett Level in East Sussex encompasses a significant coastal marsh and shingle environment, including the freshwater wetland known as Pett Pools. This area is crucial for diverse marine life and provides important nesting grounds for various bird species along the East Sussex coastline.

Name: Pevensey Marshes
Description: Pevensey Marshes is a large expanse of grazing marsh and dykes, home to rare plants and insects. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a Ramsar site, recognised internationally for its wetland importance.

Name: Pevensey Marshes
Description: Pevensey Levels, including Northeye, is a significant grazing marsh in East Sussex. It offers a vital habitat for rare invertebrates, notably the endangered Fen Raft Spider, and is designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI).

Name: Pevensey Road Nature Reserve
Description: Pevensey Road Nature Reserve is a 10.2-hectare Local Nature Reserve in Hanworth, in the London Borough of Hounslow, West London. It is owned and managed by Hounslow Council, with The Conservation Volunteers (TCV) running weekly Green Gym sessions to help manage the site. The reserve lies on the banks of the River Crane and features species-rich wildflower meadows, damp woodland, and wetlands. It is also part of the Crane Corridor Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation and connects to Little Park via a wooden bridge.

Name: Pewit Island
Description: Pewit Island is an uninhabited nature reserve in Langstone Harbour, Hampshire. It serves as a crucial high-tide roost for wading birds like dunlin and grey plover, and supports breeding terns. Saltmarsh and shingle habitats host diverse coastal flora.

Name: Pewit Island Nature Reserve
Description: Pewit Island is an uninhabited island within Langstone Harbour, providing a vital sanctuary for wildlife. It is a nationally important breeding site for little terns and other seabirds. Access is restricted to protect nesting birds and sensitive habitats.

Name: Pewley Meadows
Description: Pewley Meadows, adjacent to Pewley Down, is a recently acquired 37.5-acre chalk grassland near Guildford, managed by Surrey Wildlife Trust. It is known for its diverse wildflowers and butterflies, including nesting skylarks and chalkhill blue butterflies. The site offers panoramic views and is managed to enhance biodiversity and public access, forming a vital part of Surrey's nature recovery network.

Name: Philips Park
Description: Philips Park is a Victorian Green Flag park and Local Nature Reserve in Whitefield, Bury, Greater Manchester. It features rich woodland and grassland habitats, ancient woodlands, walking trails, and a children's play area. The park is home to diverse wildlife and includes the Barn Countryside Centre.

Name: Phillips's Point
Description: Phillips's Point is a quiet Cornwall Wildlife Trust nature reserve located on the River Lynher, near Antony Passage. It protects important saltmarsh and estuarine mudflats, vital habitats for diverse birdlife, including waders and wildfowl.

Name: Phoenix Garden
Description: The Phoenix Garden is a community green space and registered charity in London's West End. Established in 1984 on a former car park, it provides an oasis for urban wildlife and people, featuring frogs, newts, and foxes.

Name: Phoenix Park
Description: Phoenix Park is a community woodland located in Sheffield, South Yorkshire. The Conservation Volunteers (TCV) manage the site, conducting weekly practical conservation sessions every Wednesday. It provides an accessible green space for local residents.

Name: Phyllis Currie
Description: Phyllis Currie is an 8.9-hectare nature reserve in Essex, featuring mixed woodland and an old gravel pit. The woodland is mainly oak, with hornbeam and sweet chestnut. The gravel pit area hosts scrub, grassland, a small pond, and a marshy section.

Name: Phyllis Currie
Description: Phyllis Currie Nature Reserve is an 8.9-hectare (22-acre) site located north-west of Great Leighs in Essex, managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust. This reserve features diverse habitats including grassland, a lake, woodland, and ditches. It supports a rich variety of wildlife, with notable sightings of kingfishers, grey herons, 23 species of butterflies, and 13 species of dragonflies and damselflies. Access is available from Dumney Lane.

Name: Pick Triangle Wood
Description: Pick Triangle Wood, opened 2005, is a young woodland near Measham, Leicestershire. It features accessible paths, a small stream, and native broadleaf species. The wood includes an arboretum area and connects to a longer walking route along the Ashby Canal.

Name: Pickering's Meadow
Description: Pickering's Meadow is a nature reserve in West Lindsey, near Caenby Corner, featuring neutral grassland, a pond, and woodland. It provides a habitat for various orchids, butterflies, and birds, and is managed for wildlife. Public access is available via a short path.

Name: Pigneys Wood
Description: Pigneys Wood is a 23-hectare Norfolk Wildlife Trust reserve located near North Walsham, Norfolk. Originally farmland, it was transformed by the North Norfolk Community Woodland Trust from 1993, with over 20,000 native trees planted, alongside the creation of flower-rich grassland, a pond, and restored fen habitats. Norfolk Wildlife Trust took over management in 2017. The reserve features ancient woodland, including a 450-year-old oak tree and springtime bluebells, mixed plantations, meadows, and wetlands. It provides a vital refuge for diverse wildlife, including woodland birds like nuthatch and treecreeper, otters, water voles, badgers, and various butterflies and dragonflies. Accessible trails, including sections of the Paston Way, are available for visitors, with a car park on Hall Lane.

Name: Pilch Field
Description: Pilch Field is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Buckinghamshire, comprising ancient hay meadows with ridge and furrow grassland. This unimproved grassland supports diverse wildflowers, including green-winged orchids, and provides valuable habitat for insects and birds. The reserve features wet meadows, scrub, and hedgerows.

Name: Pilmuir Riparian Project
Description: The Pilmuir Riparian Project, near Peebles in the Scottish Borders, restores riverbanks along the Eddleston Water. It involves planting native trees and improving biodiversity. This is a collaboration between SP Energy Networks, Borders Forest Trust, and Tweed Forum.

Name: Pilsdon Pen
Description: Pilsdon Pen is a prominent hill in west Dorset, reaching 277 metres (909 feet) above sea level. It features an Iron Age hill fort, offering expansive views across the Marshwood Vale and to the coast. Managed by the National Trust, it is a significant archaeological and natural landmark.

Name: Pinchbeck Fen Slipe
Description: Pinchbeck Fen Slipe is a linear nature reserve managed by the Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust, situated near Spalding. It features wide areas of grassland that flood when river levels are high, wet marsh pools, borrow pits, and a roadside dyke. The reserve supports diverse flora such as water crowfoot, water violet, yellow loosestrife, yellow rattle, common fleabane, and ragged robin. It is also home to breeding birds like great crested grebe, mallard, coot, reed warbler, reed bunting, and whitethroat, with barn owls hunting over the reserve. In winter, it attracts wildfowl including wigeon, teal, tufted duck, and goosander, as well as flocks of lapwing and golden plover. The site includes a small woodland area with a mature hawthorn hedge and is grazed by cattle and used for hay-making.

Name: Pirbright Common
Description: Pirbright Common is a heathland site in Surrey, providing habitats for a range of wildlife, including rare birds, reptiles, and invertebrates. The common is managed to conserve its diverse ecosystems and support local biodiversity.

Name: Pitsford Water
Description: Pitsford Water Nature Reserve, managed by the Wildlife Trust BCN, is a significant site for overwintering wildfowl and migrating birds in Northamptonshire. The reserve features diverse habitats including woodlands, grasslands, and reedbeds. Walking trails are available.

Name: Pitts Wood
Description: Pitts Wood is a small ancient woodland in the Chiltern Hills, located near Lane End, Buckinghamshire. The site features mature beech and oak trees, a stream, and diverse ground flora. It supports varied wildlife including various birds and invertebrates, offering a quiet natural retreat.

Name: Pity Me Carrs
Description: Pity Me Carrs is a wetland nature reserve situated near Pity Me in County Durham. It encompasses diverse marshland and grassland habitats, providing a vital home for various bird species and plant life.

Name: Pixey and Yarnton Meads
Description: These two large flood meadows on the River Thames are ancient and species-rich. Designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest, they support a diverse range of grassland flora and fauna. Management involves traditional hay-cutting and grazing.

Name: Pleasley Pit Country Park
Description: Pleasley Pit Country Park, a former Nottinghamshire coal mine, has been transformed into a vibrant nature reserve. It features a preserved working steam winding engine and heritage centre, offering visitors walking trails and rich wildlife habitats. The park uniquely combines industrial history with diverse biodiversity for public enjoyment.

Name: Ploughman Wood
Description: Ploughman Wood is an ancient woodland in Nottinghamshire, rich in oak and hazel. The reserve supports a diverse ground flora, including bluebells and wood anemones, providing habitats for various bird and insect species throughout the year.

Name: Polhill Bank
Description: Polhill Bank is a sloping chalk grassland on a southeast-facing hillside overlooking the Darenth Valley, with ancient woodland and scrub at its summit. This Kent Wildlife Trust reserve provides a habitat for diverse wildflowers, including orchids and rock-rose, and numerous invertebrates, such as various butterfly species and the rufous grasshopper. It offers panoramic views over the valley and is also home to birds like blackcap and willow warbler.

Name: Polzeath Coast
Description: Pentire, near Polzeath on the North Cornwall coast, offers dramatic clifftop walks and views across the Atlantic. This headland includes diverse habitats from maritime heathland to secluded coves, supporting varied coastal wildlife.

Name: Poole Hill
Description: Poole Hill is a small nature reserve near Flax Bourton, North Somerset. Ancient woodland with mature oak and hazel supports diverse fungi and invertebrates. Adjacent limestone grassland supports varied flora. Public access is available.

Name: Poolhay Meadows
Description: Poolhay Meadows, managed by Worcestershire Wildlife Trust, is a reserve of species-rich lowland hay meadows near Corse Lawn, Tewkesbury. It is home to diverse flora including great burnet, meadow thistle, lady's smock, ragged robin, and green-winged orchids, providing important habitats for wildlife.

Name: Portbury Wharf
Description: Portbury Wharf Nature Reserve, a key coastal wetland in North Somerset, features salt marsh, open water, and reedbeds. It supports diverse bird species, including waterfowl and waders. The reserve offers walking trails and bird hides.

Name: Porth y Swnt
Description: Porth y Swnt is a National Trust visitor centre in Aberdaron, Gwynedd, on the Llyn Peninsula. It serves as an interpretive hub, detailing the area's geology, wildlife, and cultural heritage through displays. The centre offers visitor information.

Name: Porthdinllaen
Description: Porthdinllaen, a fishing village on the Llŷn Peninsula, is managed by the National Trust. Its coastal waters host extensive seagrass meadows, vital for marine biodiversity. Efforts focus on protecting and restoring these habitats, engaging local communities and visitors in conservation.

Name: Portmore Lough
Description: Portmore Lough is an important area of lowland wet grassland with open water, reedbeds and scrub, supporting many wetland birds. Significant for wintering wildfowl and breeding waders, it also hosts a range of invertebrates and plant species.

Name: Portstewart Strand
Description: Portstewart Strand is a two-mile sandy beach and dune system in County Londonderry, Northern Ireland, managed by the National Trust. It supports diverse wildlife, including a range of birds and flora, and offers access to the River Bann estuary.

Name: Pot of Doan
Description: Pot of Doan is a peatland restoration site in the Mourne Mountains, Northern Ireland. It is part of the PEATLANDS+ cross-border project, led by Ulster Wildlife. This initiative restores degraded peatlands to enhance carbon storage, biodiversity, and water quality.

Name: Potterland Wood
Description: Potterland Wood is a small ancient woodland covering 2.4 hectares near Arnold, Nottinghamshire. It features oak, ash, and hazel trees, with a rich ground flora including bluebell and wood anemone. This woodland supports diverse wildlife, including various bird species and invertebrates, providing a valuable habitat.

Name: Poulter Country Park
Description: Poulter Country Park is a reclaimed colliery site offering walking trails, wildlife habitats, and historical remnants. Located near Bolsover, it features diverse woodlands, wetlands, and open grassland areas, providing recreational and educational opportunities.

Name: Pound Farm
Description: Pound Farm is a diverse Woodland Trust site in Suffolk, located between Great Glenham and Framlingham. This 90-hectare woodland features a mix of young and ancient woodland, wide rides, wildflower meadows, and five ponds, offering splendid views and diverse habitats for wildlife.

Name: Pound Wood
Description: Pound Wood is an ancient woodland nature reserve in Essex, known for its diverse flora and fauna. It features mature hornbeam and oak trees, bluebells, and a variety of butterflies and bird species like nightingales. Managed for biodiversity.

Name: Prawle Point
Description: Prawle Point is Devon's southernmost point, offering expansive coastal views and diverse wildlife. It features a historic coastguard station, serving as a lookout for passing ships. The area is known for its rugged cliffs, rare migrating birds, and wildflowers, providing a habitat for many species.

Name: Prees Heath
Description: Prees Heath is a crucial refuge for the rare silver-studded blue butterfly, one of only three sites in England. This lowland heathland, part of a former WWII airfield, supports diverse flora and fauna, including rare birds and reptiles. Managed for conservation.

Name: Prehen Wood
Description: Prehen Wood, an ancient woodland overlooking the River Foyle, is a crucial urban green space in Derry/Londonderry. It hosts a rich diversity of native trees including oak, ash, and hazel, supporting various wildlife species. Managed for conservation and public access.

Name: Pressmennan Wood
Description: Pressmennan Wood is an 86-hectare (212-acre) ancient woodland in East Lothian, managed by the Woodland Trust. It is known for its veteran trees, diverse flora and fauna including deer, owls, otters, and bats, and overlooks Pressmennan Lake. The wood features an extensive network of paths, including a child-friendly 'Glingbobs and Tootflits' sculpture trail.

Name: Priest Hill
Description: Priest Hill, a former playing field site near Epsom, is managed by Surrey Wildlife Trust. It comprises restored chalk grassland, wildflower meadows, scrub, and ponds, supporting diverse wildlife including rare plants, butterflies, and birds. It offers public access for walking.

Name: Priestcliffe Lees
Description: Priestcliffe Lees is a limestone grassland and scrub nature reserve located in the Wye Valley. It supports a diverse flora, including several orchid species and the rare dark red helleborine. Butterflies, such as the northern brown argus and small pearl-bordered fritillary, thrive here. The site is actively managed for biodiversity.

Name: Priestclose Wood
Description: Priestclose Wood is an ancient semi-natural woodland nature reserve near Prudhoe, Northumberland. Managed by Northumberland Wildlife Trust, it features oak, birch, and hazel trees. The site supports diverse flora like bluebells and wood anemones, and various bird species. Walking trails are present.

Name: Priestley Wood
Description: Priestley Wood is an ancient woodland, once part of the deer park of Priestley House. It features a diverse range of tree species, including oak, ash, and field maple, along with a rich ground flora. Public access is available.

Name: Prince's Community Wood
Description: Prince's Community Wood is a small community woodland within The National Forest, near Tatenhill, Staffordshire. The site was formerly used for sand and gravel extraction and was bought by Tatenhill and Rangemore Parish Council in 2013. Planting of 10,000 trees was completed in 2014, and it now offers broadleaf trees, ponds, and open areas, supporting diverse wildlife habitats and providing recreational opportunities for visitors.

Name: Prior Park Landscape Garden
Description: Prior Park Landscape Garden is an 18th-century landscape garden overlooking Bath. Created by Ralph Allen with advice from Alexander Pope and Capability Brown, it features a Palladian Bridge, serpentine lake, and historic garden buildings. The National Trust cares for the garden.

Name: Prior's Coppice
Description: Prior's Coppice is a 13.5-hectare ancient woodland in Leicestershire, managed for biodiversity. It features mature oak, ash, and hazel coppice, supporting diverse flora and fauna. The site is a Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust nature reserve.

Name: Prior's Wood
Description: Prior's Wood is an ancient woodland near Portbury known for its seasonal bluebells. The site features mature trees, diverse ground flora, and a stream, providing habitat for various wildlife species including dormice and birds.

Name: Prisk Wood
Description: Prisk Wood is a 35-hectare Gwent Wildlife Trust reserve in the Wye Valley Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. This ancient semi-natural woodland features a rich diversity of mosses, lichens, and ferns. It provides a vital habitat for local wildlife within its mosaic of woodland ecosystems.

Name: Prospect Fields
Description: Prospect Fields is a 6.7 hectare nature reserve near Pitney in Somerset. The site protects species-rich grassland, providing habitats for a variety of wildflowers and insects. Traditional hay meadow management maintains biodiversity.

Name: Pryor's Wood
Description: Pryor's Wood is an ancient woodland in Hertfordshire, featuring mature oak, hornbeam, and hazel coppice. The reserve supports diverse flora including bluebells, wood anemones, and wild daffodils. Birdlife thrives here, alongside various butterfly species.

Name: Pumlumon Project
Description: The Pumlumon Project covers 40,000 hectares in mid-Wales, working to restore peatlands, improve water quality, and enhance wildlife habitats. It supports sustainable farming practices, aiming to increase biodiversity and carbon storage within the landscape.

Name: Purple Horizons
Description: Purple Horizons is a collaborative Nature Recovery Project led by Natural England, working with partners including Walsall Council, Lichfield Council, Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust, and Staffordshire Wildlife Trust. It aims to restore and connect 10,000 hectares of heathland, wetland, woodland, and grassland across the West Midlands, linking Sutton Park National Nature Reserve and Cannock Chase Special Area of Conservation, to enhance biodiversity and landscape resilience.

Name: Purwell Ninesprings
Description: Purwell Ninesprings is a mosaic of grassland, scrub, and wetland habitats on the northern edge of Hitchin, Hertfordshire. The site features the source of the River Purwell, emerging from chalk springs.

Name: Putney Heath
Description: Putney Heath is a significant open space in South West London, managed by the Wimbledon and Putney Commons Conservators. It comprises heathland, woodland, and ponds, providing public access for recreation and supporting diverse wildlife within a protected landscape.

Name: Puttenham Common
Description: Puttenham Common is a large nature reserve near Guildford, owned and managed by Hampton Estate, with Surrey County Council managing public access and car parks. Surrey Wildlife Trust is also involved in conservation projects on the common. It features extensive lowland heath, woodland, ponds, and acidic grassland, supporting diverse flora and fauna, including rare species. Visitors can explore numerous walking trails and observe various bird species and invertebrates.

Name: Puxton Moor
Description: Puxton Moor is a Somerset wetland reserve, managed by Avon Wildlife Trust. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a Site of Nature Conservation Interest (SNCI), covering nearly 70 hectares of pasture land networked with species-rich rhynes. These rhynes support diverse wetland plants like frogbit and rootless duckweed, and scarce invertebrates such as hairy dragonfly and water scorpion. The site provides habitat for breeding wading birds like skylark, reed and sedge warblers, and water voles. Public access is available via designated footpaths.

Name: Pwllywrach
Description: Pwllywrach Nature Reserve, near Colwinston in the Vale of Glamorgan, protects a steep-sided woodland valley. The reserve features ancient trees, a stream, and a notable waterfall. It is a vital habitat for various wildlife, including a nationally important population of dormice.

Name: Pymmes Brook
Description: Thames21 is restoring Pymmes Brook, a highly urbanised river in Enfield. Work focuses on improving river habitats, water quality, and biodiversity through various interventions like natural river features and riparian planting. The project enhances local green spaces.

Name: Pymmes Park
Description: Pymmes Park in Lower Edmonton, Enfield, is a Green Flag Award-winning urban park. It features a restored lake and wetland habitat, play areas, sports facilities, and a café. The park is open 24/7. The Friends of Pymmes Park actively run community events and regular volunteering days.

Name: Quants
Description: Quants reserve near Pitminster in the Blackdown Hills features ancient semi-natural woodland and species-rich unimproved grassland. It supports dormice, bats, butterflies, and various birds like marsh tit and willow warbler. The site maintains a mixed habitat mosaic.

Name: Quarr Community Woodland
Description: Quarr Community Woodland is a Local Nature Reserve bordering the A30 in Sherborne. Spanning 2.5 hectares, it provides diverse wildlife habitats and recreational space. Managed by Sherborne Town Council, the site offers public access.

Name: Quarry Bank & Styal Estate
Description: Quarry Bank is a significant industrial heritage site featuring an 18th-century cotton mill, gardens, and woodlands within the Bollin Valley. The estate includes worker's cottages, the apprentice house, and extensive natural landscapes.

Name: Quarry Banks
Description: Quarry Banks Allan Wilson Memorial Reserve is a peaceful nature reserve near Cumwhinton, Carlisle, Cumbria. In spring the woodland is carpeted with flowers and the air is full of bird song. The meadow flowers attract butterflies in the summer, including ringlet and large skipper. The reserve supports wildflowers like bluebells, wood anemone, wood-sorrel, and violets, and over 60 species of breeding birds.

Name: Quarry Hangers
Description: Quarry Hangers is a steep chalk escarpment with woodland and open grassland, managed by Surrey Wildlife Trust. It supports diverse flora, including orchids and insects like the rare Adonis blue butterfly. It offers habitat for birds such as nightingales and various fungi species.

Name: Queen Elizabeth Country Park
Description: Queen Elizabeth Country Park sits within the South Downs National Park, offering vast woodlands, walking, and cycling trails. The park includes an adventure playground and a visitor centre. It preserves diverse habitats, from chalk grassland to mature beech hangers.

Name: Queen's Park
Description: Queen's Park is a Grade II listed historic park in north west London, managed by the City of London Corporation. It features formal gardens, woodlands, ornamental ponds, and sports facilities. The park also includes a children's playground, cafe, and a bandstand. It has received Green Flag status.

Name: Queendown Warren
Description: Queendown Warren is a 76.5-hectare Kent Wildlife Trust nature reserve located on the North Downs, south-east of Rainham in Kent. It is designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), a Local Nature Reserve, and a Special Area of Conservation. The reserve comprises ancient chalk grassland, scrub, open pasture, and woodland, supporting a diverse array of wildflowers, insects, and birds. It is particularly renowned for its ten species of orchids, including the Early Spider Orchid, and rare butterflies like the reintroduced Adonis Blue. Visitors can explore various walking trails, with access from the car park on Warren Lane.

Name: Queensbury Park
Description: Queensbury Park, in Harrow, is a site for river habitat improvements along Kenton Brook. The project engages local residents and schools in environmental activities, enhancing biodiversity and waterway health.

Name: Queenswood Country Park & Arboretum
Description: Queenswood Country Park & Arboretum is a nationally important arboretum and ancient woodland, designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). It features a significant collection of over 1,200 rare and exotic trees within its 47-acre arboretum, surrounded by 123 acres of ancient woodland. The site offers expansive views, a visitor centre, cafe, gift shop, woodland playground, and various walking trails, including a Gruffalo trail. It is managed by Herefordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Quoit Heathland
Description: Quoit Heathland is a 9-hectare nature reserve located south of St Columb Major, near Newquay, Cornwall. It protects a complex mosaic of wet and dry heath, scrub, bogs, grasslands, and open water. The reserve provides habitat for species such as reed buntings and otters, and is managed for wildlife.

Name: Rackenford and Knowstone Moors
Description: Rackenford and Knowstone Moors, a complex of Culm grassland and heathland in Mid Devon, features wet rush pasture and mire. It supports rare plants like wavy St John's-wort and marsh violet. The site provides a habitat for various bird species and butterflies.

Name: Railway Fields
Description: Railway Fields is a local nature reserve in Haringey, North London, managed by The Conservation Volunteers. This former railway goods yard now boasts diverse habitats including woodland, meadow, and ponds, supporting various wildlife species. It serves as a vital urban green space and educational resource.

Name: Raincliffe Woods
Description: Raincliffe Woods is a 200-hectare woodland site near Scarborough, North Yorkshire. It comprises three distinct woodlands: Raincliffe, Forge Valley, and Lady Edith's. The site offers diverse habitats and recreational paths. It is managed for biodiversity, recreation, and education.

Name: Rainham Hall
Description: Rainham Hall, a Georgian merchant's house built in 1729 in east London, offers insights into its past residents. The site features a historic house, a community garden, and a dedicated wildlife garden for visitors to explore.

Name: Rainton Meadows
Description: Rainton Meadows is a nature reserve managed by Durham Wildlife Trust, transformed from an open cast coal mine. It features wetlands, grasslands, and woodlands, offering walking trails, a visitor centre, and a cafe.

Name: Rainworth Heath
Description: Rainworth Heath, a Nottinghamshire SSSI, is a remnant of Sherwood Forest. It features heathland, acid grassland, and woodland, supporting rare plants, diverse invertebrates, and ground-nesting birds like woodlark and nightjar.

Name: Rainworth Heath
Description: Rainworth Heath is a vital heathland remnant in Nottinghamshire, showcasing both dry and wet heath, acid grassland, and woodland. It hosts birch, oak, foxglove, heather, and birds like nightjar and woodlark. Managed by Nottinghamshire Wildlife Trust, it is one of the last remaining areas of heathland in the county.

Name: Raisby Hill Grassland
Description: Raisby Hill Grassland in County Durham is a species-rich magnesian limestone grassland, formerly a quarry. It features dry grassland, scrub, and woodland habitats, supporting diverse wildflowers and insects. Rare species are present. The site is managed for biodiversity.

Name: Rammey Marsh
Description: Rammey Marsh is a significant area of open space in Enfield, bordering the River Lee Navigation. This marshland habitat supports diverse flora and fauna, including water voles and kingfishers. It offers walking routes and connects to the wider Lee Valley Regional Park.

Name: Ramsbury Meadow
Description: Ramsbury Meadow is a species-rich wet grassland reserve on the River Kennet floodplain. Managed for biodiversity, it supports water voles, otters, and wetland birds. Delicate plants like marsh marigold thrive, enhancing its ecological value.

Name: Ramsden Corner
Description: Ramsden Corner is a small secluded reserve featuring acidic grassland, woodland, and scrub on clay and sand. Its ground flora includes heather, bilberry, bracken, sheep's sorrel, bent grasses, heath bedstraw, sweet vernal-grass, cat's ear, and tormentil. The site provides a habitat for various woodland birds, including redpoll, brambling, and grasshopper warbler.

Name: Ramsey Heights Countryside Centre
Description: Ramsey Heights Countryside Centre, run by Wildlife Trust BCN, is the visitor centre for the Great Fen. It features diverse habitats, nature trails, and a bird hide overlooking wet grassland, serving as a key starting point for exploring the wider Great Fen.

Name: Ramsey Island
Description: Ramsey Island, off the Pembrokeshire coast, is a rugged RSPB reserve. It provides vital habitat for grey seals, seabirds, and peregrine falcons. Its dramatic cliffs and coastline support diverse marine and avian life, managed for conservation.

Name: Ramsey Island - Grassland for Chough
Description: Ramsey Island is an offshore Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Wales, managed by RSPB. Its diverse habitats support grey seals, choughs, peregrines, and ravens. Grasslands are vital for choughs, with breeding occurring on cliffs. It is a significant wildlife haven.

Name: Ranscombe Farm
Description: Ranscombe Farm Reserve, located on the North Downs in Kent, is one of Kent's largest ancient woodlands and a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). It features globally important plantlife and wildlife, offering miles of footpaths through diverse habitats.

Name: Ranscombe Farm Reserve
Description: Ranscombe Farm Reserve is Plantlife's largest nature reserve in England, located near Cuxton in Kent. It is a significant site for rare arable wildflowers and ancient woodland, offering diverse habitats including chalk grassland and orchards. The reserve is part of the North Kent Woods and Downs National Nature Reserve and is managed by Plantlife in partnership with Medway Council and a tenant farmer, supporting important conservation efforts for its unique flora and fauna.

Name: Ranworth Broad and Marshes
Description: Ranworth Broad and Marshes is a Norfolk Wildlife Trust reserve within the Broads National Park. It features open water, extensive reedbeds, and wet woodland. A floating visitor centre provides views of diverse wildlife, including overwintering wildfowl and rare insects.

Name: Rathlin Island - Kebble NNR
Description: Rathlin Island's Kebble NNR hosts significant seabird colonies, including puffins and guillemots, on its dramatic cliffs. The reserve features unique cliff-top flora, providing vital nesting habitats and is a key ecological site in Northern Ireland.

Name: Rauceby Warren
Description: Rauceby Warren, a former RAF bomb store, is a Lincolnshire grassland and woodland site. It supports diverse invertebrates like marbled white butterflies and six-spot burnet moths. Rare flora includes fragrant, common spotted, and bee orchids in the grassland areas.

Name: Raveley Wood
Description: Raveley Wood is an ancient woodland in Cambridgeshire, located near Huntingdon. It features coppiced hazel and hornbeam alongside mature oak trees. The wood is a habitat for dormice and various butterfly species, with seasonal displays of wildflowers in spring and fungi in autumn.

Name: Ravensroost Wood
Description: Ravensroost Wood is an ancient oak-hazel coppice woodland in Wiltshire, supporting a rich diversity of wildlife including dormice, badgers, and numerous bird species. The reserve features meadows, ponds, and traditional management practices.

Name: Red Cross Garden
Description: Red Cross Garden is a historic Victorian garden established by Octavia Hill in 1887, located in Southwark, London. It features a tranquil pond, mature trees, and flowerbeds, offering a peaceful green space. The garden is open daily to the public for relaxation and community engagement.

Name: Red Hill
Description: Red Hill, a Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust nature reserve in the Lincolnshire Wolds, features ancient woodland and species-rich chalk grassland. It supports notable plants like orchids and scarce insects. The site offers walking trails and provides important habitat for wildlife.

Name: Red House Montgomery Canal Wetland
Description: Red House is a small wetland nature reserve adjacent to the Montgomery Canal in Powys. It features marshy grassland, reedbed, and wet woodland habitats, supporting diverse wildlife including amphibians, insects, and birds. The site is managed for biodiversity.

Name: Red Moor
Description: Red Moor, a Cornwall Wildlife Trust reserve, is a nationally important site in a sheltered valley southwest of Bodmin. It features ancient woodland, open heath, and wet mires formed on former china clay workings, supporting diverse wildlife, including the marsh fritillary butterfly.

Name: Red Moss of Netherley
Description: Red Moss of Netherley is a raised bog south-west of Stonehaven, Aberdeenshire. It supports rare flora, including sphagnum mosses, cotton-grass, and heather. The site is a nature reserve managed for its ecological significance.

Name: Red River Loscoe Nature Reserve
Description: Red River Loscoe Local Nature Reserve is an important site for nature conservation in north Amber Valley. Owned by Heanor & Loscoe Town Council, the 1.3-hectare site offers grassland, wetland, and woodland habitats. Accessible paths welcome walkers and nature enthusiasts.

Name: Red Rocks Marsh
Description: Red Rocks Marsh is a small coastal nature reserve on the Wirral Peninsula, featuring sand dunes, reedbeds, saltmarsh, and adjacent beach habitats. It supports diverse bird species like waders and terns, serving as an important breeding ground, with over 200 species recorded. It is also home to the only breeding colony of rare Natterjack toads on the Wirral Peninsula. Unique saline-adapted plants also thrive here.

Name: Reddish Vale Country Park
Description: Reddish Vale Country Park spans 161 hectares in Stockport, Greater Manchester. It features woodlands, meadows, and riverside paths along the River Tame. The park offers walking, cycling, and horse riding, and is home to diverse wildlife and historical railway structures.

Name: Redesdale Forest
Description: Redesdale Forest lies within Northumberland, forming part of the expansive Border Forest Park managed by Forestry England. It is a working forest landscape situated south-east of Kielder Water and Forest Park, near the village of Otterburn, offering diverse habitats.

Name: Redesdale Peatland Pipeline
Description: The Redesdale Peatland Pipeline is a pilot project restoring degraded peatland in Northumberland, with key efforts focused on sites such as Whitelee Moor National Nature Reserve. It is a collaboration between Northumberland National Park Authority and Northumbrian Water. The 2023/24 phase involves contractors making significant progress on the restoration efforts.

Name: Redgrave and Lopham Fen
Description: Redgrave and Lopham Fen is England's largest valley fen, managed by Suffolk Wildlife Trust. It hosts nationally rare species, including the fen raft spider. Boardwalks and hides facilitate visitor access to diverse wetland habitats.

Name: Redlake Cottage Meadows
Description: Redlake Cottage Meadows is a nature reserve managed by Cornwall Wildlife Trust, located near Lostwithiel in Cornwall. It comprises unimproved damp meadowland and wet heath, forming part of the larger Redlake Meadows & Hoggs Moor SSSI. The reserve is nationally important for its rare flora, including heath lobelia, and supports the vulnerable marsh fritillary butterfly. It also features a well-preserved ancient field system.

Name: Rendlesham Forest
Description: Rendlesham Forest, near Woodbridge in Suffolk, is a large mixed woodland offering walking trails, cycle routes, and a popular UFO trail. The site is managed by Forestry England and provides a natural space for recreation, wildlife spotting, and family outdoor activities.

Name: Reston Scar
Description: Reston Scar, a limestone escarpment overlooking the Kentmere Valley, features diverse habitats including limestone grassland, heathland, and woodland, supporting wildflowers, butterflies, and birds. This natural area offers excellent views of the Cumbrian landscape.

Name: Rewe Mead
Description: Rewe Mead is a small, species-rich wet grassland nature reserve located near Thorne St Margaret, Somerset. It sits on the banks of the River Tone and features remnants of the Grand Western Canal. The reserve supports diverse wildflowers and grasses, providing habitat for various insects, including damselflies and dragonflies. It is managed by the Somerset Wildlife Trust to maintain its biodiversity.

Name: Reydon Wood
Description: Reydon Wood, a 16-hectare ancient woodland in Suffolk, hosts diverse trees and hazel coppice. Its rich ground flora includes bluebells, wood anemones, primroses, and early purple orchids. The site is home to various butterflies such as ringlets, gatekeeper, orange tip, and speckled wood. A circular path allows exploration.

Name: Rhos Cefn-bryn
Description: Rhos Cefn-bryn is a nature reserve in Carmarthenshire, south-west Wales, managed by The Wildlife Trust of South and West Wales. It consists of unimproved acid grassland, forming a 'rhos-like' pasture. This habitat supports diverse plant species including Purple Moor Grass, Cross-leaved Heath, Heather (Ling), Cotton Grass, Bog Asphodel, Bog Myrtle, Marsh Lousewort, and Devil's-bit Scabious. The reserve is notable for its thriving population of the endangered Marsh Fritillary butterfly, as well as other invertebrates like the Marbled White and Small Copper butterflies and the Six-spot Burnet moth. Dormice, Adders, Common Lizards, Meadow Pipits, Snipe, and Reed Buntings are also present.

Name: Rhos Fiddle
Description: Rhos Fiddle is a 24-hectare nature reserve on the Welsh border, managed by Shropshire Wildlife Trust.
