Traditionally managed as a hay meadow, it floods in winter and in spring supports a diverse array of wildflowers including fen violet, marsh marigold, meadow rue, ragged robin, great burnet, cowslip, milkwort, marsh valerian, adder's-tongue fern, pepper-saxifrage, green-winged orchids, and bee orchids. The site's neutral grassland habitat attracts diverse invertebrates, including dragonflies and damselflies from Soham Lode, and provides valuable habitat for birds such as wintering flocks of redwing and fieldfare.

Name: Solent Seascape Project
Description: The Solent Seascape Project restores vital marine habitats across the Solent, focusing on seagrass meadows and oyster reefs. The initiative enhances biodiversity, improves water quality, and involves scientific research and active restoration.

Name: Solsbury Hill
Description: Solsbury Hill is an Iron Age hillfort near Batheaston, overlooking Bath. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, known for its limestone grassland and diverse wildlife. The hill offers panoramic views of the Avon Valley.

Name: Sot's Hole
Description: Sot's Hole is a Local Nature Reserve in West Bromwich, West Midlands, covering 5.5 hectares of semi-ancient woodland. It features wet woodland, a stream, and a small pool, supporting diverse flora and fauna including bluebells in spring, water horsetail, and marsh thistle. The reserve is managed by Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council and links to Sandwell Valley Country Park.

Name: Sotby Meadows
Description: Sotby Meadows is a 32-hectare nature reserve near Wragby, managed by the Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust. It comprises species-rich damp and dry grassland habitats. The site supports diverse wildflowers and insects, with grazing used to maintain the habitat structure.

Name: Sourlie Wood
Description: Sourlie Wood is an attractive native woodland and wetland site near Irvine, North Ayrshire, developed on a derelict coal yard. It features mature oak, birch, and alder trees, with a rich ground flora including bluebells and ramsons. The site supports various bird species, invertebrates, and bats, and offers accessible paths.

Name: Souter Lighthouse & The Leas
Description: Souter Lighthouse, established 1871, was the first purpose-built for alternating electric current globally. Its red and white striped tower stands on a dramatic coastline between Tyne and Wear. The adjacent Leas features 3 miles of magnesian limestone cliffs and coastal grasslands, managed for wildlife and public access.

Name: South Efford Marsh
Description: South Efford Marsh is a tidal marshland at the mouth of the River Avon, South Devon. It is a haven for overwintering and passage wildfowl and waders, including avocet and curlew. The site offers footpaths and bird hides for observation.

Name: South Hill
Description: South Hill features unimproved calcareous grassland, scrub, and mature hedgerows. Managed by grazing, the site supports diverse butterflies, insects, and plant species including orchids. The reserve lies on Lower Lias Limestone and has been quarried in the past, leading to shallow soils that encourage a rich flora.

Name: South House Pavement
Description: South House Pavement is a species-rich limestone grassland and pavement site near Grassington in the Yorkshire Dales. It features rare plants like blue moor-grass and rigid brome. The reserve is managed to preserve its biodiversity and geological features, offering botanical interest.

Name: South Milton Sands
Description: South Milton Sands is a picturesque sandy beach on the South Devon coast, featuring an iconic rock arch and clear waters. Managed by the National Trust, the site offers coastal walks, rock pooling, and diverse marine life. It is dog-friendly all year.

Name: South Solway Mosses NNR
Description: South Solway Mosses NNR in Cumbria protects extensive lowland raised bog habitats like Wedholme Flow. This internationally important peatland ecosystem supports specialist wildlife. Managed by Natural England, it is a Ramsar site and SAC.

Name: South Swale National Nature Reserve
Description: The South Swale National Nature Reserve, managed by Kent Wildlife Trust, protects extensive coastal habitats including saltmarsh, mudflats, and shingle ridges. Located between Faversham and Whitstable in Kent, it is a vital site for numerous overwintering and migrating bird species, forming part of a wider Special Protection Area.

Name: South Swale Nature Reserve
Description: South Swale is a coastal nature reserve on the Isle of Sheppey, Kent, featuring grazing marsh, reedbeds, and tidal mudflats. It supports significant bird populations, including waders and wildfowl. Managed by Kent Wildlife Trust for wildlife conservation.

Name: South Walney
Description: South Walney Nature Reserve, near Barrow-in-Furness, Cumbria, hosts the county's only grey seal colony, visible year-round. On Walney Island, it supports diverse birdlife, including eider ducks. Public access is restricted in sensitive areas to protect wildlife.

Name: South Walsham Broad
Description: South Walsham Broad is a freshwater lake in the Norfolk Broads, split into two main sections. Known for its tranquil waters, it supports diverse birdlife and aquatic plants. The area is popular for boating and offers scenic walks.

Name: Southerscales
Description: Southerscales Nature Reserve, a nationally important limestone pavement, lies beneath Ingleborough in the Yorkshire Dales. Designated as an SSSI and SAC, its deep grikes shelter a rich variety of wildflowers, ferns, and mosses.

Name: Southfield Farm Marsh
Description: Southfield Farm Marsh is an 8.6-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Kettering, Northamptonshire. Approximately 2.8 hectares are managed as a nature reserve by the Wildlife Trust for Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Northamptonshire. This spring-fed marsh features a mosaic of wet grassland, scrub, and wetland habitats beside the River Ise. It supports diverse plant species, uncommon invertebrates, and notable wildlife including breeding waders, wintering wildfowl, otters, and various birds like reed bunting, sedge warbler, red kite, and buzzard.

Name: Southmoor
Description: Southmoor Nature Reserve is a small wetland mosaic south of Havant, Hampshire. It features ditches, ponds, reedbeds, and grassland habitats. The site supports various bird species, including snipe and water rail, alongside dragonflies and rare plants.

Name: Southrepps Common
Description: Southrepps Common is a Norfolk Wildlife Trust reserve featuring diverse habitats like wet woodland, fen, reedbed, and acidic grassland. It supports a variety of plant and animal species, including rare invertebrates and wildflowers. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Southwell Potwell Dyke Grasslands
Description: Southwell Potwell Dyke Grasslands is a 1.72-hectare species-rich grassland on the south-east edge of Southwell, Nottinghamshire. It is designated as a Local Nature Reserve and a Priority Habitat by Natural England, representing one of the last examples of traditionally managed neutral grassland in the county, featuring a diverse range of plant species and significant ecological value.

Name: Southwick Coast
Description: Southwick Coast is a rich mosaic of habitats in Dumfries and Galloway. It features saltmarsh, shingle banks, woodland, and coastal grassland. The site supports a variety of wildlife, including migrating birds, natterjack toads, and otters. It is managed for biodiversity conservation.

Name: Sow Dale
Description: Sow Dale is a dry valley nature reserve in the Lincolnshire Wolds, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. It features wildflower-rich grassland with cowslips and bee orchids. Diverse insect life, including dingy skipper butterflies, thrives. Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust manages the site.

Name: Spalford Warren
Description: Spalford Warren is a Nottinghamshire nature reserve and a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) designated for its rare sand-blown heath habitat. It also features open sand, acidic grassland, and woodland, including some conifer plantation. The reserve supports diverse invertebrates, such as solitary bees and wasps, and is home to common lizards and a varied bird community. Heathland flora thrives, and the site holds significant geological and conservation value.

Name: Sparham Pools
Description: Sparham Pools is a 12-hectare nature reserve near Lyng, Norfolk, comprising former gravel pits. It supports various water birds, woodlands, scrub, and grassland, providing habitat for diverse wildlife. The site is important for overwintering and breeding birds.

Name: Speke Hall
Description: Speke Hall is a rare Tudor manor house located near the River Mersey in Liverpool. The estate features ancient woodland, a garden, and a home farm. Visitors explore the preserved wattle and daub mansion.

Name: Spencer Road Wetlands
Description: Spencer Road Wetlands is a Local Nature Reserve in Mitcham, south London, created on former watercress production land. It features reed swamps, wet willow woodland (carr), sedge-beds, and ponds. The site supports diverse wildlife including amphibians, insects (such as twin-spotted wainscot and crescent moths), and birds (like grey heron, Eurasian reed warbler, and kingfisher), offering a valuable urban green space.

Name: Spendluffe Meadows
Description: Spendluffe Meadows is a former school playing field near Alford, transformed into a wildlife haven. The site features flower-rich grassland, a small orchard, and a pond, supporting diverse invertebrates and amphibians.

Name: Spey Bay
Description: Spey Bay is a coastal reserve at the mouth of the River Spey, featuring shingle beaches and rich marine life. It is a prime location for viewing bottlenose dolphins, ospreys, and other seabirds. The site is managed for wildlife conservation and offers a visitor centre.

Name: Spong Wood
Description: Spong Wood is an ancient woodland in Kent, managed by Kent Wildlife Trust. It features diverse tree species, including oak and hornbeam, supporting various wildlife. The site is notable for its seasonal wildflowers and offers walking trails.

Name: Spring Park
Description: Spring Park is a mature woodland in the London Borough of Bromley, managed by the City of London Corporation. It features ancient oak trees and diverse species, providing essential wildlife habitats. Public footpaths offer opportunities for walking and enjoying the natural environment.

Name: Springdale Farm
Description: Springdale Farm is a 42-hectare nature reserve near Usk, Gwent, managed by Gwent Wildlife Trust. This flagship site features a mosaic of wildflower meadows, ancient woodland, and ponds. Grazing maintains species-rich grasslands, supporting diverse wildlife. Visitors can explore waymarked trails with panoramic views.

Name: Springhill
Description: Springhill, a 17th-century plantation house, sits within ancient parkland and woodland in County Londonderry. The estate features mature trees, open lawns, and waymarked walking trails. The site offers insights into the region's heritage.

Name: Springwell Reedbed
Description: Springwell Reedbed, near Rickmansworth, is a 10-hectare nature reserve. It protects reedbed, marsh, wet woodland, and grassland, supporting various warblers and dragonflies. Public access is limited to a short track. Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust manage the site.

Name: Sprotbrough Flash
Description: Sprotbrough Flash nature reserve features open water, woodland, scrub, and grassland habitats. It supports diverse wildlife, including various bird species, butterflies, and dragonflies. Winter sees wildfowl arrivals, and summer brings a range of insects to the site.

Name: Spurn National Nature Reserve
Description: Spurn National Nature Reserve is a dynamic three-mile-long sand and shingle spit located in the Humber Estuary, Yorkshire. This unique landscape provides vital habitats for migratory birds, rare plants, and insects. It features mudflats, saltmarsh, and dunes.

Name: Spyway
Description: Spyway is a former stone quarry on Dorset's Isle of Purbeck, forming part of the Jurassic Coast World Heritage Site. It offers panoramic views towards St Aldhelm's Head and the English Channel, featuring ancient strip lynchets and wildflower meadows.

Name: Spyway
Description: Spyway is a limestone grassland near Langton Matravers on the Isle of Purbeck, Dorset. It supports diverse wildflowers, including orchids, and various butterflies. The site offers expansive views of the Jurassic Coast and is managed for its wildlife.

Name: St Abb's Head NNR
Description: St Abb’s Head is a designated National Nature Reserve, supporting one of mainland Scotland’s largest seabird colonies. Puffins, guillemots, razorbills, and kittiwakes nest on the 90m cliffs. The site features a lighthouse and nature reserve centre, offering panoramic coastal views and rich biodiversity.

Name: St Agnes & Gugh
Description: St Agnes and Gugh, two islands in the Isles of Scilly, were declared rat-free in 2016 following a successful eradication project. This initiative led to a dramatic increase in breeding Manx shearwater and storm petrel populations.

Name: St Agnes Head & Wheal Coates
Description: St Agnes Head, Cornwall, offers dramatic cliffs, coastal heathland, and significant mining heritage. Wheal Coates, a historic tin mine, stands prominently on the clifftops. The site offers striking views and extensive walks along the South West Coast Path.

Name: St Audries Wood
Description: St Audries Wood, also known as Deerpark, is a small, semi-natural ancient woodland located on the north end of the Quantock Ridge within the Quantock Hills National Landscape. It offers glorious coastal views over the Bristol Channel and across to Exmoor, featuring various paths for walking. The site is an important habitat for diverse wildlife.

Name: St Austell Bay
Description: St Austell Bay, a vital marine area in Cornwall, is a focus for the 'Tor to Shore' project. This initiative by Cornwall Wildlife Trust works to restore and protect marine habitats, including seagrass beds. It aims to enhance biodiversity and promote blue carbon sequestration, with significant community involvement.

Name: St Catherine's Hill
Description: St Catherine's Hill is a chalk downland nature reserve near Winchester, featuring an Iron Age hill fort, maze, and ancient chapel site. It supports diverse chalk grassland flowers, rare butterflies like the brown hairstreak, and birds. Managed in partnership by Hampshire & Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: St Clair's Meadow
Description: St Clair's Meadow is a grassland nature reserve situated on the banks of the River Meon near Soberton in Hampshire. It encompasses species-rich chalk grassland, traditional hay meadows, and diverse riverine habitats. Managed for biodiversity, it supports a variety of wildflowers and insects.

Name: St Cyrus NNR
Description: St Cyrus NNR is a stunning coastal reserve in Scotland, featuring cliffs, dunes, and beach, backed by important volcanic grasslands. It supports diverse wildlife, including nesting seabirds, rare wildflowers, and marine life.

Name: St Ebba's Beadnell
Description: St Ebba's Beadnell (Coastal Link) refers to a section of the Northumberland Coast managed by the National Trust, encompassing Beadnell Bay and the historic Lime Kilns near Beadnell village. This area offers public access to diverse coastal landscapes, scenic views, and opportunities for walking and exploring the natural environment.

Name: St Erth Pits
Description: St Erth Pits is a disused quarry site revealing a Pliocene shell deposit, offering significant geological and palaeontological interest. The reserve features wet woodland, marshland, and open water, supporting various wildlife.

Name: St Helen's
Description: St Helen's is a small rocky tidal island within the Isles of Scilly, an important breeding ground for seabirds like storm petrels and puffins. It hosts diverse plant species adapted to its harsh coastal environment and is managed for biodiversity.

Name: St James's Park - Duck Island
Description: Duck Island, within St James's Park, serves as a significant sanctuary for diverse waterfowl species, including pelicans. This central London location provides a vital habitat for various birds, fostering biodiversity in the urban environment.

Name: St Kilda NNR
Description: St Kilda is a remote archipelago 40 miles west of North Uist, within the Outer Hebrides. It comprises volcanic islands and sea stacks, hosting vast seabird colonies including puffins and gannets. Evacuated in 1930, the islands are a dual World Heritage Site, managed for its natural and cultural heritage.

Name: St Lawrence Field
Description: St Lawrence Field is a small arable field managed by the Hampshire & Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust with wildlife in mind. It supports rare cornfield flowers, a beetle bank, and flocks of farmland birds such as linnet and yellowhammer. The site is managed for arable weeds with cereals sown every autumn, providing valuable foraging opportunities. It is notably the only remaining site in the UK for the rare field cow-wheat, also known as 'poverty weed'.

Name: St Lawrence Undercliff Woods
Description: This unusual two hectare reserve is a sycamore and ash woodland growing at the foot of a rugged cliff. The woodland, a gift from Connie Pelham, is sheltered and south-facing, and the whole area is on the largest rotational landslip in Western Europe. It has an unusual 'double coastline' effect as the result of a massive cliff-slump, spectacular views out to sea, and hosts several species of bat.

Name: St Michael's Mount
Description: St Michael's Mount is a tidal island and castle in Mount's Bay, Cornwall. Managed by the National Trust and the St Aubyn family, it offers historic exploration of its castle, terraced gardens, and island village.

Name: Stackpole
Description: Stackpole Estate in Pembrokeshire, Wales, features a diverse landscape of golden beaches, woodlands, and lakes. This National Trust property is home to abundant wildlife, including otters, and offers various walking trails. Volunteers support conservation efforts.

Name: Staffhurst Wood
Description: Staffhurst Wood is ancient woodland in the Surrey Weald near Limpsfield. It features diverse tree species, a variety of ground flora including bluebells and wood anemones, and a pond that supports amphibians. The site is managed for biodiversity.

Name: Staffordshire & Worcestershire Canal
Description: The Staffordshire & Worcestershire Canal is a 30-mile Green Flag site connecting Stourport-on-Severn to the River Trent. Designed by James Brindley, it flows through picturesque landscapes, rich heritage, and diverse wildlife habitats in Staffordshire and Worcestershire.

Name: Stainsby Wood
Description: Stainsby Wood is a remnant ancient woodland in Middlesbrough, featuring a diverse mix of tree species like oak, ash, and hazel. It supports a rich understorey and various wildlife, serving as a valuable green space for local communities.

Name: Stanborough Reedmarsh
Description: Stanborough Reedmarsh is a nature reserve in Welwyn Garden City, managed by Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust. It features reedbeds, scrub, and wet woodland, providing habitats for birds, insects, and amphibians. A boardwalk offers access to observe wildlife.

Name: Stanford Warren
Description: Stanford Warren is a 16.6-hectare nature reserve south of Stanford-le-Hope in Essex, managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust. This former gravel quarry is now one of the largest reedbeds in the county, bisected by the River Hassenbrook. It supports diverse birdlife including cettis, reed and sedge warblers, cuckoos, water rails, bearded tits, grey wagtails, and snipe. Reptiles and harvest mice are also present. It forms part of the Thameside Nature Discovery Park.

Name: Stanground Newt Ponds
Description: Stanground Newt Ponds in Peterborough, established 2005, features six ponds specifically for great crested newts, a protected species. The site includes grassland and scrub, providing diverse habitats. Volunteers manage the reserve.

Name: Stanground Wash
Description: Stanground Wash is a 70.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Farcet, Cambridgeshire. Part of the Lower Nene Valley SPA and Ramsar site, this wet grassland with shallow pools supports breeding waders and wintering wildfowl.

Name: Stanmore Marsh
Description: Stanmore Marsh is a 4.6-hectare Local Nature Reserve in Harrow, North London. It features a unique spring-fed mire, reedbeds, grassland, and woodland, forming the headwaters of the River Crane. The site is popular for walking, picnics, and includes a children's play area.

Name: Stanmore Marsh Wetlands
Description: Stanmore Marsh Wetlands, located in Harrow, is a thriving wetland habitat and Local Nature Reserve. The site has undergone significant transformation, with ongoing efforts to clear invasive species, plant native flora, and enhance public access through boardwalks. It supports diverse biodiversity.

Name: Stanton's Pit
Description: Stanton's Pit is an 8.05-hectare Local Nature Reserve in the South Kesteven district of Lincolnshire, situated between the villages of Little Bytham and Witham-on-the-Hill. Formerly a sand pit, it is now managed by the Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust and features open water, reedbeds, and damp grassland, supporting diverse bird species, amphibians, and insects. It is particularly noted for its ornithological interest, with over 50 species of birds recorded.

Name: Stanwick Lakes
Description: Stanwick Lakes is a 750-acre nature reserve and park in the Nene Valley, Northamptonshire. It features extensive walking and cycling paths, lakes for water sports, and play areas. The site supports diverse wildlife and offers educational programs.

Name: Staunton Quarry
Description: Staunton Quarry, a 2.5ha former limestone quarry, is now a nature reserve managed by Nottinghamshire Wildlife Trust. It features diverse grassland, scrub, woodland, and a well-vegetated water body. Unique for its Lias age strata, the calcareous rocks support a rare flora including species like brookweed, fen pondweed, and giant bellflower, alongside common spotted orchids and twayblade. The site is managed for wildlife conservation.

Name: Stave Hill Ecological Park
Description: Stave Hill Ecological Park is a 5.2-acre nature reserve in Rotherhithe, South East London. It features diverse habitats including woodlands, grasslands, and ponds. The park includes a re-created volcanic landscape and is managed by TCV.

Name: Staveley Woodlands
Description: Staveley Woodlands, near Staveley, Cumbria, features ancient woodland, wet woodland, and meadows. Managed by Cumbria Wildlife Trust, it supports diverse flora and fauna. Ongoing coppice restoration enhances biodiversity and improves habitats for local wildlife.

Name: Steep Holm Island
Description: Steep Holm Island is a rugged limestone island in the Bristol Channel, west of Weston-super-Mare. A designated SSSI and nature reserve, it hosts seabird colonies, rare plants, and historical remains. The Kenneth Allsop Memorial Trust manages the island to protect its unique wildlife and heritage.

Name: Stenhouse Wood
Description: Stenhouse Wood is a small, ancient woodland reserve near West Calder, managed by the Scottish Wildlife Trust. It features a diverse mix of broadleaf trees like oak, ash, and elm, supporting rich ground flora, including bluebells. The site provides valuable habitat for birds and invertebrates.

Name: Stiffkey Marshes
Description: Stiffkey Marshes is a National Trust site on the North Norfolk coast. It comprises saltmarsh, mudflats, and sand dunes, supporting diverse birdlife and unique coastal flora. The area is a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest, managed for conservation.

Name: Stiffkey Saltmarshes
Description: Stiffkey Saltmarshes are part of the Blakeney National Nature Reserve, a vast expanse of unspoilt saltmarshes and mudflats on the North Norfolk coast. Managed by the National Trust. A haven for diverse wildlife, including avocets and Brent geese. Visitors explore via public footpaths.

Name: Stiperstones Landscape National Nature Reserve
Description: The Stiperstones Landscape National Nature Reserve is a spectacular landscape of heather-clad moorland and jagged quartzite ridges in south Shropshire. It is home to rare plants like cloudberry and sundew, and birds such as red grouse, skylark, and stonechat. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and a National Nature Reserve, known for its unique geology and diverse upland habitats.

Name: Stirley Community Farm
Description: Stirley Community Farm, managed by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust, is a working farm and nature reserve near Huddersfield. It demonstrates sustainable farming practices and offers educational programmes. The site features meadows, woodlands, and ponds, supporting local wildlife.

Name: Stockbridge Down
Description: Stockbridge Down offers expansive views over the Test Valley in Hampshire. This chalk grassland is home to wildflowers, butterflies, and ancient barrows. Visitors can explore walking trails and observe local wildlife. The site is managed for conservation.

Name: Stocker's Lake
Description: Stocker's Lake is a gravel pit lake and nature reserve in Hertfordshire, managed by Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust. It features open water, reedbeds, and diverse woodland, supporting overwintering wildfowl and migrating birds. The site offers accessible trails and bird hides.

Name: Stocker's Lake
Description: Stocker's Lake is a large lake forming part of the Colne Valley Wetlands Site of Special Scientific Interest. Managed by Hertfordshire Wildlife Trust, it features reedbeds, marsh, and wet woodland. The site supports significant bird populations, including overwintering wildfowl and breeding birds, alongside otters.

Name: Stocking Springs Wood
Description: Stocking Springs Wood, a Local Wildlife Site, features ancient woodland with oak and hornbeam standards. Its diverse understorey supports seasonal wildflowers like bluebells and wood anemone, providing habitat for various bird species.

Name: Stocksmoor Common
Description: Stocksmoor Common is a nature reserve near Stocksmoor village in Kirklees, managed by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust. It features rough acid grassland, damp grassland, scrub, and woodland. The site is notable for its rich invertebrate life, including various butterfly species like the threatened Small Heath, and a range of birds such as tree pipit, linnet, and yellowhammer. A pond, dug in 1997, has been colonized by various invertebrates. The reserve offers walking paths and is a valuable example of unploughed, unimproved acid grassland habitat.

Name: Stockton Cutting & Tasker's Meadow
Description: Stockton Cutting & Tasker's Meadow is a nature reserve comprising ancient woodland, a wildflower meadow, and a disused railway cutting through limestone. It provides a habitat for diverse wildlife, including various bird species, wildflowers, and orchids. The site offers peaceful walks throughout the year. While historically managed by Warwickshire Wildlife Trust, parts of the reserve are now managed by Warwickshire County Council's Country Parks service.

Name: Stodmarsh National Nature Reserve
Description: Stodmarsh National Nature Reserve, located in the Stour Valley near Canterbury, Kent, is a unique wetland environment covering approximately 241-250 hectares. It is internationally recognized as a Ramsar site, Special Protection Area (SPA), and Special Area of Conservation (SAC) due to its extensive reedbeds (the largest in the South East of England), open water, wet grassland, alder woodland, and carr. The reserve supports diverse birdlife, including breeding marsh harriers, bearded tits, and wintering bitterns, as well as a variety of invertebrates, rare plants, and a strong population of water voles.

Name: Stoke Bruerne Brick Pits Nature Reserve
Description: Stoke Bruerne Brick Pits is a peaceful haven for wildlife next to the Grand Union Canal. This former brickworks site features a reed bed, rough and damp grassland, several ponds, and a redundant side arm of the canal, providing important habitats for diverse plant life, invertebrates, and various dragonfly species, including the white-legged damselfly.

Name: Stoke Common
Description: Stoke Common is a 100-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest and Special Area of Conservation in Buckinghamshire. It protects rare lowland heathland, part of the Chiltern commons, with diverse habitats. The City of London Corporation manages this biodiversity site.

Name: Stoke Ferry Fen
Description: Stoke Ferry Fen protects species-rich fen meadowland in Norfolk. It provides important habitat for rare plants like marsh-marigold and bog pimpernel, and insects including dragonflies, damselflies, and butterflies. This small reserve conserves a valuable wetland ecosystem.

Name: Stoke Point & Revelstoke Drive
Description: Stoke Point and Revelstoke Drive offer dramatic coastal views and clifftop paths in South Devon. This stretch, part of the South West Coast Path, is home to seabirds and rare plants. Visitors can enjoy a four-mile drive and explore various walking routes from the free car park.

Name: Stoke Wood
Description: Stoke Wood is an ancient woodland in Oxfordshire, near the village of Stoke Lyne. It offers gentle walking trails and is home to diverse wildlife including muntjac deer and birds. Historically part of Bernwood Forest, it features mature oak and beech trees.

Name: Stoke Wood End Quarter
Description: Stoke Wood End Quarter is an ancient woodland in Northamptonshire, part of a larger wood, and a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). The wood contains a great variety of plants due to its undisturbed nature, with a soil mainly composed of calcareous clay. Notable flora includes wood anemone, wood-sorrel, primrose, early-purple orchid, bluebell, dog's mercury, and the uncommon herb-Paris. In summer, enchanter's-nightshade, sanicle, meadowsweet, greater butterfly-orchid, and twayblade come into flower. Waterlogged areas support brooklime, wild angelica, wood-sedge, and various rush species. Oak and ash are the dominant trees, with abundant hazel and blackthorn, providing excellent habitat for small mammals. The reserve is rich in birdlife, with treecreepers, nuthatches, sparrowhawks, and tawny owls, and sunlit glades attract butterflies such as green-veined white, comma, small tortoiseshell, and skippers.

Name: Stonebarrow Hill
Description: Stonebarrow Hill, managed by the National Trust, is a prominent point on the Jurassic Coast in Dorset. It offers panoramic views and features heathland and grassland habitats supporting diverse wildlife. An accessible circular route is present.

Name: Stonefolds
Description: Stonefolds is a nature recovery site near Hadrian's Wall in Northumberland National Park. It focuses on restoring peatlands, woodlands, and floodplains. The site contributes to broader nature recovery efforts within the park, aiming to meet national net zero targets.

Name: Stonehill Down
Description: Stonehill Down is a 12-hectare nature reserve in Dorset, featuring species-rich chalk grassland. It supports various butterflies like the Adonis blue and chalkhill blue, alongside a range of orchids. The site offers panoramic views of the surrounding countryside.

Name: Stonepit Plantation
Description: Stonepit Plantation is a 2.4-hectare woodland and parkland site on a former abandoned quarry, owned by Nottinghamshire Wildlife Trust since 1983. It features diverse mature trees like oak, ash, and sycamore, some over 200 years old, supporting a rich ground flora. It is geologically significant as the most southerly exposure of magnesian limestone in Britain. Various bird species, including great spotted woodpecker, nuthatch, and treecreeper, are present. Paths provide public access from Houghton Drive, though they are not suitable for disabled access.

Name: Stonesby Quarry
Description: Stonesby Quarry is a disused limestone quarry, now a nature reserve in Leicestershire. Managed by LRWT, it features diverse grassland habitats supporting wildflowers, insects, and birds. The site offers public access for walks.

Name: Stoneycliffe Wood
Description: Stoneycliffe Wood Nature Reserve, managed by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust, is a semi-natural ancient woodland near Netherton, Wakefield. This stunning woodland features a meandering beck and is primarily composed of oak and birch, with veteran sweet chestnuts, alder, and willow in wetter areas. In spring, it boasts magnificent displays of bluebells and wild garlic. The reserve supports diverse wildlife, including all three species of woodpecker, treecreepers, chiffchaffs, and mammals such as foxes, voles, and stoats. Public footpaths allow visitors to explore the site, which is managed for conservation to protect older trees and enhance biodiversity.

Name: Storton's Pits
Description: Storton’s Pits is a former gravel extraction site, now a nature reserve located in Northampton. It features lakes, reedbeds, and grassland, supporting diverse waterfowl, invertebrates, and rare plants. The site is managed for wildlife conservation.

Name: Storton's Pits
Description: Storton's Pits is a former gravel quarry by the River Nene, now a wetland nature reserve in Northampton. It features open water, reedbeds, and varied habitats supporting diverse wildlife, including breeding birds and rare plants. Footpaths allow access.

Name: Stoughton Moor
Description: Stoughton Moor, managed by the National Trust, is an area near Dunstable Downs in Bedfordshire. It is part of the Chilterns landscape, contributing to local biodiversity. The Trust conserves its natural features, providing habitats for wildlife and opportunities for walking.

Name: Stourhead Estate
Description: Stourhead Estate, a 2,650-acre property in Wiltshire, features a Palladian house, world-famous landscape garden, and ancient woodlands. The site is at the source of the River Stour and undergoes active parkland restoration efforts.

Name: Stover Canal
Description: Stover Canal is a historic transport waterway bordered by wet woodland, fen, and unimproved grassland. The reserve supports diverse wetland plants, invertebrates, and breeding birds, offering a tranquil environment for wildlife. It is part of a wider nature reserve managed for biodiversity and conservation.

Name: Stowford Moor
Description: Stowford Moor, a Devon Wildlife Trust reserve near Bude, features wet and culm grassland habitats. It hosts diverse orchid populations, including Heath Spotted and Greater Butterfly-orchid, providing crucial wetland and grassland ecosystems.

Name: Strangford Lough
Description: Strangford Lough, Northern Ireland, is a large tidal inlet managed by the National Trust. It supports diverse marine and coastal habitats, including mudflats, salt marshes, and islands. A vital overwintering site for brent geese and home to common seals, it is a protected area.

Name: Stratford-upon-Avon Local Nature Reserve
Description: Stratford-upon-Avon Local Nature Reserve is a 71-acre site in Stratford-upon-Avon, designated in 2023. It is part of The Stratford Riverside Project, creating a green corridor between Fisherman's Car Park and Lucy's Mill Bridge. The reserve features diverse habitats including riverbanks, meadow grassland, reedbeds, and wetlands, offering opportunities to view wildlife such as deer, kingfishers, and otters. It is managed in partnership by Stratford-on-Avon District Council and Stratford Town Trust.

Name: Strawberry Banks
Description: Strawberry Banks is a 5.06-hectare (12.5-acre) biological Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Gloucestershire. Managed by Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust, it protects a rare oolitic limestone grassland habitat supporting diverse wildflowers, including orchids, and important insect populations like the marsh fritillary butterfly and the rare oil beetle Meloe rugosus. The site features steep slopes and is part of Stroud's Golden Valley.

Name: Strawberry Hill
Description: Strawberry Hill is a 150-hectare rewilded site in Bedfordshire, near Knotting Green. Once arable fields, it has transformed into a thriving mosaic of grassland, scrub, and young woodland, providing a haven for diverse wildlife including nightingales, turtle doves, linnets, badgers, harvest mice, marbled white butterflies, and various orchids. The site is managed by The Wildlife Trust BCN for its biodiversity and is currently being developed for public access.

Name: Strawberry Hill Heath
Description: Strawberry Hill Heath is a small remnant of heathland and grassland in Nottinghamshire. It supports a mix of acid grassland, heather, and birch scrub, providing habitat for various insects and birds. The site is a local wildlife site.

Name: Street Heath
Description: Street Heath is a lowland raised bog in Somerset, managed by Somerset Wildlife Trust. It supports diverse flora and fauna, including rare bog plants and invertebrates. Boardwalks provide access for visitors.

Name: Strensall Common
Description: Strensall Common is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, one of Yorkshire's last lowland heathland fragments. Managed by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust, it supports nationally rare plants and animals, including the emperor moth and raft spider. Parts of the common are also used by the Ministry of Defence.

Name: Stretton Gap
Description: Stretton Gap is a Shropshire Wildlife Trust nature reserve located on the eastern slopes of the Long Mynd, near Church Stretton. This species-rich grassland supports a variety of invertebrates, birds, and wildflowers, maintained through grazing by Longhorn cattle.

Name: Stringer's Common
Description: Stringer's Common in Surrey, near Worplesdon, combines heathland, woodland, and acid grassland. A remnant of a larger historic heathland, it supports species such as woodlark, tree pipit, and Dartford warbler. Management includes grazing and scrub removal.

Name: Studland Bay
Description: Studland Bay offers a 4-mile stretch of golden sand and heathland in Dorset, managed by the National Trust. It supports diverse wildlife, including all six native reptile species, and is a popular destination for nature walks, water sports, and family beach visits.

Name: Sturts East
Description: Sturts East is a 3.7-hectare nature reserve in Herefordshire, featuring unimproved grassland, wetland, and woodland. It supports diverse wildflowers, insects, and bird species. Managed by grazing, the reserve maintains rich biodiversity.

Name: Sturts North
Description: Sturts North is a wet meadow and fen habitat located in the River Wye floodplain near Letton, Herefordshire, forming part of the larger Sturts Nature Reserve. It is designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and features diverse wetland plants, sedges, rushes, and supports a rich variety of insects and birds. The reserve is managed to enhance biodiversity and maintain its unique waterlogged environment, including numerous ponds.

Name: Sumburgh Head
Description: Sumburgh Head is a nature reserve and lighthouse at the southern tip of mainland Shetland. It is a key breeding site for seabirds including puffins, guillemots, razorbills, and kittiwakes. The site offers panoramic views and an accessible visitor centre.

Name: Summer Leys
Description: Summer Leys is a mature Northamptonshire nature reserve, a former gravel pit. It features open water, reedbeds, grasslands, and wet woodlands. Supporting diverse wildlife, especially birds, it is an SSSI and popular for birdwatching.

Name: Summerseat Nature Reserve
Description: Summerseat Nature Reserve is a restored former railway goods yard now functioning as a vital woodland and wetland habitat. Situated near the River Irwell, it features ponds, wildflower meadows, and mature trees, supporting diverse local wildlife. Visitors can enjoy quiet accessible trails.

Name: Sunnybank
Description: Sunnybank is an urban nature park in north Sheffield, featuring ancient woodland, meadows, and a community orchard. Managed by Sheffield & Rotherham Wildlife Trust, it provides a valuable green space for wildlife and local residents. Bluebells carpet Longley Wood in spring.

Name: Surfleet Lows
Description: Surfleet Lows is a remnant of old grassland, historically used for salt making, with old salt pans still visible. It is a low-lying site subject to winter flooding, supporting salt and brackish marsh species due to high salinity. The reserve also features wet woodland with willows and alders, blending into a small reed bed. It is home to varied aquatic invertebrates and supports a rich birdlife, including wintering snipe, redshank, mallard, and teal, and summer reed warblers. The meadow is grazed by cattle to maintain its floristic interest. Managed by Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Sutcliffe Park
Description: Sutcliffe Park, located in Greenwich, is a significant greenspace incorporating a re-naturalised section of the River Quaggy. It forms a key part of flood alleviation and biodiversity enhancement projects, encouraging natural habitats and was designated a Local Nature Reserve in 2006.

Name: Sutton & Hollesley Heaths
Description: Sutton & Hollesley Heaths, a significant Sandlings heathland in Suffolk, features fragmented heathland, acid grassland, and woodland. It provides habitat for rare species including nightjar, woodlark, and silver-studded blue butterfly. Habitats are actively managed.

Name: Sutton Fen
Description: Sutton Fen, an RSPB reserve in the Norfolk Broads, is a secluded and largely inaccessible wilderness protecting diverse fenland habitats. It is nationally recognised for its special wildlife, supporting rare plants like the Fen Orchid, insects such as the Swallowtail butterfly, and birds like Bitterns, Marsh Harriers, and Cranes. It is one of the most important UK sites for water beetles and wetland plants, and visitors can observe its unique biodiversity and ongoing conservation efforts, often through guided events due to its restricted access.

Name: Sutton Hoo
Description: Sutton Hoo in Suffolk features Anglo-Saxon royal burial mounds, including the ship burial of an Anglo-Saxon king. The estate comprises woodland and heathland. An exhibition hall displays replica treasures and artefacts. The landscape offers various walking routes.

Name: Sutton's Fen
Description: Sutton's Fen is a relic of ancient fenland and marsh pasture. Fed by spring water, it supports diverse sedges, rushes, and grasses, attracting dragonflies, damselflies, and butterflies. Over 100 plant species thrive, including greater tussock-sedge and southern marsh-orchid. Roe deer and water voles inhabit the reserve.

Name: Swanpond Copse
Description: Swanpond Copse is an ancient woodland nature reserve near Petersfield. Managed by Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust, it features mature oaks, hazel coppice, and woodland flowers like bluebells. The site provides habitats for birds and small mammals.

Name: Swanvale
Description: Swanvale Nature Reserve in Falmouth, Cornwall, features a wooded valley and a freshwater lake. Managed by Cornwall Wildlife Trust, it supports diverse wildlife, including otters and many bird species. Public footpaths allow access for nature observation.

Name: Swanwick Lakes
Description: Swanwick Lakes Nature Reserve, managed by Hampshire & Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust, features diverse habitats including woodland, meadows, and lakes. This former clay pit supports a variety of wildlife and provides nature trails for visitors near Southampton.

Name: Sweeney Fen
Description: Sweeney Fen is a wetland site near Oswestry, Shropshire. It features diverse habitats including marshy grassland, reedbed, and wet woodland. The reserve supports a wide array of wildlife, notably various orchid species, insects, amphibians, and birds.

Name: Sweet Briar Marshes
Description: Sweet Briar Marshes is an urban wildlife haven in Norwich. It comprises 90 acres of wetlands and woodlands along the River Wensum. The site supports a diverse range of species, including water voles and otters, with significant wetland restoration efforts underway.

Name: Sweetings Meadow
Description: Sweetings Meadow is a small, species-rich grassland in Essex, formerly part of a larger area. It supports diverse wildflowers and insects, including various butterfly species. It is best visited in late spring and summer for its vibrant flora and fauna.

Name: Swell Wood
Description: Swell Wood is an ancient woodland and Coronation Meadow in Somerset. It hosts a significant heronry, numerous bat species, and many ancient trees. The reserve is managed for biodiversity and accessible via public footpaths.

Name: Swettenham Meadows
Description: Swettenham Meadows Nature Reserve, managed by Cheshire Wildlife Trust, is a 21.5-acre (8.6 ha) site in the picturesque Swettenham Valley, near the Swettenham Brook. It features a mosaic of habitats including species-rich grassland, ancient woodland, and ponds, supporting a diverse array of wildflowers, invertebrates (like 14 species of butterflies), amphibians, and birds such as kingfishers. Its species-rich grassland is particularly ecologically important, representing a rare habitat in Cheshire. The site is also used for conservation training and public enjoyment.

Name: Swettenham Valley
Description: Swettenham Valley, a Cheshire Wildlife Trust reserve, features varied habitats including woodland, meadows, and wetlands along the River Dane. It supports diverse wildlife like otters and kingfishers. The site offers walking trails and educational opportunities for visitors.

Name: Swift Valley
Description: Swift Valley Nature Reserve lies on the northern edge of Rugby, following the River Swift. The site features grassland, wetland, and woodland habitats, supporting diverse wildlife. A network of paths and boardwalks allows year-round exploration.

Name: Swift's Hill
Description: Swift's Hill Nature Reserve is an important example of limestone grassland, located near Slad. It supports diverse flora including cowslips, wild thyme, and orchids. The site offers panoramic views across the Slad Valley. Management includes grazing to maintain habitat diversity for wildflowers and insects.

Name: Swineshead & Spanoak Woods
Description: Ancient woodland and former parkland trees on clay soil near Swineshead. This site features a rich mix of ash, oak, and field maple, supporting diverse flora and fauna. Maintained by the Woodland Trust for public access and wildlife.

Name: Swinley Forest
Description: Swinley Forest, a Crown Estate woodland in Berkshire, is managed by Forestry England. It offers extensive trails for walking, cycling, and horse riding, and is known for its mountain biking routes. The forest spans 2,600 acres.

Name: Swinn Wood
Description: Swinn Wood is an ancient woodland located on the edge of the Lincolnshire Wolds near Aby. Considered one of the most significant ancient woodland sites in the county, it is likely a remnant of the original Wildwood. Acquired by the Trust in 2016, the woodland features a diverse mix of tree species including ash and oak with a hazel understorey. In spring, the woodland floor is carpeted with bluebells, wood anemone, and early purple orchids. Its seven ponds attract a variety of dragonflies and damselflies, such as migrant hawker and common darter.

Name: Swithland Wood
Description: Swithland Wood is a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a recently designated National Nature Reserve (NNR) in Leicestershire, East Midlands. This ancient woodland features historic slate quarries and diverse ecosystems. Owned and managed by Bradgate Park Trust, it offers significant habitats for wildlife and is popular for walks.

Name: Syderstone Common
Description: Syderstone Common is a 24-hectare nature reserve managed by Norfolk Wildlife Trust, featuring diverse habitats including grass heathland, seasonal ponds, and surrounding woodland. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, known for supporting rare fauna such as the nationally rare natterjack toad, great crested newts, and various bird species, offering significant conservation value in Norfolk.

Name: Sydlings Copse
Description: Sydlings Copse, near Headington, Oxford, is a small ancient woodland and nature reserve. It features diverse habitats including wildflower meadows, ponds, and fen. Known for its rich flora and fauna, including rare butterflies and orchids, it offers walking trails.

Name: Sydlings Copse
Description: Sydlings Copse is a diverse nature reserve featuring ancient woodland, calcareous grassland, and fen habitats. This site supports a rich array of flora and fauna, including rare orchids, butterflies, and invertebrates. It offers accessible paths for visitors to explore its varied ecosystems.

Name: Sywell Country Park
Description: Sywell Country Park is a Green Flag Award winning site in Northamptonshire. Built around a former Victorian reservoir, it provides habitat for diverse wildlife, including overwintering wildfowl. The park offers walking trails, bird hides, a play area, and a cafe for visitors.

Name: Tadnoll and Winfrith Heath
Description: Tadnoll and Winfrith Heath is a large nature reserve near Dorchester, Dorset, encompassing dry and wet heathland, bog, and ancient woodland. It supports rare species like the Dartford warbler and sand lizard, and all six native British reptiles. The site holds SSSI, SAC, and Ramsar designations.

Name: Taf Fechan
Description: Taf Fechan is a woodland reserve in the Brecon Beacons National Park, featuring a limestone gorge and a section of the river. A Site of Special Scientific Interest, it supports diverse flora and bird species such as dipper. Managed by Welsh Wildlife Trust.

Name: Tailby Meadow
Description: Tailby Meadow is a 4.9-hectare Local Nature Reserve in Desborough, Northamptonshire, managed by the Wildlife Trust BCN. This traditional hay meadow, situated in the valley of the River Ise, features a rich diversity of wildflowers and grasses, supporting various insect species including orange-tip butterflies and red-eyed damselflies. It is a tranquil spot for nature observation, with seasonal management including hay cutting. The meadow has not been ploughed for hundreds of years and artificial fertilisers have never been applied.

Name: Tailby Meadow
Description: Tailby Meadow is a species-rich grassland situated next to the River Ise in Northamptonshire. The site supports diverse wildflowers like ragged robin and great burnet, attracting many insects. Managed for conservation, it provides a vital habitat for local wildlife.

Name: Tailend Moss
Description: Tailend Moss is a lowland raised bog, an extremely rare and threatened habitat in Scotland. The reserve supports diverse bog plants including cotton grasses, cranberries, and sundews. It serves as a significant site for dragonflies and damselflies, particularly during July and August.

Name: Talybont Reservoir
Description: Talybont Reservoir, located in the Brecon Beacons National Park, is a significant water body within the Usk catchment. Designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a local nature reserve, it is central to conservation efforts and supports various wildlife habitats, particularly important for wintering wildfowl and passage migrants. Welsh Wildlife Trust collaborates with Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water on catchment partnership initiatives here, focusing on nature-based solutions and biodiversity enhancement.

Name: Tame Valley Canal
Description: The Tame Valley Canal is an 8.5-mile green corridor in Birmingham, connecting to the national canal network. It traverses industrial landscapes, offering walking and cycling routes, and is a significant wildlife haven within an urban setting.

Name: Tandle Hill Country Park
Description: Tandle Hill Country Park in Oldham covers 110 acres of woodland and grassland, offering panoramic views across the Manchester Plain and Pennine Hills. The park features a children's play area, cafe, and picnic spots.

Name: Tardebigge Reservoir
Description: Tardebigge Reservoir is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Worcestershire, England. It serves as a feeder reservoir for the Worcester and Birmingham Canal, supporting diverse wetland habitats and birdlife. The area offers opportunities for walking and wildlife observation.

Name: Tarr Steps
Description: Tarr Steps features an ancient clapper bridge crossing the River Barle, set within Exmoor's Tarr Steps Woodland National Nature Reserve. The reserve is owned and managed by the Exmoor National Park Authority, offering diverse wildlife habitats and scenic riverside walks.

Name: Tas Valley Woods
Description: Tas Valley Woods comprises a mosaic of woodlands, meadows, and wetlands situated along the River Tas in Norfolk. It provides habitat for diverse wildlife, including otters, kingfishers, and various bird species, with public walking trails available for visitors.

Name: Tasker’s Meadow
Description: Tasker's Meadow is a traditionally managed meadow adjacent to the River Leam, supporting over 80 species of wildflowers and grasses. It provides a habitat for rare orchids and is maintained through regular grazing.

Name: Tattershall Castle
Description: Tattershall Castle is a significant red-brick castle built for Ralph Cromwell in the 15th century. It stands in Lincolnshire, featuring a tower with multiple floors and grand fireplaces. Visitors can explore its architecture and history, set within grounds near the Fenland.

Name: Teal Lough NNR
Description: Teal Lough NNR is a lowland raised bog in County Londonderry/Tyrone, Northern Ireland, within the Teal Lough Special Area of Conservation (SAC) and Teal Lough and Slaghtfreeden Bogs Area of Special Scientific Interest (ASSI). It is valued for its unique biodiversity and significant peatland features, representing a crucial conservation area for this rare habitat, and is part of the wider Sperrins Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONB).

Name: Tealham & Tadham Moors
Description: Tealham & Tadham Moors is a Somerset Wildlife Trust nature reserve. This large area of lowland wet grassland, ditches and rhynes within the Somerset Levels and Moors supports diverse plant and insect life. The site holds nationally important populations of wetland birds, with traditional grazing maintaining valuable habitats.

Name: Tealham and Tadham Moors
Description: Tealham and Tadham Moors is a Site of Special Scientific Interest within the Avalon Marshes. Adjacent to Honeygar Farm, it forms a crucial peatland buffer zone, supporting diverse wetland habitats and species. The area is part of a significant restoration project by Somerset Wildlife Trust.

Name: Teän
Description: Teän is a low-lying, uninhabited island in the Isles of Scilly, managed by the Isles of Scilly Wildlife Trust. It supports a nationally important breeding colony of Lesser Black-backed Gulls and holds SSSI designation. The island is leased from the Duchy of Cornwall.

Name: Tees-Swale: Naturally Connected
Description: Tees-Swale: Naturally Connected is a landscape initiative in the North Pennines AONB. It focuses on restoring and connecting habitats, including peatlands and river systems across the Tees and Swale catchments, enhancing biodiversity and water quality.

Name: Teifi Marshes
Description: Teifi Marshes Nature Reserve, near Cardigan, is the flagship site of the Wildlife Trust of South and West Wales. It provides access to diverse wetlands, reedbeds, and woodlands along the River Teifi. Visitors explore walking trails and spot otters, kingfishers, and rare butterflies.

Name: Teifi Marshes Nature Reserve (Willow Wheel)
Description: Teifi Marshes Nature Reserve, home to the Welsh Wildlife Centre, is a 264-acre site located near Cilgerran on the Pembrokeshire/Ceredigion border, adjacent to the Pembrokeshire Coast National Park. Managed by The Wildlife Trust of South and West Wales, it enhances biodiversity and public access, acting as a vital buffer zone. The reserve features diverse habitats including wetlands, woodlands, and meadows, with restoration efforts focusing on wildflower meadows and native woodland planting, including a notable living willow maze. Recent expansion includes a 59.1-acre area for temperate rainforest restoration, further buffering existing habitats.

Name: Teigngrace Meadow
Description: Teigngrace Meadow is a wet grassland nature reserve beside the River Teign, near Newton Abbot, Devon. It features fen, rush pasture and swamp, supporting water vole, otter, and various insects. Managed for biodiversity.

Name: Teignmouth & Shaldon Coast
Description: The Teignmouth & Shaldon Coast in South Devon offers coastal walks with views of the Teign Estuary and historic ports. Diverse habitats include saltmarsh and cliffs. Visitors can explore local beaches and learn about the area's natural history.

Name: Temple Balsall
Description: Temple Balsall is a peaceful 3-hectare nature reserve in the West Midlands, managed by Warwickshire Wildlife Trust. This wet woodland is bisected by Cuttle Brook, with marshy ground resulting from a former artificial lake. It is rich in native flowers, offering a fine display of snowdrops and ramsons (wild garlic) in spring, alongside common reed, sedges, butterbur, large bittercress, and opposite-leaved golden-saxifrage. It provides habitat for diverse wildlife.

Name: Temple Grafton Limestone Grassland
Description: Grove Hill, near Temple Grafton and Alcester in Warwickshire, is a significant semi-natural limestone grassland reserve managed by Warwickshire Wildlife Trust. This rural haven features a checkerboard of habitats including grass, scrub, woodland, and ponds. It supports diverse wildflowers such as cowslip, wild strawberry, common gromwell, hairy violet, fairy flax, and longstalked crane's-bill, providing essential habitat for butterflies and grasshoppers. The site lies on a steep scarp slope with heavy calcareous Jurassic and Triassic clays.

Name: Ten Acre Wood and Meadows
Description: Ten Acre Wood and Meadows is an urban nature reserve in Hillingdon, West London, managed by the London Wildlife Trust. It features a century-old oak plantation over hazel coppice, wildflower meadows, marshland, and hedgerows, supporting diverse birds and invertebrates. Yeading Brook runs along its western side. This vital green space is part of the wider Yeading Brook Meadows Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation and offers habitats for local wildlife and serves the community.

Name: Tentsmuir Point NNR
Description: Tentsmuir Point NNR, on the North East Fife coast, features sand dunes, woodlands, and intertidal habitats. This dynamic landscape is home to seals, migratory birds, and diverse plant life. Visitors can enjoy walks and observe wildlife.

Name: Terrace Meadows SNCI
Description: Terrace Meadows SNCI, a traditional hay meadow in Sherborne, is managed to protect and enhance its rich biodiversity. This Site of Nature Conservation Interest provides important habitat for wildflowers, grasses, and invertebrates. It offers public open space for local residents.

Name: Testwood Lakes
Description: Testwood Lakes is a nature reserve near Totton, Hampshire, created from former gravel pits. It features diverse habitats including lakes, woodlands, and grasslands, supporting a variety of bird species and invertebrates.

Name: Tetney Blow Wells
Description: Tetney Blow Wells is a unique geological site near Grimsby, Lincolnshire, known for its freshwater springs. These springs emerge through chalk, creating distinctive ponds and reedbeds. The reserve supports a variety of aquatic invertebrates and plant species. It forms part of the Humber Estuary SSSI and Ramsar site, crucial for its ecological value.

Name: Teversal Pastures
Description: Teversal Pastures is a species-rich grassland site in Nottinghamshire, featuring diverse meadows, scrub, and woodland. It supports a variety of wildflowers, grasses, insects, and birds. The site is managed for conservation and public enjoyment.

Name: Teversal Trail & Pleasley Viaduct
Description: Pleasley Pit Country Park, encompassing parts of the Teversal Trail and Pleasley Viaduct, is a 50-hectare wildlife haven. This green corridor connects Nottinghamshire and Derbyshire green spaces, forming part of a 100-mile network of trails on a disused railway line. It is popular with walkers, cyclists, and horse riders.

Name: Tewin Orchard and Hopkyns Wood
Description: Tewin Orchard is an ancient Hertfordshire orchard, established around 1880, featuring over 100 fruit trees, including rare varieties. Adjacent Hopkyns Wood supports diverse flora and fauna. This site is a valuable habitat for dormice and various bird species.

Name: Tewinbury
Description: Tewinbury Nature Reserve, managed by Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust, is a diverse site nestled in the Mimram Valley. It features a variety of habitats including tall fen, swamp, alder carr, willow scrub, and ancient woodland. The reserve supports a range of wildlife such as water voles, otters, badgers, muntjac deer, and numerous bird species including Cetti's Warblers. Visitors can explore walking trails and observe wildlife from a two-storey hide.

Name: Thames Barrier Park
Description: Thames Barrier Park in East London offers landscaped gardens, a rose garden, and wildflower areas providing important urban habitats. It features fountains, a children's play area, and views of the iconic Thames Barrier.

Name: Thames Chase Community Forest
Description: Thames Chase Community Forest spans east London and south Essex. This community forest features woodlands, parks, and open spaces, offering a range of recreational activities. The forest centre provides information, a shop, and a café.

Name: Thames Road Wetland
Description: Thames Road Wetland is a constructed wetland in Crayford, Bexley, filtering surface water before it enters the River Cray. Managed by Thames21, it improves water quality and provides vital habitat for local wildlife. The site helps mitigate pollution impacts on the river system.

Name: Thameside Nature Discovery Park
Description: Thameside Nature Discovery Park, a former landfill site in Thurrock, is a wildlife haven offering a 3-mile sea wall walk with Thames Estuary views. Its diverse habitats support various birds and insects. The park includes a visitor centre and café.

Name: Thatcham Reedbeds
Description: Thatcham Reedbeds is a Berkshire nature reserve featuring extensive reedbeds, fen, wet grassland, and open water. It hosts diverse bird species, including bitterns, marsh harriers, and Cetti's warblers, plus various invertebrates and plants.

Name: The Argory
Description: The Argory is a neo-classical house and 320-acre wooded riverside estate in County Armagh, Northern Ireland. It features an original gas-lighting system, stable yard, and a scenic garden overlooking the River Blackwater.

Name: The Avenue Country Park
Description: The Avenue Country Park in Wingerworth is a former coking works transformed into a diverse wildlife haven. It features ponds, grasslands, woodlands, and a river corridor, supporting varied species. The park provides walking trails and green space for nature observation and public enjoyment.

Name: The Avenue Washlands
Description: The Avenue Washlands is a new nature reserve near Chesterfield, featuring extensive wetlands and grasslands on a former opencast coal mine. It supports diverse wildlife, including various bird species and amphibians. Part of the Trans Pennine Trail, it provides public access for walks and nature observation.

Name: The Carbon Landscape
Description: Risley Moss Nature Reserve is a significant lowland raised bog and wetland site in Warrington, managed by Warrington Borough Council. It is a Local Nature Reserve, Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), and Special Area of Conservation (SAC), forming a key part of The Carbon Landscape partnership programme. The reserve is vital for biodiversity, carbon capture, and connecting communities with nature in a historically industrial landscape.

Name: The Carrifran Wildwood
Description: The Carrifran Wildwood is a rewilding project in the Southern Uplands of Scotland, managed by Borders Forest Trust. Since 2000, over 600,000 native trees have been planted, restoring woodland and associated habitats. The site focuses on ecological restoration and biodiversity.

Name: The Combe
Description: The Combe is a sloping ancient oak woodland near Whitchurch, North Shropshire, managed by Shropshire Wildlife Trust. It features numerous streams, ponds, and is a significant site for ancient woodland plants, providing an ideal habitat for dormice.

Name: The Compound
Description: Salmon Pastures is an urban nature reserve in Sheffield, managed by Sheffield & Rotherham Wildlife Trust. This transformed industrial riverbank provides a vital biodiverse habitat for wildflowers and birds, and a green space for community engagement and education.

Name: The Crumbles
Description: The Crumbles, near Eastbourne, is a unique shingle beach and vegetated ridge formed by coastal processes. Located in East Sussex, it supports a distinctive range of coastal plants and invertebrates, part of the Eastbourne Coastal Local Nature Reserve.

Name: The Dark Peak
Description: The Dark Peak is a rugged moorland landscape within the Peak District, managed by the National Trust. It features extensive peat bogs and heather, vital for carbon storage and flood management. Conservation efforts focus on restoring these habitats, supporting wildlife like mountain hares.

Name: The Deneway
Description: The Deneway is a nature reserve located in Brighton and Hove, East Sussex. It comprises woodland, chalk grassland, and a pond, supporting diverse local wildlife. Managed by Sussex Wildlife Trust, it offers a tranquil green space.

Name: The Denny
Description: The Denny is a small, uninhabited island in the Severn Estuary, near Chepstow. Composed of Old Red Sandstone, it provides an important roosting site for various bird species, particularly gulls and waders. Designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: The Devil's Spittleful
Description: The Devil's Spittleful is a remnant heathland core near Kidderminster, Worcestershire. It encompasses diverse habitats including dry heath, acid grassland, and woodland edges. This reserve supports reptiles, rare insects, and ground-nesting birds. Public footpaths provide access.

Name: The Doward
Description: The Doward features ancient woodlands, grassland, and limestone rock faces near Symonds Yat in Herefordshire. It is home to diverse wildlife, including horseshoe bats and dormice. The reserve provides crucial habitats for rare plants and insects, alongside panoramic views of the River Wye.

Name: The Farne Islands NNR
Description: The Farne Islands NNR, off the Northumberland coast, hosts tens of thousands of seabirds, including puffins, and a large grey seal colony. Visitors take boat trips to observe wildlife and the historic lighthouse. Managed by the National Trust.

Name: The Fine Foundation Wild Chesil Centre
Description: The Fine Foundation Wild Chesil Centre sits on Chesil Beach causeway, near Portland, Dorset. It offers insights into the Fleet Lagoon and Chesil Beach, a unique 18-mile shingle barrier. The centre provides educational exhibits on local wildlife, geology, and coastal processes.

Name: The Flit
Description: The Flits is a National Nature Reserve in Herefordshire, an area of low-lying grassland, fen, scrub, and woodland on peaty soils within the floodplain of the River Wye. It is notable for its diverse invertebrate community, including many rare flies, spiders, and beetles, as well as numerous butterfly and moth species. While public access is permitted for quiet enjoyment, there are no waymarked trails.

Name: The Garrison, St Mary's
Description: The Garrison on St Mary's, Isles of Scilly, is a 20-hectare site protecting coastal heathland and maritime grassland. It supports rare plants, diverse birds including shags, and historic military defences. Walking trails offer panoramic views.

Name: The Great Canal Orchard
Description: The Great Canal Orchard in Wolverhampton is a community green space managed by the Canal & River Trust. It features various fruit trees, providing fresh produce for local communities and hosting events. The site is situated along the canal network.

Name: The Great Fen
Description: The Great Fen is a vast landscape-scale conservation project in Cambridgeshire, connecting Woodwalton and Holme Fens. It aims to restore 3,700 hectares of wetland habitat, enhancing biodiversity and creating new spaces for wildlife. The site offers trails and hides for visitors.

Name: The Great North Bog
Description: The Great North Bog protects 92% of England's upland peat, spanning 7000 sq km across Northern England. This initiative restores degraded peatlands, vital for carbon storage, biodiversity, and water quality.

Name: The Green Park
Description: The Green Park covers 40 acres of mature grassland and trees in central London. Located between Buckingham Palace and Piccadilly, it provides a tranquil, open space popular for relaxation. Part of the Royal Parks, it is a significant green lung for the city.

Name: The Growing Space
Description: The Growing Space is a community garden in Wincanton, Somerset, offering a welcoming environment for local people. It provides opportunities to learn gardening skills, connect with nature, and improve wellbeing. Produce is utilised by the Balsam Centre cafe and distributed within the local community.

Name: The Gwent Levels
Description: Magor Marsh, a key Gwent Wildlife Trust reserve within the internationally important Gwent Levels wetland in Wales, is a focus for restoring ponds and re-connecting vital habitats, enhancing biodiversity and increasing climate change resilience.

Name: The Hollies
Description: The Hollies is a small, semi-natural woodland reserve near Pulverbatch, Shropshire, dominated by ancient holly trees, some over 200 years old. It features oak, birch, and rowan, alongside diverse ground flora, managed for biodiversity.

Name: The Hook
Description: The Hook Local Nature Reserve, in Lady Bay, West Bridgford, Nottinghamshire, is a strip of land between the Grantham Canal and River Trent. It features grassland, scrub, and mature trees, supporting diverse wildlife and offering accessible paths.

Name: The Hudnalls
Description: The Hudnalls is an ancient woodland reserve within the Wye Valley Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, Gloucestershire, representing a vital fragment of the Atlantic rainforest. It is globally significant for its rich lichen, moss, and fern communities, supporting diverse woodland birds and wildlife. The site's varied terrain slopes towards the River Wye.

Name: The Knapp & Papermill
Description: A beautiful and varied reserve in the Leigh Valley with abundant wildlife. Ancient woodland, traditional orchards, unimproved meadows, the Leigh Brook, and diverse habitats. Woodland birds, otters, kingfishers, and a rich invertebrate fauna thrive here.

Name: The Lines Way
Description: The Lines Way is an urban greenway in West Yorkshire, following a disused railway line between Garforth, Allerton Bywater, and Fairburn Ings. Managed by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust, it provides a vital wildlife corridor with diverse habitats.

Name: The Lizard Wildlife Watchpoint
Description: The Lizard Wildlife Watchpoint offers panoramic views of the coast and sea from mainland Britain's southernmost tip. It is a prime location for observing marine life and diverse bird species.

Name: The Lofts
Description: Lofts, managed by Essex Wildlife Trust, is a nature reserve in Essex. It features ancient woodland, unimproved grassland, and a pond, supporting diverse wildlife including dormice, great crested newts, and various woodland birds.

Name: The Loons and Loch of Banks
Description: The Loons and Loch of Banks is a significant wetland on the Orkney mainland. It features wet grassland, reedbeds, and open water, providing habitat for breeding waders and wintering ducks and geese. It is the largest remaining wetland of its type in Orkney.

Name: The Mens
Description: The Mens is an ancient woodland nature reserve in West Sussex. It features historic beech trees, clearings and ancient wood banks. Managed by Sussex Wildlife Trust, it is a site of scientific interest, providing habitat for diverse wildlife.

Name: The Mere, Ellesmere
Description: The Mere at Ellesmere is a glacial lake in Shropshire, forming part of the Shropshire Meres and Mosses Ramsar site. It comprises open water, reedbeds, and woodland habitats, supporting diverse wildlife. The site is popular for walks and wildlife observation.

Name: The Mill Pond
Description: The Mill Pond is a small wetland reserve located near the River Avon, south of Warwick. It features sedge, rush, and reed communities within a wet grassland setting. The site provides a habitat for breeding birds, including little ringed plover and gadwall, and is home to various dragonflies and damselflies.

Name: The Naze
Description: The Naze, a coastal Essex site, is a Site of Special Scientific Interest due to its geology, revealing London Clay and Crag formations where fossils are found. It is important for migrating birds and features varied habitats including scrub and beach.

Name: The Parks
Description: The Parks encompasses two fields alongside the Dulas Brook. The site is managed for diverse habitats, including wildflower meadows, wet grassland, and scrub, supporting various wildlife species. Public access is available for visitors to enjoy.

Name: The Pennings
Description: The Pennings is a wet grassland site bordering the River Dove in Suffolk. Historically managed as hay meadow, it features reedbed, fen, and wet woodland. The site supports rich plant and invertebrate life.

Name: The Pools
Description: The Pools is a wetland nature reserve in Norfolk, transformed from a former sand and gravel quarry. This site features shallow pools, extensive reedbeds, and areas of willow scrub, supporting diverse bird species, invertebrates, and native flora. Boardwalks and hides are present.

Name: The Regent's Park Wildlife Garden & West Pond
Description: Regent's Park hosts a dedicated Wildlife Garden, fostering diverse flora and fauna within London. The park also features the West Pond, an important habitat for aquatic life and birds, contributing to urban biodiversity. It serves as a green sanctuary.

Name: The Riddy
Description: The Riddy nature reserve in Bedfordshire protects a section of the River Ivel floodplain. It features wet grassland, reedbed, and wet woodland habitats, supporting diverse wildlife including otters, water voles, and various bird species. Public access is available.

Name: The Rifle Range
Description: The Rifle Range, a nature reserve in Worcestershire, buffers Hartlebury Common SSSI. Once a military site, it now hosts heathland and acid grassland, supporting common lizards, green tiger beetles, and heathland plants. Management includes grazing and scrub removal.

Name: The Roaches
Description: The Roaches is a prominent gritstone ridge in the Peak District, featuring expansive blanket bog. Staffordshire Wildlife Trust actively restores degraded peatland here, enhancing biodiversity and improving carbon storage. It provides vital habitats for upland birds and plants.

Name: The Roman Road & Fleam Dyke
Description: The Roman Road and Fleam Dyke are two Scheduled Monuments in Cambridgeshire, spanning over 20km. These sites represent significant chalk grassland habitats. The Friends of the Roman Road and Fleam Dyke conserve, protect, and enhance their character, beauty, and scientific interest.

Name: The Rough
Description: The Rough is a nature reserve in Devon, situated on the lower flanks of Dumpdon Hill within the Blackdown Hills AONB. It features damp unimproved grassland with a small area of woodland, supporting a diverse flora including various grasses, sedges, and 17 recorded species of butterfly. Bird species such as buzzard, sparrowhawk, green and greater spotted woodpecker are regularly seen. The reserve is open to visitors.

Name: The Seek
Description: The Seek is a 2.5-hectare nature reserve located on the Lincolnshire/Leicestershire border, acquired by LRWT in 1999. It comprises mature woodland with oak, ash, and hazel, and a hay meadow. The site supports diverse flora including green-winged orchids, and wildlife such as buzzards and badgers.

Name: The Sill: National Landscape Discovery Centre
Description: The Sill is an award-winning visitor centre and youth hostel, providing a gateway to Northumberland National Park and Hadrian's Wall. It offers exhibitions, learning spaces, and a cafe, promoting understanding and enjoyment of the landscape.

Name: The Stepping Stones Project
Description: The Stepping Stones Project works to restore habitats and reintroduce species like water voles in Carding Mill Valley, Shropshire. It is a National Trust collaboration with Shropshire Wildlife Trust and the AONB Partnership, focusing on river health and creating connected wildlife sites.

Name: The Vyne Estate
Description: The Vyne Estate, a former Tudor powerhouse in Hampshire, features a historic chapel, extensive gardens, and a tranquil lake. Its wider estate includes wetlands and woodlands, supporting diverse wildlife. Seasonal events and family activities are regularly hosted.

Name: The Warren
Description: The Warren is a nature reserve in south east London, managed by London Wildlife Trust. It protects ancient semi-natural woodland, home to mature oak and hazel, with diverse ground flora including bluebells and wood anemones.

Name: The Wash National Nature Reserve
Description: The Wash National Nature Reserve is England's largest, covering intertidal sand, mudflats, and saltmarsh. It is a vital feeding ground for hundreds of thousands of birds, supporting important populations and England's largest seal haul-out.

Name: The White Cliffs of Dover
Description: Iconic landmark in Kent offering dramatic views across the English Channel. The site features rare wildflowers and butterflies, with walking trails along the cliff tops. It is managed for conservation and public access.

Name: The White Rocks
Description: White Rocks is a species-rich woodland and grassland nature reserve near Woolhope, Herefordshire. The lime-rich soils support diverse flora, including orchids and wildflowers. Mature trees and open glades provide habitats for various insects and birds.

Name: The Wilderness
Description: The Wilderness is a nature reserve near Ellesmere in north Shropshire, featuring wetland and alder woodland. A small stream flows through the site. It supports diverse wildlife, including willow tit and kingfisher, and various plants. Shropshire Wildlife Trust manages the reserve for conservation.

Name: The Wilderness
Description: The Wilderness is a small urban nature reserve within Milford Haven, Pembrokeshire, Wales. It features woodland, grassland, and wetland habitats, supporting diverse wildlife, including otters and kingfishers. Visitors can explore a network of paths.

Name: The Wood
Description: The Wood is a small, ancient woodland covering 2.4 hectares near Presteigne. It features a diverse tree population, including sessile oak, ash, wych elm, and field maple. The reserve supports a rich ground flora, with bluebells, wood anemones, and early purple orchids. The site is part of the Radnorshire Wildlife Trust’s network of nature reserves.

Name: The Workhouse, Southwell
