Description: The Workhouse, Southwell, is a preserved Victorian workhouse built in 1824. It offers insight into 19th-century poverty and social welfare history through original architecture. A heritage orchard and meadow showcase traditional local flora and fruit varieties.

Name: The Wou
Description: The Wou, a 70-hectare degraded peatland in Northumberland's Border Mires SSSI, undergoes restoration by Northumberland Wildlife Trust. They block drains and rewet peat, promoting moss recovery. This enhances carbon storage and wildlife habitat.

Name: The Wou
Description: The Wou, a 20-hectare peatland restoration site located at Moss Peteral near Thirlwall within Northumberland National Park. This site is part of a wider partnership project led by the Northumberland National Park Authority, working with the Border Uplands Peat Partnership to restore vital peatlands in the Border Uplands.

Name: The Wrekin & The Ercall
Description: The Ercall is an ancient woodland forming part of the Wrekin Forest, known for its significant geological features dating back 550 million years. The site supports diverse wildlife, including various bird species within its coppiced oak, birch, and hazel habitats.

Name: Thelnetham Fen
Description: Thelnetham Fen is a Suffolk Wildlife Trust nature reserve featuring fenland, wet grassland, scrub, and woodland habitats. It supports rare plants, invertebrates, and birds like snipe and lapwing, contributing to local biodiversity.

Name: Thetford Warren
Description: Thetford Warren is a Site of Special Scientific Interest in Breckland, Norfolk. It features typical Breckland grassland on sandy soils, supporting rare plants and invertebrates. The reserve also contains the ruins of a medieval warren lodge, a Scheduled Monument built in the early 15th century.

Name: Thirlmere
Description: Thirlmere is an active working forest in the Lake District National Park. It serves as a vital catchment for United Utilities, providing water and hydro-electric power. The area offers various footpaths and cycle trails for recreation while focusing on conservation and wildlife.

Name: Thompson Common
Description: Thompson Common, managed by Norfolk Wildlife Trust, is a unique wetland site in Norfolk famous for its 'pingo' ponds, formed during the last Ice Age. In 2021, the Trust acquired adjacent land and successfully reintroduced the northern pool frog, the UK's rarest amphibian, while also reinstating lost pingo ponds. The reserve features wet and dry grassland, heathland, and scattered pools, supporting diverse wildlife including dragonflies, damselflies, and various bird species.

Name: Thompson Common
Description: Thompson Common is a 154-hectare Norfolk Wildlife Trust reserve in Breckland, featuring internationally important pingo ponds, a unique ice-age landscape. It supports diverse flora and fauna, including rare aquatic invertebrates and Great Crested Newts.

Name: Thorley Wash
Description: Thorley Wash is a diverse wetland site next to the River Stort in East Hertfordshire. It features wet grassland, reedbed and supports water vole, otter, and various birds. Rare-breed cattle maintain valuable habitats.

Name: Thornbury Park
Description: Thornbury Park in Isleworth, West London, hosts a TCV Green Gym every Wednesday morning. Volunteers participate in practical conservation tasks, improving the local environment. It offers opportunities to learn new skills and meet people.

Name: Thorndon
Description: Thorndon encompasses ancient woodland, open parkland, and extensive conifer plantations in Essex. It supports diverse wildlife, including deer and various bird species. Visitors can explore a network of trails and engage with nature.

Name: Thorney Island
Description: Thorney Island, a Site of Special Scientific Interest in Chichester Harbour, features extensive mudflats, saltmarshes, and shingle beaches. These support migratory birds and marine life. Public access is limited to a coastal path. The site is managed to conserve its unique ecosystems.

Name: Thornham Marshes
Description: Thornham Marshes, part of Holme Dunes National Nature Reserve, lies near Holme-next-the-Sea in Norfolk. This coastal area features extensive saltmarsh, intertidal mudflats, and freshwater pools, providing a crucial habitat for various bird species, especially during migration.

Name: Thornton Glen
Description: Thornton Glen is a small woodland reserve in East Lothian, east of Innerwick. Owned by the Scottish Wildlife Trust, it features a tributary of the Thornton Burn with a small waterfall. Diverse plant life, including ferns, mosses, and ancient woodland indicators, thrives.

Name: Thornton Wood
Description: Thornton Wood is a 6.24-hectare ancient woodland in Thornton Hough, managed by Wirral Wildlife. It is part of the Dibbinsdale Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). The site features diverse ground flora, including Ramsons, Bluebells, Wood Anemone, and Wood Sorrel, and supports a range of woodland birds and mammals like badgers. The reserve is generally not accessible to the public, but visits can be arranged by participating in organised work parties or specific events.

Name: Thorpe Wood
Description: Thorpe Wood is a maturing woodland in the Tees Valley, planted in 1999 on former arable land. It features over 15 native tree species, a wetland area, and a wildflower meadow. The reserve provides valuable habitats, supporting diverse wildlife including dragonflies, damselflies, and bird species.

Name: Thorpe Wood
Description: Thorpe Wood is a small area of ancient semi-natural woodland to the west of Peterborough, characterised by mature oak, ash, and field maple. The reserve supports a variety of woodland birds and insects. It is managed by Wildlife BCN.

Name: Thorswood
Description: Thorswood, part of the Weaver Hills, is a limestone grassland reserve in Staffordshire. It features rich flora including orchids and rare plants like rigid brome. The site is managed by Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Threave Garden & Nature Reserve
Description: Threave Estate, near Castle Douglas, focuses on nature recovery across diverse habitats. The site supports significant populations of bats, otters, and ospreys. Conservation efforts involve wetland restoration and native woodland expansion.

Name: Three Groves Wood
Description: Three Groves Wood is an ancient semi-natural woodland in Gloucestershire's Golden Valley. It features mature oak and ash, with wild garlic and bluebells in spring. The reserve supports local wildlife and offers peaceful walks. Management focuses on conserving its biodiversity.

Name: Threecorner Grove
Description: Threecorner Grove is a magical stand of ancient chalk woodland nature reserve in New Addington, Croydon, managed by the London Wildlife Trust. It features a tall canopy of oak, ash, and wild cherry, with field maple, small-leafed lime, and whitebeam trees. The site is a valuable habitat for woodland birds and invertebrates, and is part of a larger complex of reserves including Hutchinson's Bank and Chapel Bank.

Name: Thrunton Wood
Description: Thrunton Wood offers walking and mountain biking trails amidst coniferous forest in Northumberland. Visitors can find challenging routes and enjoy views of the Cheviot Hills and the Northumberland coastline.

Name: Thundry Meadows
Description: Thundry Meadows is a traditional wet grassland, bordered by woodland and the River Wey. It supports a diverse range of plant and animal species, including wading birds and various invertebrates. The site is a valuable habitat for biodiversity conservation in Surrey.

Name: Thurlby Fen Slipe
Description: Thurlby Fen Slipe is a wetland corridor in Lincolnshire, managed by the Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust. It comprises wet grassland, ditches, and reedbeds, forming a crucial link for wildlife between larger fenland areas. The site supports diverse invertebrates, wetland birds, and rare plants.

Name: Thurrock Thameside Nature Park
Description: Thurrock Thameside Nature Park is a 120-acre former landfill site, set to expand to 845 acres, transformed into a thriving wildlife haven. It features habitats including grassland, woodland, and a large lake, offering extensive views of the Thames Estuary. The park provides walking and cycling trails and includes a visitor centre.

Name: Tiddesley Wood
Description: Tiddesley Wood is an ancient woodland in Worcestershire, managed by Worcestershire Wildlife Trust. It features diverse habitats including oak and hazel coppice, glades, and a pond. It is known for its spring bluebells and wildflowers, supporting various bird species and invertebrates.

Name: Tile Wood
Description: Tile Wood is an ancient woodland, once part of the Great Forest of Essex, featuring mature oak, hornbeam, and hazel. It provides habitat for woodpeckers and dormice and connects with other woodlands, forming the Daws Heath Corridor, vital for local wildlife.

Name: Tilton Cutting
Description: Tilton Cutting, a Geological SSSI in Leicestershire, exposes Jurassic rocks including the Marlstone Rock and Tilton Formations. Key for understanding East Midlands geology, it is rich in fossils such as ammonites and belemnites. The site also supports significant calcareous grassland flora and various butterflies.

Name: Tilton Railway Cutting
Description: Tilton Railway Cutting is a disused railway line now a nature reserve in Leicestershire. It is a Geological Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) known for its Jurassic period fossils and exposed rock layers. The site features species-rich grassland, woodland, and scrub habitats, supporting diverse flora, including wildflowers and ferns, and numerous insect types, particularly butterflies. It was also featured in David Attenborough's documentary 'A Life on Our Planet'.

Name: Tintagel Coast & Barras Nose
Description: Tintagel Coast and Barras Nose feature a rugged coastline surrounding Tintagel Castle in North Cornwall. This exposed headland supports various seabirds and coastal flora. The South West Coast Path traverses the area, offering expansive Atlantic views amidst a landscape rich in Arthurian legend.

Name: Tiptree Heath
Description: Tiptree Heath is a living relic, the last fragment of a once extensive heathland. Dominated by heather and gorse, it provides habitat for uncommon wildlife. Nationally important for its invertebrates, including rare bees, wasps, and spiders.

Name: Titchmarsh
Description: Titchmarsh Nature Reserve is a complex of former gravel pits and grasslands in Northamptonshire. It is an important inland wetland site, known for breeding and wintering wildfowl and waders. Notable species include Gadwall, Shoveler, and Bitterns. Diverse invertebrate and plant life are supported.

Name: Titchmarsh Nature Reserve
Description: Titchmarsh Nature Reserve offers diverse wetland habitats within the Nene Valley, bordering the River Nene. The site includes lakes, reedbeds, meadows, and scrub, supporting many bird species, otters, and invertebrates. Public access is available via trails and bird hides.

Name: Titchwell Marsh
Description: Holme Dunes National Nature Reserve, on Norfolk's north-west coast, features diverse habitats including dunes, saltmarsh, and freshwater pools. It supports many bird species, including migrants, and various insects. This reserve is a key site for coastal conservation.

Name: Titford Pools
Description: Titford Pools are large reservoirs in the Black Country, serving the Titford Canal and wider Birmingham New Main Line Canal network. A wildlife haven, the pools offer popular activities like walking, fishing, and boating, providing a vital green space for the local community.

Name: Titley Pool
Description: Titley Pool is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and one of Herefordshire's largest natural open areas of water. It is an important wetland for wintering bird populations, including teal, tufted duck, pochard, and goosander. The pool is surrounded by ancient woodlands and meadows, and its outflow ultimately feeds into the River Arrow.

Name: Tocil Wood
Description: Tocil Wood is an ancient woodland with a carpet of bluebells in spring. This Warwickshire Wildlife Trust nature reserve provides a habitat for various bird species, including buzzards and tawny owls, and supports diverse flora.

Name: Tollesbury Wick
Description: Tollesbury Wick is a coastal nature reserve in Essex. It encompasses saltmarsh, mudflats, and grazing marsh, supporting diverse bird species and marine life. The reserve is actively managed by Essex Wildlife Trust for biodiversity conservation and coastal defence.

Name: Tollymore Forest Park
Description: Tollymore Forest Park, near Newcastle, County Down, is Northern Ireland's first state forest park. Established in 1955, it covers 630 hectares at the Mourne Mountains' base. The Shimna River flows through it, known for its arboretum and historic follies.

Name: Tonford Wood
Description: Tonford Wood is a Kent Wildlife Trust reserve north of Ashford, Kent. This deciduous woodland features oak, ash, and hazel trees, with hornbeam coppice. Diverse ground flora includes dog's mercury and wood anemone. The Great Stour river forms its western boundary.

Name: Tophill Low NNR
Description: Tophill Low NNR, managed by Yorkshire Water near Watton, East Yorkshire, is a Site of Special Scientific Interest. It features diverse wetlands, woodlands, and two reservoirs. This popular reserve offers excellent birdwatching opportunities.

Name: Tortoiseshell Wood and Porter's Lodge Meadows
Description: Tortoiseshell Wood is a fine example of Kesteven boulder clay primary woodland, featuring mature oak, ash, hazel, and field maple trees. Its calcareous clay gives rise to a rich and varied ground flora, including carpets of bluebell, dog's mercury, primrose, wood anemone, and yellow archangel. Porter's Lodge Meadows, adjacent to the wood, are traditionally managed calcareous clay meadows with a diverse flora including bird's-foot-trefoil, cowslip, oxeye daisy, and common knapweed. The reserve supports various fungi species and birds like green and great spotted woodpeckers, nightingale, and nuthatch. Fallow deer are frequently seen.

Name: Totteridge Fields
Description: Totteridge Fields is a tranquil mosaic of traditionally managed wildflower meadows, hedgerows, and mature trees in north London. The site provides a vital habitat for various species, including bats, stag beetles, and migrating birds. Footpaths allow public access.

Name: Totternhoe
Description: Totternhoe nature reserve in Bedfordshire, managed by the Wildlife Trust for Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Northamptonshire, features impressive flower-rich chalk grasslands on spoil heaps from former quarries for Totternhoe stone. It supports diverse wildlife including rare butterflies like the Duke of Burgundy and small blue, and various orchids. The site offers walking trails with panoramic views and includes parts of Totternhoe Knolls, which features the earthworks of a Norman motte-and-bailey castle.

Name: Totternhoe Nature Reserve
Description: Totternhoe Nature Reserve, managed by the Wildlife Trust for Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire & Northamptonshire, is located in Bedfordshire. It features a rich mosaic of habitats including flower-rich chalk grassland, woodland, and historic medieval quarries. The site is renowned for its diverse wildflowers, including various orchid species, and supports a significant population of butterflies, notably the scarce Duke of Burgundy and small blue butterflies. The area's unique geology includes Totternhoe stone, a durable chalk used historically in buildings like Westminster Abbey. It encompasses parts of several Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs), including Totternhoe Knolls and Totternhoe Chalk Quarry, and is often managed in partnership with the National Trust and Central Bedfordshire Council for certain sections.

Name: Town Kelloe Bank
Description: Town Kelloe Bank is a nature reserve in County Durham, managed by Durham Wildlife Trust. It features a unique landscape shaped by the last ice age, with steep-sided magnesian limestone grassland, scrub, and trees. The reserve is known for its diverse flora, including fragrant orchids, wild thyme, and autumn gentian, and supports butterflies like the northern brown argus. It forms part of a wildlife corridor, with Raisby Hill Grassland being a nearby reserve. Part of the reserve follows the route of the former Coxhoe railway line.

Name: Townclose Hills
Description: Townclose Hills, also known as Billy Goat Hill, is a limestone grassland reserve in the Lower Magnesian Limestone belt. It features woodland, scrub, and grassland habitats. Nationally rare rigid brome grass and moonwort thrive here. Green woodpeckers, buzzards, and various butterflies inhabit the site. Footpaths offer views across the landscape.

Name: Townend
Description: Townend is a preserved 17th-century farmhouse in the Lake District, once home to the Browne family. Visitors explore its historical rooms, extensive library, and traditional Lakeland garden. The site includes a small heritage orchard and an historic barn, showcasing four centuries of rural life.

Name: Townhead Wood
Description: Townhead Wood is a mixed woodland and grassland reserve on the western shore of Loch Leven. Acquired in 2021, it connects existing protected areas. The site supports red squirrels, great spotted woodpeckers, and various woodland birds, enhancing local biodiversity.

Name: Townsend
Description: Townsend Reserve, near Swanage, encompasses maritime grassland and a former limestone quarry. It supports rare plants, including Early Spider Orchid, and nationally important lichen communities. Migratory birds use the site for rest and foraging.

Name: Toys Hill
Description: Toys Hill is a high wooded ridge in Kent, part of the Wealden Greensand Ridge. It offers panoramic views across the Weald. The site features ancient woodlands and is rich in wildlife, with public footpaths for exploration.

Name: Trasna Island
Description: Trasna Island, within the Lower Lough Erne Islands SPA, focuses on habitat restoration for breeding waders. LELP volunteers manage the site, which recently celebrated the successful fledging of three Curlew chicks. Work aims to support endangered bird populations.

Name: Tredegar House Parkland
Description: Tredegar House in Newport, Wales, features significant parkland biodiversity. The National Trust works to restore diverse habitats including ponds, wetlands, and species-rich meadows, supporting local wildlife.

Name: Tregonetha Downs
Description: Tregonetha Downs is a nature reserve in Cornwall, featuring species-rich grassland habitats. The site supports a diverse range of wildflowers and insects, notably the marsh fritillary butterfly. Active management, including grazing, maintains its biodiversity.

Name: Trelissick Maritime Woods
Description: Trelissick Maritime Woods offers tranquil garden and wooded parkland walks with panoramic views of the Fal estuary. Visitors can explore a variety of trails, from gentle strolls among trees and shrubs to longer hikes along the estuary. The site is located seven miles south of Truro.

Name: Trellwyn Fach
Description: Trellwyn Fach is a new 146-acre (59-hectare) reserve in Pembrokeshire, situated in the Gwaun Valley near Llanychaer and Fishguard. It is owned and managed by the Wildlife Trust of South and West Wales. Funded in part by The Wildlife Trusts' Atlantic rainforest recovery programme (supported by Aviva) and partners like Lost Rainforests of Britain and Size of Wales, the project aims to restore temperate rainforest by expanding woodland and connecting ancient woods.

Name: Trench Wood
Description: Trench Wood is an ancient woodland and SSSI in Worcestershire, managed by Worcestershire Wildlife Trust. Noted for spring bluebells and diverse fungi, the site supports rare butterflies like the pearl-bordered fritillary through ongoing woodland management practices.

Name: Tresco: Abbey Pool & Great Pool
Description: Great Pool is a significant freshwater lake on Tresco, Isles of Scilly. It supports a diverse range of bird species, particularly migrating waterfowl. Nearby Abbey Pool also forms part of this important wetland system, contributing to the island's rich biodiversity.

Name: Treswell Wood
Description: Treswell Wood is an ancient woodland in Nottinghamshire, featuring oak standards and hazel coppice. It supports a rich ground flora, including bluebells, and a diverse range of breeding birds. The reserve is one of the county's oldest woodlands.

Name: Trevone Bay
Description: Trevone Bay is situated on the North Cornwall coast near Padstow, featuring dramatic cliffs, sandy beaches, and numerous coves. Part of the South West Coast Path runs along Trevose Head, offering coastal views of the Atlantic and opportunities to spot seabirds.

Name: Trevose Head
Description: Trevose Head is a prominent headland near Padstow, Cornwall, designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). It features coastal grassland, dramatic cliffs, and important seabird breeding sites. Visitors enjoy scenic walks and observe diverse wildlife.

Name: Trillis Banks
Description: Trillis Banks is a nature reserve located in the Golden Valley, managed by Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust. It features a hidden grassland valley with sloping banks, fields, a babbling brook, and links to the canal and ancient woodlands. The reserve supports species-rich calcareous and neutral grassland habitats, providing a home for diverse flora and fauna, including Southern marsh-orchids.

Name: Trimdon Grange Quarry
Description: Trimdon Grange Quarry is a former limestone quarry now a Durham Wildlife Trust nature reserve near Trimdon. Its varied habitats include grassland, scrub, and woodland, supporting a diversity of plant and animal life. The site features calcicolous grassland and wetland areas, attracting rare invertebrates and birds.

Name: Trimley Marshes
Description: Trimley Marshes is a Suffolk Wildlife Trust nature reserve located on the Orwell Estuary. It features freshwater lagoons, reedbeds, and grazing marsh, providing crucial habitats for a diverse range of bird species. The reserve supports overwintering and breeding waterfowl and waders, including avocets and marsh harriers.

Name: Tring Reservoirs
Description: Tring Reservoirs, comprising Startops End, Marsworth, Tringford, and Wilstone, is a significant site for overwintering wildfowl and migrating waders. Located at the head of the Grand Union Canal, the reserve's diverse habitats support water voles and dragonflies. Footpaths offer access for nature observation.

Name: Tring Reservoirs National Nature Reserve
Description: Tring Reservoirs, a National Nature Reserve and SSSI in Hertfordshire, supports diverse birdlife. The four reservoirs provide crucial habitats for wintering waterfowl and breeding birds. Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust manages the site, focusing on conservation and habitat preservation.

Name: Trinity Broads
Description: Trinity Broads is a complex of five freshwater bodies located in Norfolk, managed by Norfolk Wildlife Trust. The site is a haven for waterbirds and is surrounded by reedbeds and fen, supporting diverse plant life.

Name: Trosley Country Park
Description: Trosley Country Park is a 170-acre site near Meopham on the North Downs. It offers expansive views and significant chalk grassland slopes. Kent County Council manages the park, while Kent Wildlife Trust maintains a vital chalk grassland area within it.

Name: Troublefield
Description: Troublefield is a 13-hectare wetland reserve south of Uddens in East Dorset, within the Stour Valley catchment. It features reedbed, fen, and wet woodland habitats. The reserve is known for dragonflies, damselflies, and diverse bird species. Access is limited.

Name: Troup Head
Description: Troup Head is Scotland's largest mainland gannet colony, home to over 30,000 gannets during the breeding season. This cliff-top reserve also supports kittiwakes, fulmars, and guillemots. Seals are often visible below the cliffs.

Name: Trowell Marsh Nature Reserve
Description: Trowell Marsh Nature Reserve is a small but important wetland site nestled in the Erewash Valley, Nottinghamshire. It features a mosaic of habitats including reedbed, marshland, scrub, and open water, supporting diverse birdlife, amphibians, and insects. The site is managed for conservation, providing a tranquil natural space for wildlife observation.

Name: Trumland
Description: Trumland is an RSPB nature reserve on Rousay, Orkney. It features heathland, wetlands, and moorland habitats. The reserve is home to diverse bird species including hen harriers, red-throated divers, and arctic skuas. Visitors can explore walking trails.

Name: Trumpington Meadows
Description: Trumpington Meadows is a 58-hectare country park and nature reserve south of Cambridge. It features wildflower meadows, woodlands, and riverside habitats along the River Cam. Created as part of a housing development, it provides diverse environments.

Name: Tuckmill Meadows
Description: Tuckmill Meadows is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) nestled between Shrivenham and Watchfield villages in southwest Oxfordshire. This 15-acre reserve combines floodplain meadows, reedbeds, woodlands, and a stream (Pennyhooks Brook, a tributary of the River Cole). It is home to over 300 plant species, rare insects, otters, and various birds. The site is managed by Earth Trust, in partnership with Vale of White Horse District Council and Friends of Tuckmill volunteers, for biodiversity and public access.

Name: Tuckmill Meadows
Description: Tuckmill Meadows is a valuable wildflower meadow, fen, and wet woodland reserve near Shrivenham and Watchfield in south-west Oxfordshire. It is fed by Pennyhooks Brook, a tributary of the River Cole, supporting diverse plant and insect life, including water voles, rare spiders, and various butterfly species. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) for its fen habitat and species-rich grasslands.

Name: Tudhoe Mill Wood
Description: Tudhoe Mill Wood is a small, ancient woodland on the steep banks of the River Wear near Spennymoor. It features oak, ash, and elm trees with diverse ground flora including wild garlic and bluebells, supporting various bird species and mammals.

Name: Tummel Shingle Islands
Description: The reserve is an important site for breeding wading birds, especially common sandpipers, oystercatchers and ringed plovers. Its shingle islands are formed by the meandering River Tummel, creating dynamic habitats for diverse wildlife.

Name: Tunman Wood
Description: Tunman Wood is an ancient woodland nature reserve in Lincolnshire, managed by the Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust. It features oak, ash, and hazel trees, with a rich ground flora including dog's mercury and bluebells. It provides a habitat for various wildlife.

Name: Tunstall Forest
Description: Tunstall Forest is a mixed woodland in Suffolk, East of England, offering walking, cycling, and horse riding trails. Part of the Suffolk Coasts and Heaths Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, it consists of coniferous plantations, broadleaved belts, and heathland areas. It is part of the Sandlings Forest Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a Special Protection Area (SPA), providing diverse habitats for wildlife, including ground-nesting birds like the Nightjar and Woodlark. It is managed sustainably for timber and recreation.

Name: Turf Hide
Description: Turf Hide is an accessible wildlife viewing facility overlooking the tidal River Crouch. It offers views of saltmarsh, mudflats, and the river, hosting diverse bird species, including wintering waders and wildfowl. It is a key birdwatching spot within the River Crouch marshes.

Name: Turner's Wood
Description: Turner's Wood is a small nature reserve in Pelsall, Walsall, comprising ancient woodland with mature oak and birch trees. It supports diverse flora and fauna, including bluebells and various bird species. A vital green space, it offers peaceful walks.

Name: Turners Puddle Heath
Description: Turners Puddle Heath is a nature reserve protecting lowland heath, mire, and bog. It supports scarce wildlife including nightjars, Dartford warblers, sand lizards, and smooth snakes, crucial for biodiversity in Dorset.

Name: Turnford and Cheshunt Pits
Description: Turnford and Cheshunt Pits, a nature reserve in the Lee Valley, features flooded gravel pits. It is an SSSI and SPA, supporting diverse birdlife including overwintering wildfowl and breeding birds. Birdwatching hides and walking paths are available.

Name: Twickenham Rough
Description: Twickenham Rough is a nature reserve in Twickenham, owned by Richmond Council. TCV volunteers undertake coppicing, scrub clearance, and path maintenance to manage the site's biodiversity.

Name: Two Mile Bottom
Description: Two Mile Bottom is a Forestry England site within Thetford Forest, Norfolk. It offers walking, cycling, and horse riding trails amidst woodlands near the Little Ouse River. It serves as a gateway to the wider forest experience.

Name: Two Tree Island
Description: Two Tree Island is a 259-hectare nature reserve managed by Essex Wildlife Trust on the Thames Estuary, near Leigh-on-Sea. This reclaimed island features extensive saltmarsh, mudflats, lagoons, grazing marsh, mixed scrub, rough grassland, and reedbed. It is a vital site for wintering wildfowl and waders, including avocets, lapwings, curlew, and brent geese, as well as rare insects, butterflies, and reptiles. The reserve is designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest, Special Protection Area, and National Nature Reserve, offering public footpaths and bird hides.

Name: Tyland Barn
Description: Tyland Barn is a Kent Wildlife Trust nature reserve and visitor centre near Maidstone. It features wildlife gardens, a learning centre, and accessible trails. Facilities include a shop, seasonal cafe, and picnic areas. Events and educational programs are offered on site.

Name: Tywardreath Marsh
Description: Tywardreath Marsh is a rare freshwater marsh behind Par Beach in Cornwall, featuring two ponds, grazed pasture, and reed-fringed ditches. It supports nationally rare fen orchids, snipe, water rail, and kingfishers. Cornwall Wildlife Trust manages the site to maintain its diverse wetland habitats.

Name: Ubley Warren
Description: Ubley Warren is a former lead mine in the Mendip Hills. It features a unique calcicolous grassland habitat, supporting a diverse range of plant and insect species. The reserve is known for its rare wildflowers and mining spoil heaps.

Name: Uffmoor Wood
Description: Uffmoor Wood is an ancient woodland near Hagley, managed by the Woodland Trust for conservation and public access. It features diverse habitats, including broadleaf trees, conifers, and open glades. Visitors can explore a network of walking trails and observe various wildlife, including numerous bird species.

Name: Ufton Fields
Description: Ufton Fields Nature Reserve, a former quarry and railway cutting, is a diverse wildlife haven. It features wildflower-rich grasslands, ancient woodland, scrub, and ponds. The reserve supports over 20 butterfly species and 200 flowering plant species.

Name: Ughill Farm
Description: Ughill Farm is a working farm on the western edge of Sheffield, within the Peak District National Park, spanning approximately 132 hectares. It is an important site for nationally threatened wading birds like curlews and golden plovers. The site prioritises wildlife-friendly farming practices, creating a mosaic of habitats including woodlands, wildflower meadows, and wetlands, and includes a small area of the internationally important Eastern Moors Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Ullswater Catchment Restoration
Description: The National Trust manages the Ullswater catchment area, undertaking conservation work and restoring habitats. Efforts include tree planting and rewilding valleys to mitigate flood risk and enhance the natural landscape.

Name: Ulverscroft
Description: Ulverscroft is a secluded ancient woodland in Leicestershire, featuring a diverse array of birds, plants, and butterflies. The reserve is managed for wildlife, creating a mosaic of habitats including ancient woodland, wildflower meadows, and serene ponds.

Name: Umbra
Description: Umbra Nature Reserve is a significant dune system at Magilligan, County Londonderry. It hosts a unique flora, including rare orchids, and important fauna like natterjack toads and diverse bird species. The site holds Ramsar, SAC, and ASSI designations.

Name: Underhill Wood
Description: Underhill Wood is a small ancient woodland near Habberley, Shropshire. It features mixed broadleaf trees, including oak and hazel, supporting diverse wildlife. The reserve provides a habitat for various bird species and wildflowers.

Name: Upcott Cross
Description: Upcott Cross is a small wet woodland nature reserve in Herefordshire. The site features ancient woodland species like sessile oak, birch, and rowan. A stream runs through the reserve, supporting a diverse range of amphibians and invertebrates. This reserve is managed for biodiversity conservation.

Name: Uphill Hill
Description: Uphill Hill is a coastal limestone grassland near Weston-super-Mare with views of the Bristol Channel. It features ancient monuments, diverse flora including orchids, and supports various bird species. The site offers walking trails.

Name: Uppacott Wood
Description: Uppacott Wood is an ancient oak woodland situated on a steep valley side above the River Taw. This nature reserve supports diverse woodland birds and invertebrates. A public footpath crosses the site, offering access through its typical sessile oak habitat.

Name: Upper Conwy Catchment - Afon Eidda Project
Description: The Upper Conwy Catchment is a landscape of ancient woodland, farmland, and blanket bog in the Afon Conwy valley. It supports diverse wildlife, including red squirrels and otters. The Afon Eidda Project focuses on restoring nature and improving water quality within the sub-catchment area.

Name: Upper Derwent Catchment
Description: Located within the Peak District National Park, the Upper Derwent Catchment is a vital upland area of peatlands and reservoirs. Moors for the Future Partnership undertakes extensive restoration, re-wetting degraded blanket bog habitats to enhance biodiversity and capture carbon effectively.

Name: Upper Derwent Valley
Description: The National Trust cares for the Upper Derwent Valley, an area of picturesque woodlands and extensive peat moorlands. It encompasses the iconic Derwent, Howden, and Ladybower reservoirs, offering walking, cycling, and diverse wildlife discovery.

Name: Upper Dunsforth Carr
Description: Upper Dunsforth Carr Nature Reserve is a wetland site on the River Ure in North Yorkshire. It features wet woodland, fen, and reedbed, supporting diverse birds, dragonflies, and butterflies. The reserve is managed to enhance its rich biodiversity.

Name: Upper Minety Meadows
Description: Upper Minety Meadows, an expansion of the existing Emmett Hill nature reserve and part of the wider Braydon Forest Project, integrates wildflower-rich grassland, woodland, and wetland habitats. Managed by Wiltshire Wildlife Trust, the reserve is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) known for supporting diverse wildlife, particularly the threatened marsh fritillary butterfly, and features abundant devil's-bit scabious, betony, saw-wort, sneezewort, and heath spotted orchids.

Name: Upper Nethan Gorge
Description: Upper Nethan Gorge is a semi-ancient woodland site located in South Lanarkshire, near Blackwood and Lesmahagow. Carved by the River Nethan, this peaceful gorge features steep, wooded slopes, riverine habitats, and ancient trees. It is part of the Clyde Valley Woodlands National Nature Reserve and a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). The reserve supports diverse wildlife, including great spotted woodpeckers, buzzards, and badgers, as well as locally uncommon plants such as broadleaved helleborine, wood melick, and meadow saxifrage. Public access is available via marked trails.

Name: Upper Park Wood
Description: Upper Park Wood is an ancient woodland in West Yorkshire, managed by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust. It hosts diverse tree species like sessile oak, birch, and rowan, with a rich ground flora of bluebells and wood sorrel. The reserve supports a variety of bird life and woodland invertebrates.

Name: Upper Ray Meadows
Description: Upper Ray Meadows, on the Oxfordshire/Buckinghamshire border near Marsh Gibbon, is a complex of species-rich meadows, pastures, hedgerows, and ditches. It supports wildlife like otters, curlew, and many scarce plants.

Name: Upper Ray Meadows
Description: Upper Ray Meadows is a series of traditional floodplain meadows and wetlands in Buckinghamshire. Managed for biodiversity, it supports diverse wildlife, including breeding waders and wildflowers, and aids natural flood management.

Name: Upper Titchfield Haven
Description: Upper Titchfield Haven is a Hampshire nature reserve in the Meon Valley. It protects fen, reedbed, and wet grassland habitats. The site supports diverse birdlife, dragonflies, and water voles. Accessible trails allow visitors to explore the area.

Name: Upper Welson Marsh
Description: Upper Welson Marsh is a valuable site for wildflowers and insects, nestled beside the River Wye near Hay-on-Wye. The reserve features wet grassland habitats supporting diverse plant species and a rich invertebrate community. It is managed to conserve its unique biodiversity.

Name: Upper Wharfedale
Description: Upper Wharfedale is a glacial valley in the Yorkshire Dales. The National Trust manages 7,000 acres of upland, featuring hay meadows, limestone pavements, and ancient woodlands. It supports rare plants and wildlife like red squirrels. Conservation work maintains diverse habitats.

Name: Upton Broad and Marshes
Description: Upton Broad and Marshes is a tranquil Norfolk Wildlife Trust nature reserve near Acle, featuring a diverse mix of habitats including fen, grazing marsh, reedbeds, and wet alder carr woodland. It is home to rare wildlife such as iconic swallowtail butterflies, Norfolk hawker dragonflies, otters, water voles, and nationally rare plants like the fen orchid. Boardwalks and paths provide access for visitors to explore this wetland haven, which is managed for biodiversity conservation.

Name: Upton Broad and Marshes
Description: Upton Broad and Marshes is a significant wetland nature reserve within the Norfolk Broads. It features a large shallow broad, extensive reedbeds, and fens, supporting rare invertebrates and marshland birds. Management focuses on maintaining diverse habitats.

Name: Upton Meadow
Description: Upton Meadow is a 0.8-hectare nature reserve near St Just-in-Roseland, Cornwall, featuring grassland, scrub, and wet woodland alongside the River Fal. Managed by Cornwall Wildlife Trust, it supports otters, dormice, and diverse wildflowers. A circular path allows visitor access.

Name: Upwood Meadows
Description: Upwood Meadows is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and National Nature Reserve near Ramsey, Cambridgeshire, managed by the Wildlife Trust for Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Northamptonshire. These traditionally managed fenland meadows feature a rich diversity of wildflowers and grasses, supporting numerous insect species, including butterflies and bees. The site is open to the public for quiet enjoyment.

Name: Upwood Meadows
Description: Upwood Meadows SSSI is an unimproved neutral grassland in Cambridgeshire. Managed by Wildlife BCN, its two species-rich meadows, The Lings and Old Chapel Field, feature green-winged orchid, adder's-tongue fern, oxeye daisy, and yellow rattle.

Name: Uswayford Forest
Description: Uswayford Forest, located within the Cheviot Hills, is a designated Red Squirrel Reserve within Northumberland National Park. Managed by Forestry England, it forms part of the Cheviots Forest Plan, aiming to enhance woodland connectivity and support crucial biodiversity, contributing to regional ecological resilience.

Name: Uxbridge Alderglade
Description: Uxbridge Alderglade is a nature reserve near Harefield, west London. Managed by Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust, it protects ancient woodland and wet alder woodland. The River Colne flows through, creating diverse habitats.

Name: Uxbridge Alderglade
Description: A small wet woodland and marshland nature reserve in Uxbridge, located along a former railway embankment between the Frays River and the Shire Ditch. It features mature crack willow and alder trees, with areas of marsh. Notable ground flora includes birds-foot trefoil and small toadflax. The reserve provides important habitat for various wildlife, including mammals such as stoats, weasels, moles, foxes, and the rare Brandt's bat.

Name: Vane Farm
Description: Vane Farm sits on the southern shore of Loch Leven, a large freshwater lake in Scotland. It offers panoramic views and diverse habitats including woodlands and reedbeds. The reserve provides accessible trails, hides, and a visitor centre, supporting numerous bird species.

Name: Vann Lake
Description: Vann Lake & Candy's Copse is a Surrey Wildlife Trust reserve and a 57.8-hectare (143-acre) biological Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Surrey, England. It features an eight-acre (approx. 3.2-hectare) man-made lake surrounded by ancient woodland, grassland, mire, and heathland. The reserve is known for its diverse wildlife, including over 900 species of fungi, numerous invertebrates, and over 100 bird species such as kingfishers.

Name: Vealand Farm
Description: Vealand Farm, near Holsworthy in West Devon, is a nature reserve lying on the Culm measures. It encompasses a variety of semi-natural and manmade habitats including grassland, scrub, and open water, providing diverse habitats for wildlife such as marsh fritillary butterflies, dragonflies, and damselflies. Grazing helps maintain the grasslands.

Name: Veilstone Moor
Description: Veilstone Moor is a Devon Wildlife Trust nature reserve near Chulmleigh, featuring culm grassland, valley mire, and woodland. It hosts wildflowers such as meadow thistle and marsh violet, and birds including willow warbler and cuckoo. The site is managed for conservation.

Name: Vell Mill Daffodil Meadow
Description: Vell Mill Daffodil Meadow is a nature reserve near Newent, Gloucestershire. It showcases ancient woodlands and a notable display of wild daffodils each spring. The site is managed by Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust to protect its diverse flora and habitats.

Name: Velvet Bottom
Description: Velvet Bottom, in the Mendip Hills SSSI, is a tranquil valley with ancient woodland and grasslands. It supports diverse wildlife, including dormice and horseshoe bats. Visible spoil heaps reveal its lead mining history.

Name: Venn Ottery
Description: Venn Ottery Nature Reserve, managed by Devon Wildlife Trust, is a significant part of the East Devon Pebblebed Heaths. It features a diverse landscape of wet and dry lowland heath, ancient woodland, unimproved grassland, and a spring-fed raised bog. The reserve is home to a rich array of wildlife, including 40 species of breeding birds, four of the UK's six native reptiles (adders, grass snakes, common lizards, and slow worms), and rare plants such as pale butterwort and sundew. Dormice and badgers are also present. Public footpaths offer access, though some areas can be very wet and challenging to traverse.

Name: Ventnor Downs (St Martin's Down)
Description: Ventnor Downs, including St Martin's Down, on the Isle of Wight, is a significant area of chalk grassland and heathland with dramatic sea cliffs. This diverse habitat supports a variety of wildlife, including butterflies, soaring birds, and rare plants.

Name: Verne Common
Description: Verne Common is a calcareous grassland nature reserve on the Isle of Portland. It supports diverse wildflowers, insects, and birds, including horseshoe vetch and the small blue butterfly. Grazing maintains the habitat, which offers views over Portland Harbour and Weymouth Bay.

Name: Vicar Water Country Park
Description: Vicar Water Country Park, north of Clipstone Village, is a former colliery site transformed into a Green Flag park. It now features woodlands, open heathland, and a large lake, offering diverse wildlife habitats and well-maintained paths for walkers and cyclists.

Name: Vinters Valley Nature Reserve
Description: Vinters Valley Nature Reserve is a peaceful haven of woodland, grassland, and wetland in Maidstone, Kent. The River Len flows through the valley, supporting diverse wildlife including birds, mammals, and invertebrates.

Name: Vinters Valley Nature Reserve
Description: Vinters Valley Nature Reserve is an ancient woodland nature reserve managed by Kent Wildlife Trust, located in Maidstone. It features coppiced sweet chestnut and oak, supporting diverse fungi, mosses, and lichens. The site provides a habitat for various bird species and invertebrates, with seasonal wildflowers.

Name: Waen Fraith
Description: Waen Fraith is a peatland restoration site within Eryri National Park, Wales. The National Trust, in partnership with Admiral, is restoring 100 hectares to capture carbon and mitigate flood risk. This three-year project blocks ditches to re-wet the peat and remove invasive species.

Name: Waitby Greenriggs
Description: Waitby Greenriggs is a nature reserve in Cumbria, a disused section of the former Stainmore railway line. It features limestone grassland habitats, rich in wildflowers and diverse invertebrates, supporting rare plant species.

Name: Walborough
Description: Walborough is a limestone grassland and saltmarsh in North Somerset, bordering the Severn Estuary near Uphill. The reserve supports a diverse array of wildlife, including rare plants, butterflies, and wading and migratory birds. It is managed by Avon Wildlife Trust.

Name: Waldridge Fell SSSI
Description: Waldridge Fell SSSI is a lowland heath in County Durham, providing a vital habitat for various rare plants and insects. Designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest, it represents one of the last remaining areas of this unique ecosystem.

Name: Walkeringham Nature Reserve
Description: Walkeringham Nature Reserve was originally a claypit and later a landfill site, which was capped with river sand and seeded. It features wetland, grassland, scrub, and plantations of Corsican pine and broadleaved trees, providing valuable habitats for a variety of birds, insects, and plant species. The site is managed for wildlife conservation by Nottinghamshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Wallasea Island
Description: Wallasea Island, Essex, is a significant conservation and engineering project, forming Europe's largest man-made nature reserve. Created from Crossrail tunnel spoil, it features extensive mudflats, saltmarshes, and lagoons, providing vital habitats for diverse migratory and breeding bird species.

Name: Wallington River Wansbeck Restoration
Description: Wallington, a National Trust property in Northumberland, features a historic house, gardens, and expansive estate. It is currently undertaking a pioneering River Wansbeck restoration project, improving water quality, increasing flood storage, and creating wetland habitats.

Name: Wallis Wood
Description: Wallis Wood is an ancient woodland reserve featuring coppiced sweet chestnut and oak standards on sandy clay soil. The site includes diverse ground flora with bluebells and wood anemones. A small stream and wet woodland areas are present, supporting various bird species.

Name: Walltown Crags
Description: Walltown Crags, a connectivity node in Northumberland National Park, is part of the Hadrian's Wall Wetlands Project. It restores wetlands, peatlands, and grasslands, enhancing biodiversity and wildlife corridors.

Name: Walsall Canal Wildlife Haven
Description: The Walsall Canal runs through a mix of urban and green spaces in the West Midlands. It provides a habitat for various wildlife species, including waterbirds and insects. The canal supports local ecosystems and offers a linear green corridor.

Name: Waltham Brooks
Description: Waltham Brooks is a 42-hectare grazing marsh and a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) within the Arun Valley floodplain, managed by Sussex Wildlife Trust. It features a mosaic of damp grassland, ditches, ponds, and wet woodland. The reserve is important for a rich variety of aquatic flora, including Southern Marsh-orchids, and supports diverse wildlife such as dragonflies (including Scarce Chaser), bats, and numerous bird species. It is particularly significant for wintering wildfowl like Teal, Shoveler, Wigeon, and Pintail, and breeding waders such as Lapwing and Redshank. Conservation grazing helps maintain its valuable wetland habitats.

Name: Walthamstow Marshes
Description: Walthamstow Marshes is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in East London. It features a diverse mix of marshland, rivers, and ditches, supporting unique flora and fauna. Historically, it hosted Britain's first powered flight in 1909 and the nation's first aircraft factory.

Name: Walthamstow Wetlands
Description: Walthamstow Wetlands is a 211-hectare urban wetland nature reserve in North East London. Owned by Thames Water, it comprises 10 reservoirs supplying drinking water to the capital and is managed for conservation and public access by the London Wildlife Trust. Thames21 is a partner involved in broader river health and wetland creation projects in the Lea Valley.

Name: Walthamstow Wetlands
Description: Walthamstow Wetlands is a 211-hectare nature reserve in London, comprising ten operational reservoirs that supply water to the city. It is a significant site for wildlife, particularly birds, and offers opportunities for birdwatching, walking, and fishing.

Name: Wandlebury Country Park
Description: Wandlebury Country Park is a historic parkland on the Gog Magog Hills near Cambridge, featuring Iron Age hillfort remains. It offers walking routes, nature trails, and views over the city, managed for wildlife and public enjoyment.

Name: Wangford Warren
Description: Wangford Warren, a Suffolk Wildlife Trust reserve, features rare open inland sand dunes, a habitat typically coastal. It supports specialised flora and fauna adapted to sandy, nutrient-poor conditions. Active management maintains its unique character.

Name: Wanlip Meadows
Description: Wanlip Meadows is a wet grassland reserve beside the River Soar, managed by Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust. It hosts breeding waders, wintering wildfowl, and diverse grassland habitats, ditches, and ponds. The site provides a rich environment for numerous bird species.

Name: Wanstead Park
Description: Wanstead Park hosts floating reedbeds launched by Thames21 in 2025. These reedbeds improve water quality and create habitats for wildlife, supported by volunteers and the City of London Corporation.

Name: Wappenbury Wood
Description: Wappenbury Wood is an ancient woodland, home to diverse wildlife and flora. Visitors can explore various habitats, including ancient oak and hazel coppice, and a small pond. It is managed for conservation, supporting species like dormice and woodcocks.

Name: Warburg Nature Reserve
Description: Warburg Nature Reserve is a wildlife refuge in a deep, sheltered valley within the Chilterns. It features juniper glades, chalk grassland, and varied woodlands, supporting diverse wildflowers and local wildlife.

Name: Warburton's Wood
Description: Warburton's Wood is an ancient semi-natural clough woodland in Cheshire, featuring a steep-sided gorge with a tributary of the River Weaver. It supports mature trees like oak, ash, and hazel, alongside uncommon species such as small-leaved lime and wild service-tree. The ground flora is rich with over 50 species including bluebell, wood anemone, and primrose. The reserve is home to a variety of woodland birds, and kingfishers can be spotted along the stream.

Name: Waresley & Gransden Woods
Description: Waresley & Gransden Woods is an ancient woodland in Cambridgeshire, managed by Wildlife BCN. It is noted for its spring displays of bluebells and wood anemones, mature trees, and diverse wildlife. Waymarked trails are available for visitors.

Name: Waresley and Gransden Woods
Description: Waresley and Gransden Woods is an ancient woodland site in Cambridgeshire, comprising diverse broadleaf woodland, rides, and glades. It supports woodland birds, mammals, and invertebrates, managed for wildlife conservation and public access.

Name: Wark Forest
Description: Wark Forest is a large working forest located within Kielder Forest Park in Northumberland. Managed by Forestry England, it is known for its diverse wildlife, including red squirrels and ospreys. The area offers various outdoor activities.

Name: Warleigh Point
Description: Warleigh Point is a peninsula in Devon where the Rivers Tavy and Tamar converge, offering expansive views across the estuaries. This nature reserve encompasses ancient woodland, historic parkland, and vital saltmarsh habitats. It supports diverse wildlife, including various bird species and native flora.

Name: Warley Place
Description: Warley Place is a nature reserve in Essex, located on the former grounds of a stately home. It features historic garden remains, ancient trees, ponds, and diverse wildlife including birds and insects. It is known for its spring flowers.

Name: Warnborough Greens
Description: North Warnborough Greens Nature Reserve comprises picturesque, species-rich wet meadows adjacent to the River Whitewater, and ancient woodland in North East Hampshire. Designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), it supports a variety of wildlife, including plants like ragged-robin, marsh-marigold, and various orchids, and birds such as tawny owl. The site is managed by the Hampshire & Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust for conservation, with accessible paths.

Name: Warrens Wood
Description: Warren Wood is a former ancient woodland plantation near Maidstone, Kent. Dominated by mature oak, hornbeam, and hazel coppice, with some sycamore and ash. It features footpaths and an adjacent public bridleway, with part of it a Local Wildlife Site.

Name: Wart Barrow
Description: Wart Barrow is a Cumbria Wildlife Trust reserve, featuring steep limestone grassland and woodland. It provides habitat for diverse wildflowers, butterflies, and insects. Mature ash and hazel woodlands are present, and the site overlooks the Kent Estuary, offering views.

Name: Warton Crag
Description: Warton Crag is a prominent limestone hill and nature reserve in Lancashire, designated as a SSSI. Managed by Lancashire Wildlife Trust, it features diverse habitats including woodland, grassland, and limestone pavement. The site supports rare butterflies and offers panoramic views of Morecambe Bay.

Name: Wasdale & Eskdale
Description: Wasdale, in the Lake District, encompasses England's highest mountain, Scafell Pike, and deepest lake, Wastwater. The National Trust manages this valley, undertaking vital conservation work, including high fell path repairs and visitor access.

Name: Washburn Valley
Description: Yorkshire Water, through its Washburn Valley Biodiversity Enhancement Project, improves 200 hectares for wildlife. Efforts include restoring peatland, creating new woodlands, and improving river habitats within the scenic Washburn Valley area.

Name: Washland
Description: Upton Broad and Marshes is a freshwater grazing marsh and broad, forming part of the Trinity Broads system near Great Yarmouth. Managed by Norfolk Wildlife Trust, this reserve provides important habitat for diverse wading birds, dragonflies, and butterflies, including the nationally rare Norfolk hawker. The site floods seasonally, supporting a wide range of aquatic and grassland species.

Name: Waterford Heath
Description: Waterford Heath is a former sand and gravel quarry in Hertfordshire, now a varied nature reserve. It features acid grassland, wetland, heathland, woodland, and wildflower meadows. The site supports skylarks, green woodpeckers, dragonflies, and various other wildlife species.

Name: Watersmeet
Description: Watersmeet is a deep gorge woodland in Exmoor National Park, Devon, where the East Lyn River and Hoar Oak Water meet. Owned by the National Trust, it features scenic walking trails and a historic tea-garden, popular for its natural beauty and diverse wildlife.

Name: WaterWorks Centre Nature Reserve
Description: The WaterWorks Centre Nature Reserve, in East London, features wetland habitats, wildflower meadows, and open water, supporting diverse wildlife. Located adjacent to the Lee Navigation, the site offers walking routes and bird hides for visitors to observe nature, particularly a range of bird species.

Name: Watford Lodge
Description: Watford Lodge, near New Mills, is a crucial nature reserve for great crested newts. The site features a mix of broadleaf woodland, grassland, and ponds, providing diverse habitats. It also supports various birds, invertebrates, and wildflowers throughout the year.

Name: Watlington Hill
Description: Watlington Hill offers panoramic views across the Oxfordshire plain, situated high above Watlington. This site features a mosaic of chalk grassland and ancient woodland, supporting a variety of rare plants and insects, including the red kite.

Name: Watts Wood
Description: Watts Wood, managed by Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust, was planted between 1991 and 2000, transforming a former cereal field into a woodland with 3,200 trees. It features diverse species, wildflowers, a pond, and hedges, attracting various wildlife.

Name: Wayland Wood
Description: Wayland Wood is an ancient woodland, approximately 31.7 hectares, near Watton, Norfolk. It is a biological Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and supports diverse flora like bluebells, wood anemones, and the rare yellow star-of-Bethlehem, as well as many bird species. The site offers trails for walking and nature observation.

Name: Weald Country Park
Description: Weald Country Park is a large, historic country park in Brentwood, Essex, managed by Essex County Council. Spanning over 500 acres, it features extensive woodlands, lakes, and open grasslands. The park is home to diverse wildlife, including fallow deer and various bird species, and offers visitors a network of paths to explore, alongside popular attractions like the Stick Man sculpture trail.

Name: Weavers Down Bog
Description: Weavers Down Bog, East Hampshire, is a two-hectare wet heath and mire, part of Woolmer Forest, surrounded by pine and birch woodland. It is notable for supporting rare plants such as the water-loving cranberry, a scarce species in southern England, and birds like the Dartford warbler. This site protects important biodiversity.

Name: Weeleyhall Wood
Description: Weeleyhall Wood is an ancient woodland in north-east Essex, managed for conservation. It features diverse tree species, a seasonal pond, and a rich understory of wildflowers. The site supports various bird species and invertebrates, offering a quiet habitat for wildlife.

Name: Weeleyhall Wood
Description: Weeleyhall Wood is an ancient woodland nature reserve in Essex, managed by Essex Wildlife Trust. It features broadleaf trees like oak, hornbeam, and sweet chestnut, supporting diverse bird species. The understorey displays a spectacular bluebell display in spring. It is open for public walks.

Name: Weeting Heath
Description: Weeting Heath is a significant Norfolk Wildlife Trust reserve, known for supporting Stone Curlew, nightjars, and woodlarks. Its sandy soils host rare plants such as Moonwort fern and insects like the Dark Green Fritillary. Rabbit grazing helps maintain the open heathland habitats.

Name: Weeting Heath National Nature Reserve
Description: Weeting Heath National Nature Reserve is a vital relic of the Breckland landscape in Norfolk, managed by Norfolk Wildlife Trust. It features diverse habitats including bare sandy soil, scattered heath, grassland, and woodland. The site is nationally important for its population of rare stone curlews and supports many scarce Breckland plants such as fingered speedwell, Spanish catchfly, maiden pink, and rare spring sedge. It is a designated SSSI.

Name: Weetslade Country Park
Description: Weetslade Country Park is a former colliery site near Newcastle. It features grassland, woodland, and ponds, providing habitat for skylarks and roe deer. The park offers walking trails and panoramic views across Northumberland for visitors.

Name: Weir Wood Reservoir
Description: Weir Wood Reservoir is a 153.5-hectare (379-acre) Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in East Sussex, with an 81-acre Local Nature Reserve at its western end. It is managed in partnership by Southern Water, East Sussex County Council, and The Friends of Weir Wood. The site supports diverse bird species, including overwintering wildfowl and migrating waders. Public access is limited, with bird hides available, particularly at the western end.

Name: Welcombe Hills
Description: Welcombe Hills, near Stratford-upon-Avon, features diverse habitats including wildflower-rich grasslands, ancient woodlands, and ponds. The site offers extensive views across the Avon Valley and includes historical landmarks like the Welcombe Lodge.

Name: Wellington Gravel Pits
Description: Wellington Gravel Pits, a former aggregate quarry in Herefordshire, is now a diverse nature reserve. It features a deep central lake, shallow pools, reedbeds, scrub, and grassland, attracting wildfowl, butterflies, dragonflies, and various bird species.

Name: Wells Farm
Description: Wells Farm is a nature reserve in West Oxfordshire, featuring limestone grassland and ancient woodland. It supports a diverse range of wildflowers, butterflies, and bird species. Visitors can explore waymarked trails. The site is managed for conservation.

Name: Wem Moss
Description: Wem Moss is a rare raised bog in north Shropshire, a designated National Nature Reserve. It supports diverse plant life, including sphagnum mosses and carnivorous plants, providing critical habitat for insects, birds, and amphibians.

Name: Wembury Bay
Description: Wembury Bay is a popular Devon coastal site, managed by the National Trust, featuring diverse habitats from sandy beaches to rocky shores. It offers rockpooling, beach walks, and a marine centre focused on education and marine conservation.

Name: Wendover Woods
Description: Wendover Woods is a extensive woodland managed by Forestry England in the Chiltern Hills, Buckinghamshire. It features walking and cycling trails, a café, and a popular treetop adventure course. The site offers diverse habitats and panoramic views across the Aylesbury Vale.

Name: Wenlock Edge
Description: Wenlock Edge is a limestone escarpment stretching for 19 miles in Shropshire. A woodland of ash, lime and hazel covers the ancient coral reef, providing habitat for diverse wildlife. It offers walking trails and is a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest managed by the National Trust.

Name: Wenlock Edge
Description: Wenlock Edge is a 19-mile limestone escarpment in Shropshire, featuring ancient woodlands and grasslands. Designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), it forms part of the Shropshire Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. It supports diverse wildlife and geological features.

Name: Wentworth Castle Gardens
Description: Wentworth Castle Gardens, in South Yorkshire, is a historic landscape with formal gardens, parkland, and architectural follies. Managed by the National Trust in partnership with Barnsley Council, it focuses on conservation and public access to heritage.

Name: Wern Plemys Nature Reserve
Description: Wern Plemys Nature Reserve, a former coal mine site in the Tawe Valley, now features a mix of woodland, wildflower meadows, and wet areas. The reserve supports diverse wildlife, including otters and various bird species, alongside its industrial heritage.

Name: Werndryd
Description: Werndryd is a wet heath and bog sanctuary in Radnorshire, Wales, managed by Radnorshire Wildlife Trust. It protects diverse dragonflies, damselflies, and unique bog plants. Cattle grazing sustains the habitat. An accessible boardwalk aids visitor exploration.

Name: Wernffrwd Loughor Estuary Saltmarsh
Description: Wernffrwd is a key saltmarsh and scrub habitat on the east bank of the Loughor Estuary. It supports important overwintering wildfowl and wader populations. The site is a Special Area of Conservation and Special Protection Area.

Name: Wessington Pasture
Description: Wessington Pasture is a 1.25-hectare traditionally managed flower-rich SSSI. It hosts green-winged orchid, adder's-tongue fern, yellow rattle, ancient trees, and a ridge and furrow field system. Hay is cut annually, sheep graze in autumn.

Name: West Bexington
Description: West Bexington is a coastal reserve in Dorset, featuring a shingle beach, freshwater marsh, and reedbeds. It supports diverse birdlife, including overwintering and migrating species, alongside various insects and plant communities.

Name: West Blean and Thornden Woods
Description: West Blean and Thornden Woods is a 1,200-hectare ancient semi-natural woodland in Kent. Managed by Kent Wildlife Trust, it is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and home to the Wilder Blean project, introducing European bison and other grazing animals for rewilding.

Name: West Burton Meadow
Description: West Burton Meadow is a traditional hay meadow near Burton Joyce, Nottinghamshire, close to the River Trent. It features diverse flora including great burnet, meadowsweet, ragged robin, and cuckoo flower. This Trent Valley site is an important stopover for migrating birds.

Name: West Burton Reedbed
Description: West Burton Reedbed is a Nottinghamshire Wildlife Trust wetland reserve. It features extensive reedbeds, open water, and wet grassland habitats. The site provides a vital refuge for diverse bird species, including bitterns and marsh harriers, crucial for wetland conservation.

Name: West Coker Fen
Description: West Coker Fen is a wet meadow and wetland area near Yeovil, managed by Somerset Wildlife Trust. It features diverse flora including southern marsh orchids and ragged robin. The site supports various insects, amphibians, and birds, reflecting its rich biodiversity.

Name: West Dean Woods
Description: West Dean Woods, a remnant of ancient woodland in the South Downs National Park near Chichester, features beech, oak, and ash trees with a hazel and hawthorn understorey. The site includes veteran trees, a dew pond, and ancient woodland indicator plants.

Name: West Ham Park
Description: West Ham Park is a historic 31.1-hectare (77-acre) green space in Newham, East London. It features formal gardens, sports facilities, a children's playground, and an arboretum. The park is managed by the City of London Corporation and provides diverse recreational opportunities.

Name: West Haystoun
Description: West Haystoun is an important site for nature in Peeblesshire. Acquired in 2021, this small reserve safeguards ancient semi-natural woodland alongside newly planted areas. The site contributes to a vital woodland corridor and features a mix of broadleaved trees like oak, ash, and birch. It supports diverse wildlife and enhances riparian habitats along the River Tweed, improving biodiversity in the Borders region.

Name: West Muchlarnick
Description: West Muchlarnick is a site in Cornwall, part of the Rainforest Legacy project, where Cornwall Wildlife Trust works to protect and expand temperate rainforest habitats. These unique ecosystems are rare in the UK, found in areas of high rainfall.

Name: West Runton and Beeston Regis Heath
Description: West Runton and Beeston Regis Heath offers panoramic views of the the North Norfolk coast and a diverse landscape of heathland, woodland, and meadows. It is home to various wildlife species, including butterflies, birds, and deer. The site is popular for walking and nature observation.

Name: West Walk - Forest of Bere
Description: West Walk, within the Forest of Bere, is a woodland site in Hampshire. It offers marked walking, cycling, and horse riding trails through ancient woodland and heathland habitats. Managed by Forestry England, it supports biodiversity and provides recreational access.

Name: West Wickham Common
Description: West Wickham Common and Spring Park, managed by the City of London Corporation, offers heathland, woodland, ponds, and open green spaces in South London. This Green Flag awarded site is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, protecting ancient woodland and providing a refuge for wildlife.

Name: West Williamston
Description: West Williamston is a diverse nature reserve in Pembrokeshire, situated on a promontory at the confluence of the Carew and Cresswell rivers. It features tidal creeks, saltmarsh, limestone rock outcrops, and woodland. The reserve supports rich flora, including marsh mallow, and a variety of bird species and butterflies, such as the brown hairstreak. Note that the woodland section is currently closed to the public due to ash dieback.

Name: West Wood
Description: West Wood is a small ancient woodland in Essex, managed by coppicing hornbeam and oak. This practice benefits ground flora like wood anemone and bluebells. The site supports various butterflies, including white admirals, and bird species such as nightingales.

Name: Westhay Moor
Description: Westhay Moor National Nature Reserve, managed by Somerset Wildlife Trust, is an internationally acclaimed site within the Avalon Marshes. Reclaimed from former peat workings, it features extensive reed beds, open water, and the largest surviving fragment of lowland acid mire in the South West. It is a vital habitat for diverse wildlife, including significant bird populations and spectacular starling murmurations in winter, and holds a rich history as part of the ancient peatland landscape.

Name: Westhay Moor NNR
Description: Westhay Moor National Nature Reserve, managed by Somerset Wildlife Trust, is a crucial peatland habitat in the Somerset Levels. It supports rare plants, invertebrates, and important bird populations throughout the year, including wintering wildfowl.

Name: Weston Big Wood
Description: Weston Big Wood is an ancient woodland of about 38 hectares in North Somerset, boasting a rich variety of trees, plants, and wildlife. Managed by Avon Wildlife Trust, it features both ancient and secondary woodland, coppiced areas, and a grassland glade. Rare whitebeam trees grow on limestone cliffs.

Name: Weston Turville Reservoir
Description: Weston Turville Reservoir is a shallow, alkaline waterbody and a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Buckinghamshire. It supports diverse aquatic plants and invertebrates, attracting migratory waterfowl and surrounded by reedbeds and grasslands.

Name: Westwood Manor Estate
Description: Westwood Manor is a medieval house in Wiltshire, featuring a beautiful garden and topiary. The property reveals its changing uses, from a medieval hall to a Georgian clothier's home and a 20th-century family residence, with collections of furniture and musical instruments.

Name: Wetmoor
Description: Wetmoor is a 14.7-hectare nature reserve near Lucton, Herefordshire, featuring traditional orchard, meadow, and ancient woodland. It provides an important habitat for dormice and mistletoe. The site is actively managed to support diverse wildlife populations.

Name: Wharram Quarry
Description: Wharram Quarry is a disused chalk quarry near Wharram-le-Street, managed by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust. The reserve protects chalk grassland, scrub, and woodland habitats, supporting wildflowers, butterflies, and birds for visitors to observe.

Name: Wharram Quarry Nature Reserve
Description: Wharram Quarry Nature Reserve is a species-rich chalk grassland in North Yorkshire, managed by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust. It features unimproved meadows rich in wildflowers and grasses, supporting a variety of insect life, including numerous butterflies. The reserve also provides habitat for ground-nesting birds and is known for its orchids.

Name: Wheldrake Ings
Description: Wheldrake Ings, part of the Lower Derwent Valley NNR, is a vital wetland in Yorkshire, managed by YWT. It supports significant populations of wintering wildfowl and breeding wading birds. Its extensive floodplains offer diverse habitats for plants, invertebrates, and mammals.

Name: Whichford Wood
Description: Whichford Wood is an ancient woodland, a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), located near Whichford, Warwickshire. It is known for its spring bluebells, mature oak and ash trees, and diverse ground flora. The site is managed for conservation, providing habitats for various wildlife.

Name: Whinlatter Forest
Description: Whinlatter Forest, England's only true mountain forest, is nestled high in the Lake District National Park. It provides extensive walking and cycling trails, a Go Ape course, and a visitor centre. The forest is home to ospreys and red squirrels, offering stunning views.

Name: Whinlatter Forest
Description: Whinlatter Forest, near Keswick, offers walking and cycling trails with views of Bassenthwaite Lake and surrounding fells within the Lake District National Park. Managed by Forestry England, it provides routes for various abilities and supports a diverse range of local wildlife.

Name: Whirlow Hall Farm
Description: Whirlow Hall Farm is a working educational farm and charity in Sheffield, bordering the Peak District. Managed by the Whirlow Hall Farm Trust, it provides educational experiences for children and young people, particularly those facing challenges, focusing on farming, food production, and environmental awareness. The site includes various livestock and offers public access to a cafe, shop, and playground.

Name: Whistlestop
Description: The Whistlestop Community Wellbeing Hub, managed by Derbyshire Wildlife Trust, is located at Matlock Bath Railway Station. It serves as an environmental education and community hub, connecting visitors to the diverse natural habitats nearby, including the River Derwent, which supports local wildlife like kingfishers and otters. The site is easily accessible for visitors.

Name: Whitacre Heath
Description: Whitacre Heath is a 46-hectare nature reserve in Warwickshire, bordering Staffordshire at the River Tame. It features diverse habitats including wet woodland, wildflower meadows, marshy grasslands, and reedbeds. The reserve is important for breeding water birds and aquatic wildlife thrives in its pools. It is a good example of vegetation succession from open water through marsh into willow carr and woodland.

Name: Whitbarrow Nature Reserve
Description: Whitbarrow Nature Reserve is a prominent limestone scar rising from the Lyth Valley. Its diverse habitats include limestone pavement, grassland with lime-loving plants such as orchids, and ancient oak and hazel coppice woodland. It is notable for its butterflies, including dingy and grizzled skippers, and is managed for biodiversity by Cumbria Wildlife Trust.

Name: Whitbarrow Scar
Description: Whitbarrow Scar is a designated National Nature Reserve and Special Area of Conservation in Cumbria. This site features impressive limestone pavements, ancient woodlands, and rich grasslands, supporting a diverse array of wildlife including rare butterflies and orchids.

Name: Whitcombe Hill
Description: Whitcombe Hill Nature Reserve in Dorset is a significant chalk grassland site managed by Dorset Wildlife Trust. It supports diverse flora and fauna, including rare butterflies and wildflowers. The reserve offers panoramic views across the Frome Valley, providing a crucial habitat for local wildlife.

Name: White Field
Description: White Field is a small area of species-rich hay meadow in Butleigh, Somerset, managed by Somerset Wildlife Trust. It also features a damp reed fen, a small area of fruit trees, and broadleaf woodland. The reserve supports wildflowers like yellow-rattle, bird's-foot trefoil, meadow buttercup, selfheal, oxeye daisy, and cowslips. Grazing occurs in late summer/autumn after hay cutting.

Name: White Hill
Description: White Hill is a chalk grassland nature reserve located on a steep south-west facing slope of the North Downs in Kent. It is an important habitat supporting a variety of insects, including the Adonis Blue butterfly, and different plant species. The site is part of the Kent Downs Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Name: White Horse Hill
Description: High on a chalk downland ridge in Oxfordshire, the Bronze Age White Horse is carved into the hillside. Iron Age earthworks of Uffington Castle surround the chalk figure, while Dragon Hill and Wayland's Smithy are nearby.

Name: Whitecross Green Wood
Description: Whitecross Green Wood is an ancient woodland, restored from a conifer plantation, rich in butterflies and dragonflies. Varied habitats include wet woodland and wildflower meadows, supporting diverse wildlife. The reserve offers peaceful walks.

Name: Whitecross Green Wood
Description: Whitecross Green Wood is a significant fragment of ancient Bernwood Forest, featuring diverse habitats like semi-natural woodland, meadows, and ponds. It supports a wide array of wildlife, including butterflies, dragonflies, and birds. Visitors can explore well-maintained paths.

Name: Whiteford Burrows
Description: Whiteford Burrows is a coastal reserve on the Gower Peninsula in South Wales. It features an expansive sandy beach, a dune system, saltmarsh, and woodland, supporting diverse wildlife. The area is known for its historic cast-iron lighthouse and provides habitats for many bird species and rare plants.

Name: Whiteford Hill
Description: This National Trust site offers open access to ancient woodland and chalk downland within the South Downs National Park in Hampshire. It provides spectacular views across the landscape, encompassing diverse wildlife habitats and features tranquil walking trails.

Name: Whitehaven Coast
Description: The Whitehaven Coast offers dramatic cliff-top walks and panoramic views across the Irish Sea. This area encompasses important maritime grasslands, providing vital habitats for diverse wildlife and unique coastal flora, accessible via maintained public paths.

Name: Whitehouse Lagoon
Description: Whitehouse Lagoon is an international wetland and vital migratory stopover on Belfast Lough, part of RSPB Belfast's Window on Wildlife. It hosts diverse bird species year-round. Two hides offer observation points for visitors overlooking the lagoon.

Name: Whitehouse Meadow
Description: Whitehouse Meadow Nature Reserve is a small, species-rich grassland located in Fleet, north-east Hampshire, managed by the Hampshire & Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust. Once part of a much larger landscape lost to development, it now provides a vital wildlife oasis and is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). This small woodland and open meadow hosts plants such as lousewort, bedstraw, and tormentil, supporting various insects, including butterflies like the meadow brown. The site is actively managed for conservation.

Name: Whiteleaf Hill
Description: Whiteleaf Hill offers panoramic views across the Chilterns, featuring a prehistoric barrow and the striking Whiteleaf Cross carved into the chalk hillside. The site includes woodlands and open grasslands, supporting diverse wildlife. Popular for walking and wildlife spotting.

Name: Whitelee Moor National Nature Reserve
